body.title: [En-Es] The first pair of mushrooms
body.body:
***Happy Fungi Friday, friends!***

>*Feliz viernes de hongos amigos.*

![20260410_081434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23tbnYFPex7wNosJGPG2HcJttLJ4ZSJADTccJ2sbyJzVmoQBEmSkJh5NAFRBBJB9XLreU.jpg)

***The first pair of mushrooms 🍄 of the season has appeared. At least as far as I know.***

>*Apareció el primer dúo de setas 🍄 de la temporada. Al menos que yo sepa.*

![20260410_081413(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23u5YxFqFWT64SeyWNzHTv23cQV6Sw21AXjHh3MS5TPp5cLXpSjaHLqAHVpZJPmGxXfZR.jpg)

***We are currently experiencing very high temperatures with a severe drought, so it is imperative to water plants daily, especially those in pots.***

>*Actualmente estamos sufriendo temperaturas muy elevadas con una fuerte sequía, por lo que es imperativo regar las plantas a diario, sobre todo las que están en maceta.*

![20260410_082623.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/EoGxQR3guXTqKY62VQzcHMUG39edbMmVfkdAWrvWJo7KYQWbNaqYXV3mvWkx5cxw8Xm.jpg)

***We also have a problem with the accumulation of dry leaves and branches, as the authorities announced that they would fine those who burn them, even if they are on their own property.***

>*Tenemos además un problema con la acumulación de hojas y ramas secas ya que las autoridades anunciaron que iban a poner multas a los que quemen, aunque estén en su propiedad.*

![20260410_082545.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23wWvxK98r8LE7AcqHM1RpFEqVkPg5MFiNwh7HN48mwrLuis7PRMdagFR3hbPhDedLGtq.jpg)

***It was precisely in some leaf litter that I saw a mushroom sticking out almost at nightfall, while I was watering the plants.***

>*Fué precisamente en una hojarasca que vi una seta sobresalir casi al anochecer, mientras regaba las plantas.*

![20260410_082613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/EoeEWTiGNZH8b79o48vS55nDSBoZ9HmfAja5c9LdGofA5XuUqRTDqkAvwQGtC2pAmm5.jpg)

***As it was getting dark, I decided to photograph it the following morning.***

>*Como oscurecía preferí fotofrafiarla a la mañana siguiente.*

![20260410_082655.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23x12ve2FiP5JqqnfRgWRUhFAJL23iaVJidkg3TjSG3VhTQqkwVAQz9qKU6gMnsAkWm2a.jpg)

***To my surprise, there were actually two, one larger than the other.***

>*Para mi sorpresa, eran en realidad dos, una de mayor tamaño que la otra.*

![20260410_081320.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23wC7QQBaY6hkDTHNPn4n6RmN8DFTcVfz959tZJcYtLUg6j8eX2sBYNVviNt9usQj8S5p.jpg)

***One had a diameter of about 4.5 centimeters at the hat, the other 6.
Both were 5 centimeters tall.***

>*Una tenía unos 4,5  centímetros de diámetro en el sombrero, la otra 6.
La altura de ambas era de 5 centímetros.*

![20260410_081338.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/EoGwwDTsVesfGBydmVkSjHkzepV2hazMJacekA9AfcAPsDacPbZYCsTWDCDgVAJuEqv.jpg)

***[Macrolepiota procera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrolepiota_procera) one of the possible identifications for this species. This is a widely distributed agaric fungus that is said to be edible.***

>*[Macrolepiota procera](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrolepiota_procera) es una de las posibles identificaciones que les corresponden. Este es un hongo agárico de amplia distribución que, se dice, es comestible.*

![20260410_082719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23tvaHUpvknaMKpgbFWbUxJrBgq7y9n5rSuUwgpZaiARD127nwixaY5m5rbYVbzHqYdY9.jpg)

***Another one that could be [macrolepiota rhacodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyllum_rhacodes) which has a toxicity that depends on dose, processing and handling.***

>*Otro que podría ser es [macrolepiota rhacodes](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyllum_rhacodes) que tiene una toxicidad que depende de dosis, procesamiento y manipulación.*


![20260410_110304.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23xKxeJGWxmobDVK7VrhdL9hF4Xx9wdTm8GDSACXmv7cwPkFzaXXECjCK8vMp8nSC6mnh.jpg)

![20260410_110251.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/243M54xrGEHtYQ99hLSb17cxEpdeKnVWtqRMEsRWucJa2raL9igQB3sGqrhtDE3QZM5rD.jpg)

***Another possible name is lepiota, which is a genus that is known to be deadly if ingested, especially [Lepiota brunneoincarnata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepiota_brunneoincarnata).***

>*Otro posible nombre es lepiota que es un género que si tiene fama de ser mortal si se ingiere, sobre todo [Lepiota brunneoincarnata](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepiota_brunneoincarnata).*

![20260410_110239.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/243WVff2YzWvUUgBGUbxkc6W2y5FW1twsePWbK6V7qtHsTVnNbKxb7Fek38PtvFvUDhJx.jpg)

![20260410_110313.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23xAVy2PPba2zVgJDpRa9wekrbA1cWyLZENnondY2bYfK5wFGzrzEajVcyMa31qXsduxY.jpg)

***Among the criteria to consider in order to identify it and better understand its degree of toxicity are whether it has a volva or not, whether the veil can be moved without breaking, and its size.***

>*Entre los criterios a tomar en cuenta para identificarla y conocer mejor su grado de toxicidad están si tienen volva o no, si el velo se puede desplazar sin romperse y su tamaño.*

![20260410_110319.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23wgQH8ZYu9Zjz48YVo9d2msvQcRYqicRv9xu2RXhSzpM2PCh7u4XHd8KFMLFXWbUTvS6.jpg)

![20260410_110232.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/243frcATPhVZf3P1rDsdxRWJLSjmttQ9hkKhTuSSKYzdvfysHDcTD2zbBmjmAASFpK3xu.jpg)

***In this case, I didn't see a volva, but the veil did move. Its size makes it more likely to be a Lepiota because its cap measures less than 10 centimeters.***

>*En este caso no vi volva, pero el velo si se desplazba. El tamaño hace que sea más probable que sea trate del género Lepiota porque su sombrero mide menos de 10 centímetros.*

![20260410_110014.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23uR5YtYWv88E5T3SFisFs5svRvqB6U6MrPK6qu14T7hzcP6fif93s8PBSdxHBYZjwJ6G.jpg)

***Given the possibility that they were poisonous, I pulled them up to protect the pets (even though I don't like doing it).***

>*Ante la posibilidad se que fueran venenosas, las arranqué para proteger a las mascotas (aunque no me gusta hacerlo)*

![20260410_110304.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23xKxeJGWxmobDVK7VrhdL9hF4Xx9wdTm8GDSACXmv7cwPkFzaXXECjCK8vMp8nSC6mnh.jpg)

![20260410_081404(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/AK2C4PvhdnHnifkZSywMCPFP1xXTXp8MQUYtDuwQepe1KTzBCbVUbW72PrQdJnV.jpg)

![20260410_082705.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23vsLA4FQ1xUW9CEaZTpWczhb7uPJQq5w6y3EoLP2ReutLPtCVuDcQjaCsw6nvuEzEKZv.jpg)

![20260410_082556.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23vsNB5mrWYyENwYDsTqhB5Ds8SmsXho7YrZ7XKtDePPdpg1x5NretRsPKeR5Csh3WeaC.jpg)

***This is my contribution to the weekly Fungi Friday challenge from @ewkaw.***

>*Esta es mi contribución al reto semanal Fungi friday de @ewkaw.*

![20260410_081330.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23wC7M2oa6AxjbHjDyAmdCJ2hqwhZQ5a2G3MvjGLovedXMsJ5mPpvvxZE6RSuapFQLmxd.jpg)

***All photos were taken with Samsung Galaxy A15 and Xiaomi Redmi9C smart devices.***

>*Todas las fotos fueron tomadas con dispositivos inteligentes Samsung Galaxy A15 y Xiaomi Redmi9C.*

![20260410_081404.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/EoEjDPSthsprtwWcxCNHFRsXQ3JHDU1Wn6ktPSSRuRVD9P7mJyk9UKtU45TVCEsLRNS.jpg)

***Thank you so much for stopping by and reading my post.***

>*Muchas gracias por detenerse y leer mi publicación.*

![Presentación Mi proyecto Final Femenino Delicado Rosa y Nude.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elentogether/23wXQcW8JRJd8imKFZA3Dy18RijyjDHUdiC5TgotdiqGY4T3Qgdfd52nijjcAxkWDLDQx.jpg)

body.body:

Hace un par de días les comenté que vi una escultura de hierro, bueno hecha con resto de hierro. Muy cerca está una empresa que realiza motores de barcos, gandolas, tractores, carros, entre otras maquinarias y piezas de la industria automotor. 

Creo que esa escultura fue realizada por dicha empresa, no estoy seguro, pero se pueden ver restos de componentes que al parecer son piezas. 

Lo prometido es deuda, así que les traigo la foto. No pude tomar una foto mas cercana porque era hora pico y cruzar esa calle tiene su espera, además que el transporte público se maneja con horarios precisos y no quería perder el de la salida más próxima, sino me tocaba esperar un largo rato. 

Espero tengan una linda noche.

body.title: 从OpenClaw到Hermes
body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![lAoGsX373SNQpD3I_bxt5.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/alpha-omega/images/lAoGsX373SNQpD3I_bxt5/lAoGsX373SNQpD3I_bxt5.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

这两天一直在刷X，感觉X上简直每天都不同。从今年年初以来AI圈最后的是OpenClaw这个AI私人助理，我也试着安装了一个，不过装完就再也没用过。昨天X上突然有个类似的AI agent -> Hermes(爱马仕)突然爆火，宣传的特点是相比OpenClaw轻便，配置过程不复杂，用Python编写，有记忆功能可以自动生成Skill文件等等。于是我就跟着教程在电脑上安装了一个，正好前两天我在本地用ollama安装了Google Gemma4B大模型。把大模型配给Hermes，Token钱节省下来了。

安装完成后肯定要使用一下试试效果，正好我下载了一些图片，要从一个文件夹移动到另一个文件夹，然后挨个给这图片重命名。往常我都是手动操作，一张图片一张图片重命名，非常麻烦。我把任务抛给Hermes后就不管了，它自己调用大模型思考然后操作，完成后向我汇报。我打开文件夹看了下，果然完成了。虽然整个过程有几分钟时间，但这段时间我彻底解放了，可以去做其它事情，相当于并行完成任务。

接下来我又让Hermes处理网上下载图片的水印，这次它完成的不理想，要么水印没有完全处理完，要么处理后有严重失真。尝试了几次后我让它停止工作，自己用截图工具把水印去掉。看来Hermes并不能完美完成所有事情，不知道是不是本地大模型的缘故，准备换个大模型再试试。不管怎么说现在电脑上有了一个AI私人助理，可以帮我处理一些简单工作，还是挺香的。

---

For the best experience view this post on [Liketu](https://liketu.com/@alpha-omega/open-claw-hermes)

body.title: 5 Minutes Free Writing - Analyst of What?
body.body:
Good morning all, doing my 5 minutes free writing with prompt - Analyst of What? Hope you enjoy the story.


![images?q=tbn:ANd9GcTjmrFnF7whFah8qdOGjTCPlp693Yld_1KCgb_sC2MnKw&s=10](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcTjmrFnF7whFah8qdOGjTCPlp693Yld_1KCgb_sC2MnKw&s=10)
[Source](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcTjmrFnF7whFah8qdOGjTCPlp693Yld_1KCgb_sC2MnKw&s=10)

Sometimes I wonder if the word \
has been overused in today's job title enhancement in the workforce. Many times, new contacts introduce themselves as an analyst, not to sound impolite by asking \

An analyst like the name suggests is one who collects large amount of raw data, does some pre processing as raw data in it's original form is usually messy, unsorted and even of different data type that cannot be reconcile on its own to another dataset. Thus pre processing is to clean up these data and with that, try to draw a link between different data or certain behavioral relationship between them and to draw a conclusion of certain event, or as what we always like predict the future with what we see from the past.

These processes sound easy in writing, but it requires specific skill set to handle the data like what to collect, where to collect, why do we collect it and how we do it needs knowledge of the domain the analyst is handling. 

Thus, next time when we were introduced to an analyst, let's try to get their domain politely.

body.title: Mi compañera de entrenamiento de hoy.😎🏃🏽‍♀️‍➡️🌞
body.body: > Dia Viernes, hoy tocaba entrenar 8 kilometros a ritmo intermedio, mi esposo ha estado full trabajo y no ha podido entrenar, por lo que hoy cuadre con una amiga para salir a entrenar juntas, asi como una charla de amigas mientras trotamos, asi si que es facil determinar si estamos en zona 2, porque podemos conversar. Como vivimos cerca la pase buscando a las 5:40 am, nos fuimos las dos a un ritmo comodo. Un bello amanecer nos deslumbro hoy, acompañado de una neblina sobre el mar, que cubria tambien parte del borde del malecon, y de la avenida, pareciera neblina, pero era el rocio de las olas, que son el producto de las burbujas que rompen en la interfaz aire - mar, tenia tiempo que no veia este fenomeno natural en el ambiente marino. A pesra de ser viernes, las personas estaban activas entrenando ya sea caminando, trotando, haciendo ejercicios. Un ambiente muy atractivo lucia hoy en este espacio. --- Para el entrenamiento de este dia mantuve un ritmo medio entre 7:16 y 6:23 min/Km, me senti bien, ya que podia conversar bien con mi amiga sin sentir fatiga. Fue un entrenamiento muy productivo, y en muy buena compañia, ya que conversar con personas que nos gusta lo mismo todo fluye muy bien, y nunca paramos de hablar. Siempre tenemos opciones para diversificar los entrenamientos y asi de esta forma mantenernos siempre activos, y no caer en rutinas aburridas, de estar forma siempre estamos animados. Y sigo activa con mis entrenamientos, preparandome para el entrenamiento largo de la semana.😎 . >Greetings and blessings.! >

>Friday. Today’s plan was to run 8 kilometers at a moderate pace. My husband has been swamped with work and hasn’t been able to train, so I arranged to meet up with a friend to go for a run together—and catch up while we jogged. That way, it’s easy to tell if we’re in Zone 2, because we can hold a conversation. Since we live close by, I picked her up at 5:40 a.m., and we both set off at a comfortable pace. A beautiful sunrise dazzled us today, accompanied by a mist over the sea that also covered part of the boardwalk and the avenue. It looked like fog, but it was actually the spray from the waves—the result of bubbles breaking at the air-sea interface. It had been a while since I’d seen this natural phenomenon in a marine setting. Even though it was Friday, people were out and about, training by walking, jogging, or doing exercises. The atmosphere here today was very lively. --- >For today’s workout, I maintained a pace between 7:16 and 6:23 min/km. I felt good, as I could easily chat with my friend without feeling tired. It was a very productive workout, and in great company, since talking with people who share our interests makes everything flow smoothly, and we never stop talking. We always have options to diversify our workouts and thus stay active, avoiding boring routines; this way, we’re always in high spirits. body.title: Release of new HAF API stack 1.28.6 next week
body.body:
![blocktrades update.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSihw8Kz4U7TuCQa98DDdCzqbqPFRumuVWAbareiYZW1Z/blocktrades%20update.png)

It has been quite a while since I've made a post, but it doesn't mean the BlockTrades team hasn't been busy, quite the opposite. 

The reason I haven't posted is I've been personally swamped with work since I started using Claude Code back in mid November, working around 12-14 hours a day, 7 days a week (something I haven't done since back in my early twenties when I started my first company).

Usually I report on the whole teams work, but it has been a long time since my last report, and it would take a huge post just to summarize what other team members have done. So mostly this is a report on the US programming team's work (which is just me and efrias).

### Moving from coding to clauding 

Our team had previously been using other AI tools like Github Copilot to assist with coding, but the gains, while substantial, weren't impressive enough to suck me back into full-time (or perhaps more accurately \

) programming again. 

But then I read an article that recommended Claude Code, and when I mentioned it to efrias, he said he had already bought a personal license and switched to it,  and he said it was much better than Copilot, so I decided to give it a try (Copilot was $10/month, Claude Code was $200/month).

Once I started working with Claude Code, I realized just how much we could potentially accelerate our work (10x or more faster), and also what the potential blocker to that was: a slow and flaky software CI (build-test system) that was designed to just barely be fast enough for purely human-based software development, but which completely failed for AI-assisted software development.

### Build and test (CI) overhaul

The essential problem was that AI can add a new feature or make a bug fix in 5-15 minutes, but we had tests that ran for up to 90 minutes (and had intermittent fails too which makes it hard to judge whether a code change has caused the problem or it is just a random test fail, which leaves you and the AI particularly confused as to what to do next).

So I spent the next 2 1/2 months overhauling our compile and test software on most of our repos (we have a lot of repos) on https://gitlab.syncad.com, eliminating intermittently failing tests (AKA flaky tests) and reducing the time to build the software and run the tests. The overhauled CI still is far from perfect, but it is much more consistent and considerably faster. Also, based on the type of the change, the CI can decide to do less work, using less computer resources and finishing much faster. 

### NFS caching of HAF and HAF app replay data

Another big change I did was to add a NFS-based caching for replayed data for haf and haf apps our CI builders. This is not only useful for speeding up test times, it also makes it easier to compare \

data for modified code, making it easier to diagnose bugs and performance regressions over time.

### Major CI hardware overhaul

We also made major upgrades to our builder hardware as well. We added 2 new AMD 9950X3D systems with ZFS raided gen5 4 and 8TB Crucial T705 nvme drives as builders to speed up the bottleneck jobs. We updated the hardware where gitlab itself was hosted to run on a 9950 as well. And we put all the builders on an internal 10GB network along with a local docker registry  and a local artifacts cache to reduce the load on the gitlab server. Most recently (this week), we also adding local caching for external packages (e.g. npm and pip) to speed up CI, reduce traffic to external servers, and avoid CI fails when 3rd party servers are offline or operating in a degraded mode.

## Updates to the HAF API server stack (version 1.28.6)

After I got through overhauling CI, I was able to finally kick into high gear on updates to the software itself. I made a lot of  changes across the repos, but probably the most significant changes are performance changes to HAF and to the most important HAF app (hivemind).  

### Speedup of hivemind replay from 60 hours down to 24 hours

Hivemind in particular has long been a bottleneck for our release cycle because even on our very fastest machines (which we only have a few of), it took over 2 1/2 days to do a replay, which meant every code change in hive, haf, or hivemind itself required a 2 1/2 testing cycle (and that's neglecting another 14 hours for the replay of haf itself if the change was in hive or haf rather than hivemind). Now hivemind fully replays in a single day, making this much less painful.

## HAF API stack expected next week

We've already deployed a release candidate of the new stack to https://api.syncad.com for apps to test their code against. I recommend you all do this quickly, as we'll be deploying the same stack to https://api.hive.blog soon as a truly \

production test before recommending it to other Hive API server operators.

# And now for the truly incomprehensible portion of this post...

Below are the changes to the Hive API calls that may impact Hive app developers:

## Breaking Changes (fields removed/added/changed type)

### 1. `HIVE_ENABLE_SMT` removed from config

**Affected methods:** `database_api.get_config`, `condenser_api.get_config`, `call` (wrapping get_config)

The `HIVE_ENABLE_SMT` boolean field has been removed from the config response. Code
that reads this field will get `undefined`/`KeyError` instead of `false`.

```
# Before (HIVE_BLOCKCHAIN_VERSION 1.28.3):
\

: false

# After (HIVE_BLOCKCHAIN_VERSION 1.28.6):
(field absent)
```

### 3. `stats.muted_reasons` — new field on posts

**Affected methods:** `bridge.get_discussion`, `bridge.get_account_posts`,
`bridge.get_ranked_posts`, `bridge.get_post`

Posts that are grayed/muted now include a `muted_reasons` array in `stats`.
Previously `stats.gray` could be `true` but the reason was not exposed.

```json
// Before:
\

: [2], ... }
```

The `muted_reasons` field is only present when the post is grayed. The array
contains integer reason codes. Multiple reasons can apply simultaneously.
~43 instances observed across 543K requests.

#### Reason codes

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| 0 | `MUTED_COMMUNITY_MODERATION` | Explicitly muted by a community moderator |
| 1 | `MUTED_COMMUNITY_TYPE` | Post in a journal/council community where author lacks member+ role |
| 2 | `MUTED_PARENT` | Reply to a muted post (inherited) |
| 3 | `MUTED_REPUTATION` | Author has negative reputation (calculated dynamically) |
| 4 | `MUTED_ROLE_COMMUNITY` | Author has a muted role in the community (calculated dynamically) |

These codes can be retrieved programmatically via `bridge.list_muted_reasons_enum`:

```bash
curl -s http://api.hive.blog \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\

, ...]
//  ^ author now included as first entry
```

This is an intentional bug fix. Code that checks `.length` or iterates over
rebloggers will see one extra entry.

## Value Changes (same fields, different values)

These are due to bug fixes in hivemind 2.0.0dev1. The values change but the
types and field names remain the same.

### Community statistics (num_pending, sum_pending, num_authors)

**Affected methods:** `bridge.get_community`, `bridge.list_communities`

Pending post counts and payout sums differ slightly due to changes in how
`is_paidout` is calculated. These are small numeric differences (typically
1–18 fewer pending posts per community in bodyval).

### Post counts (post_count)

**Affected methods:** `bridge.get_profile`, `bridge.get_profiles`

Account `post_count` values are slightly higher in bodyval (typically +1 to +17).
This affects high-volume posters most.

### Trending tags statistics

**Affected methods:** `condenser_api.get_trending_tags`

Tag-level `comments`, `top_posts`, and `total_payouts` values differ slightly
due to the post counting and payout status changes above.

### Children counts

**Affected methods:** `condenser_api.get_content`, `bridge.get_post`

Post `children` counts may differ by small amounts (e.g., +4) due to the
post counting changes.

### Reply ordering

**Affected methods:** `bridge.get_account_posts` (sort=replies)

When multiple replies have the same timestamp, the tiebreaking order may differ.
This affects which post appears at a given array index but not the set of posts
returned.

## Non-Changes (confirmed identical)

The following were verified identical across 543K requests:

- **Block data:** `block_api.get_block`, `condenser_api.get_block`, `block_api.get_block_range` — all match
- **Account data:** `condenser_api.get_accounts`, `database_api.find_accounts` — match (except `vesting_withdraw_rate` 1→0 cleanup on a few accounts, intentional)
- **Transaction data:** `condenser_api.get_transaction`, `account_history_api.get_account_history` — match
- **Market data:** `condenser_api.get_order_book`, `get_ticker`, `get_recent_trades` — match
- **Witness data:** `condenser_api.get_witnesses_by_vote`, `get_witness_by_account` — match
- **RC data:** `rc_api.find_rc_accounts`, `rc_api.get_rc_stats` — match
- **Follow data:** `condenser_api.get_followers`, `get_following`, `get_follow_count` — match
- **Proposal data:** `database_api.list_proposals`, `list_proposal_votes` — match

Those who only listen, without questioning, without knowing a multimeter, and without analyzing each of the sentences will end up arriving at the wrong answer. body.body:
To affirm or claim one's success is easy but to actually deserve what you're getting isn't something everyone can claim they do.
Most times we simply give the respects to something vague like luck and divine placement and although those are valid reasons for success too, one person we should give respect to is ourselves.


[![17758575435947199349832708039383.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seki1/ALBh1mFoStBxSApZgFg1HENCkmoE6x9wmvW16pUqZysZ2v5F2Cr4iDehJT7rJse.png)](https://share.google/edhRsK8wNVS0CRfMV)
Before having my bedtime shower, something moved me to play Kendrick's GNX album and after a while, the song **\

** started playing.
It's a song I've well known to be powerful, on the level of Reincarnated, Gloria and the heart part 6, and it's a song I've listened to multiple times.
Yet today is the first day I'm actually listened to it. Listening and truly understanding what it's about.

In this song, with the title referencing the biblical \

(heaven) Kendrick plays the role of a man listing his actions and roles, things he did to deserve him entrance into the garden.
In another way, the song is a memento of his accolades and struggles. He deserves everything he gets because of the sacrifices he's made and the morals he's upheld.

I'm about to clock a new year, a year older, a year wiser and hopefully maybe happier. 
Yet, I've found out that this new year is coming with its troubles, finishing school, getting a job and earning money.
Starting up my business plans and a few other things. 
My country isn't the best for a starry eyed youth with big dreams, thankfully the stars in my eyes were plucked since I was 7 and now turning 21, I can say my dreams are becoming bigger and with more form.
I guess I'm just waiting for a time when the results come out.

The kind of results that would make some question their sources.
So in a way, this song is like an affirmation and reflection.
It makes me ask myself questions..
What have I done to actually deserve my successes?
Do I deserve them? Or am I just lucky...

body.title: 復原中的一些反思
body.body:
今天要換一下我平時發文的作瘋。我們先來看圖作文，下面圖片過後才來心得分享。畢竟今天的話題有一點點沉重。

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdEfNjdrHsFu88hrWSrcsPzY9XgiFtBfJh8ncwLM6vqwQ/1775807978417.jpg)

見復健師前一天晚上，母老虎心血來潮是要吃肉骨茶。雖然明知膽固醇很高，還是去了。

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeHDPRqrwwuraKe5L2WTPoaqpVZcdyj1seBCsyGWti4NS/1775807978509.jpg)

隔天早上七早八早就趕路，坐地鐵去中央醫院。一路上肚子已經嘰哩咕嚕響。到站了時間還早，於是買了咖啡和三明治。

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUWvjA6gB5SDdehxmxUw8etfvnUCQPAGtKwWTmoJjzjEk/1775807978594.jpg)

這些藥物的藥效很強大，而且我們這種病患服用的更是重量級的藥。雖然趕路來，但是心跳還是不會過百，呼吸變得很長又很重，動作也快不起來。

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWtjakkakoxRKFpuYvQVx4UaJy2egQba7MFxHddf7EH8Y/1775807978659.jpg)

麵包哽完以後，直接用咖啡把藥罐進去，才過去醫院找復健師小姐姐。這次不錯，還真的安排了個比較年輕的小姐姐給我。不然每次都是很壯的大媽或健碩的男護士😅

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmStpFrxWufUTD2y5AjVbdsny4e1z7oBzkJovY3knRWAJV/1775807978718.jpg)

重頭戲在回程時，這一天是這一季最後一次上來醫院這一間鍛煉場所。以後拉叔就必須去戶外鍛煉，跟另一班精英選手去做有氧運動。有鑑於此，我決定了馬上從這裡走過去買醫藥報告，因為這一區比較接近那個醫藥報告部門。室內復健部門和醫藥報告部門之間是一家清真寺-回教堂。

以前也有經過這個回教堂，但是一般都會直接路過不看一眼。但這天不知什麼神推鬼使，覺得內部有什麼閃閃發亮的，就看了一眼……哦……是餐車呀……餐……不對……說時遲那時快，我人已經“快步”離開了看到“手推餐車”那個房。一邊步行一邊覺得不妥，那根本就是回教堂的停屍間😑 那個不是餐車，是用來罩著屍體的擔架。

在馬來西亞凡是加入了回教，都不能出教。在馬來有立定的憲法，註明回教徒的子孫也必須是制定回教。不管是外嫁內娶，男入女出，另一邊的伴侶也必須改教改名。所以，這個國家的回教教徒，目前已經超過了全國的百分之七十以上了。凌晨六點鐘你要是聽到有人大聲念經，震動整個社區的，就是我們的好友回教徒了。

我買醫藥報告時，一直心不在焉，想了很多事。如果那天我也走了，那麼躺在那個冰冷的餐車上是什麼感覺？這又讓我想起很多素食者會形容我們吃葷的人等同吃屍體。可不是？把一具人的屍體放在餐車上，用不銹鋼材的蓋子罩住，還不是一樣？鴨的屍體要進烤爐才有烤鴨，人的屍體要進焚化爐才有骨灰可以收起來以後方便拜祭。不同的是，我們人把烤鴨子吃了，但你不會想烤人吧？

知道了餐車停在那裡，回程時不自覺的往回教堂裡面看去，還真有一群人伴著一具木乃伊，就是人體形狀被包裹著，讓在毛毯上，身邊圍繞著一群人在念經。經過那個餐車時，又忍不住再往裡面看了一下……整個人都涼了。心寒了一哈……我不是膽小怕鬼的人，但是這一刻，自己剛面臨過的差不多進烤爐的經驗全部湧現了在眼前。帶現在，餐桌上擺著的滷豬耳朵，那頭豬可是別人的孩子唉😑我這，恐怕一陣子吃不下別人的家人、家豬、家雞、家鴨了……誰不是別人的孩子？我也有孩子，如果別人問我，我可以烤你娃不？難道我說可以？

body.title: Japan’s Regulatory Evolution: Beyond Assets to Strategic Infrastructure
body.body: https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/pichat/9751cb09c582f3fe05fe0205a37cd6a4482fc8d4.png\n\nThe financial landscape in Japan is undergoing a fundamental structural realignment as the government moves toward reclassifying Bitcoin and other crypto assets. This transition is not merely a semantic change but a systemic integration designed to bring digital assets into the fold of traditional financial frameworks. By potentially shifting the legal status of crypto from \
governed by the Payment Services Act to \

under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (FIEA), Japan is signaling a clear move toward high-level institutionalization.

From a systems-thinking perspective, this shift addresses a critical root cause of limited institutional adoption: regulatory ambiguity. When crypto is treated as a standard financial instrument, it opens the floodgates for traditional investment trusts and institutional funds to include Bitcoin in their portfolios with a clear legal mandate. This move creates a feedback loop of stability; higher institutional participation leads to decreased volatility, which in turn fosters further regulatory clarity and public trust.

The data supports this trend. Japan has consistently been a first-mover in the crypto space, being one of the first nations to implement a licensing system for exchanges. However, the existing framework primarily focused on consumer protection within payment services. The new direction targets the broader financial ecosystem, aiming to align crypto assets with stocks and bonds. This alignment is expected to significantly impact the tax structure—moving from a miscellaneous income tax (which can be as high as 55%) to a separate flat tax rate of 20%, consistent with other financial products.

This change is not about following a pattern; it is about creating a new one. By dismantling the silos between digital and traditional finance, Japan is positioning itself as a global hub for the future of decentralized finance, backed by a robust, evidence-based regulatory framework. The story being told here through the data is one of maturity—moving away from the \
era into a structured, scalable financial future.\n\nPosted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@pichat/japans-regulatory-evolution-beyond-assets-to-strategic-infrastructure-5zc)

body.title: Holy Friday | Monomad Challenge
body.body: > Happy to greet you all through the Black and White Photography Community. I hope everyone participating here is doing well. This is my second time in this community and my second entry for the #Monomad challenge. Those who follow me know that I love taking photos and sharing them in full color, but since last Friday I've been thinking about these images in black and white, as they are from Good Friday. All this week I've been sharing my adventures and a bit of my Catholic rituals during Holy Week, and Good Friday is one of the days I respect most all year, as well as being one of the saddest in terms of what we commemorate.

> ![IMG_20260402_174544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23xVF4bPs2TNtNkjYgWuYTETEfg8GsUj8JxaUqTnDfC2BQ61PtSXmfg2oFo7UFEKPmBTf.jpg) ![IMG_20260402_174610.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23uQiCCF8L3KmpimWsojkwWessseY8Zf4wfBMqv1jTetKFpUyrF6Sd1sv3MmfUknegdoZ.jpg)
The first image that captured my memory is a sculpture of Our Lady of Sorrows and the dead Christ, and that is the most representative image of Good Friday, the only day of the year that Mass is not celebrated in the Catholic Church. This particular image is located in the Church of Our Lady of Mercy in Caracas, a huge temple with gray walls that helped me connect with the feeling of that day. My family and I attended two churches; this was the first, where we joined in prayer at 3 p.m. with the reading of the Seven Last Words. Afterward, we went to a nearby church, the Caracas Cathedral, and there we attended the Passion service. In particular, all the moments and readings of the day conveyed images that are easily associated with feelings of sadness, death, and black and white, at least for me...

> ![IMG_20260402_215236.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/243BcGRdQMNHWVZT1sExwPJLLezD95aP6bgXRb7oJjU8gHGyuHpTjHthD3garT59Z4duP.jpg) ![IMG_20260403_172217.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23wCBXykKAJGGxvVdFFm3QheUDvbGTJmZLe4uD6Knaybrrd5oWTfSi68ckqMJ9JwFygB6.jpg)
Although I like color images, the inspiration came in black and white this time, so I've edited the photos and zoomed in on what I really want to share. Good Friday night in Caracas takes on a somber tone, as there are at least nine large churches in the city center, and at nightfall the processions begin. All the images of the Virgin Mary in mourning are taken out to walk the streets with mournful chants and prayers following behind them, and some churches also bring out the image of the Holy Sepulchre of Jesus. Generally, the images and the processions of the people meet in the streets; it's a special moment, one that I deeply respect. It reminds me of my father, who always told me that Good Friday is a day that must be respected.

> ![IMG_20260402_210326.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23wC1PqYswxyWeuhtzc8XkT8R3oG3vBXAMSWfvjwvutVPntYF82xkH5Yd7rknFy5h9kz2.jpg) ![IMG_20260402_225919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23wqke3ZHBmimEmNdChuexNaTUo8qR6rrHSBYnGCUrbG8VrA1fFjG86ZYYtpctMaEbEzt.jpg)
I understand that everyone feels differently; some people don't believe, and some are simply unaware. Even I don't know the truth. I'm glad to have a belief in something as beautiful as the story of Jesus, who is the representation of God made man. I believe that Good Friday is a crucial day in Holy Week and for Catholics in general, and when you're so immersed in what it's meant to commemorate, nostalgia, sadness, and sublime feelings arise, which these images perfectly represent. Candles, tears, sadness, prayer, and meditation—that's what Good Friday means to me, and now these black and white images also serve as a reminder of what 2026 was like, recorded here on my blog. I hope you liked them too, and I'll take advantage of the community theme to say goodbye again with the first image, but in color, so you can appreciate the beauty of the art, design, and decorations of that day 🙏
![IMG_20260402_175124.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jesuslnrs/23w2jFr4XsVZ54hT1KzrG9WUasBzAxauCTf56KCc8XtZtfKgtULcnJpA2LibkcWrbQopp.jpg)

Háblate más lindo, 
mirate con más paciencia, 
deja de exígirte tanto y empieza a abrazarte como  abrazas a los demás.

No necesitas que alguien te regale flores si puedes florecer desde adentro.

Celebremos el amor que se queda, el que te acompaña todos los días, el que te sostiene incluso cuando dudas, tu Amor Propio.

 Elígete, cuídate, regálate momentos que te recuerden lo valiosa que eres.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUAoLjaYre2y8Z2YUW31rPdHycyNx28ZMQ99Fc6TgkdBo/1775750389397.jpg)

Speak to yourself more kindly,
look at yourself with more patience,
stop demanding so much from yourself and start hugging yourself the way you hug others.

You don't need someone to give you flowers if you can bloom from within.

Let’s celebrate the love that stays — the love that accompanies you every day, the love that holds you up even when you doubt. Your self-love.

Choose yourself, take care of yourself, give yourself moments that remind you how precious you are.

body.title: Crecer, soltar y aprender en el momento justo
body.body: Qué tal, comunidad. Espero que se encuentren bien. He estado un poco ausente, pero hoy regreso con algo más personal, casi como un desahogo. Han sido semanas intensas… no precisamente trágicas ni malas, pero sí cargadas de muchas cosas en muy poco tiempo. De esos momentos en los que uno se detiene un segundo y piensa: “¿en qué momento pasó todo esto?”. En lo personal, como algunos saben, soy padre de un nene de 3 años. Después de celebrar su cumpleaños, comenzamos a observar algo que nos hizo reflexionar bastante: al compararlo con otros niños de su edad, sentíamos que aún se comportaba como un bebé.

/> Otros niños hablaban más, formaban oraciones completas, hacían cosas por sí solos como quitarse los zapatos, subir escaleras o incluso jugar de manera más independiente. Eso nos llevó a tomar la decisión de iniciar terapia ocupacional con él. No porque estuviera “mal”, sino porque queríamos darle herramientas para desarrollarse mejor. Y siendo completamente honestos, entendimos algo importante: parte de esa “inmadurez” también era responsabilidad nuestra. Lo habíamos sobreprotegido más de la cuenta. ¿A qué me refiero? Evitaba que subiera escaleras por miedo a que se cayera, siempre lo ayudaba en todo, incluso le cambiaba la ropa aunque ya podía intentar hacerlo solo. Muchas veces interpretaba lo que quería decir en lugar de darle la oportunidad de expresarse mejor. Básicamente, le resolvía antes de que lo intentara. No le estaba dando espacio para equivocarse, aprender y comunicarse. Han pasado dos meses desde entonces… y el cambio ha sido impresionante. Ahora lo veo diferente. Ya no es ese bebé dependiente, sino un niño que busca su independencia, que intenta, que se equivoca, pero también aprende. Habla más, se expresa mejor y hasta reclama cuando siente que puede hacer algo por su cuenta. Claro, para nosotros siempre será nuestro pequeño, pero es evidente que está creciendo, y rápido.

>Y ese crecimiento también viene con una pequeña nostalgia… porque uno empieza a entender que cada etapa pasa más rápido de lo que quisiera.

En lo laboral, también han ocurrido cambios importantes. En la empresa hubo una reestructuración y, de alguna manera, salí beneficiado al ser considerado para un nuevo cargo. Honestamente, con los gastos adicionales de sus terapias, esto llegó en el momento justo, como una especie de equilibrio dentro del caos. Pero no todo es perfecto. Con estos cambios, mi antiguo jefe renunció, y ahora estoy asumiendo tanto mi nuevo rol como parte del anterior. Eso significa más carga laboral, más tiempo en la oficina y menos margen para desconectarme. Y aquí viene otra de esas pequeñas grandes realidades: ahora que mi hijo se expresa mejor, entiende más y tiene mayor noción del tiempo, se molesta cuando llego tarde. Ya no es el mismo niño que simplemente jugaba sin notar la hora; ahora espera, pregunta, siente.

></center>

He tenido que reorganizarme, ajustar prioridades y ser más consciente del tiempo. Porque hay algo que no tiene precio: llegar a casa y escuchar ese “Papá, llegaste”. Sentarme a jugar con él, escuchar cómo me cuenta su día, reírnos juntos… conversaciones que hace dos meses simplemente no existían.

Y ahí es donde todo cobra sentido.

A veces uno se pierde en las responsabilidades, en el trabajo, en las preocupaciones, y olvida que estos momentos son los que realmente importan. Que el crecimiento no es solo de ellos, sino también de nosotros como padres.

Listo. Necesitaba sacarlo.

Gracias por leerme, comunidad. Espero que mi experiencia les deje algo, aunque sea una pequeña reflexión. Si están pasando por algo similar, sepan que no están solos; todos estamos aprendiendo en el camino.

Les deseo un excelente fin de semana.

body.title: Eres lo que dices: El impacto invisible de tus palabras | You Are What You Say: The Invisible Impact of Your Words
body.body:
> A veces, inconscientemente, hacemos comentarios negativos sobre nosotros, por ejemplo: “Soy un desastre” o “Hago todo mal”. Con estos comentarios que no son precisamente positivos, nos definimos y a la vez nos limitamos. Nosotros somos capaces de hacer grandes cosas; además, siempre estamos en constante evolución, así que no podemos ser un desastre toda la vida o hacer todo mal siempre.
\n\n

> Muchas veces esos comentarios no se originaron de nuestro propio pensamiento, sino que estamos repitiendo lo que alguien más dijo. Las palabras tienen poder, por eso, si escuchamos cualquier cosa durante mucho tiempo, inconscientemente lo terminaremos creyendo y eso limitará nuestra forma de actuar e influirá en las decisiones que tomemos. Esas palabras pueden influir en nuestra autoestima, causarnos estrés, volvernos inseguros, pesimistas, entre otros, por eso debemos desecharlas de nuestra mente.
\n\n

> Muchas veces, lo decimos con tanta naturalidad que ni siquiera somos conscientes de cuándo lo decimos, pero si lo analizamos, podremos darnos cuenta de ello. Saber sobre el problema es el primer paso, luego tendremos que intentar dejar de decirlo. Esto no es tan fácil porque para muchas personas esos comentarios se vuelven parte de su vida y los dicen sin pensar. Quitar algo cotidiano no es fácil, pero tampoco imposible.
https://images.pexels.com/photos/5910961/pexels-photo-5910961.jpeg
Imagen de

> Algo importante que aprendí, es que a veces las personas tienen una perspectiva diferente de lo que son las palabras hirientes, por lo que suelen decírselas a todo el mundo sin pensar que estas causan algún daño. También que si no respondes ante palabras hirientes, las personas se acostumbrarán a decirlas sin medirse porque saben que no habrá consecuencia alguna. Debemos tener cuidado con eso y darles un límite para no terminar creyendo lo que dicen.
\n\n

> Para lidiar con eso, se puede enfrentar a la otra persona y preguntarle de frente si su intención al decir esas palabras es herirte o si le hace feliz hacerte sentir mal. Al principio eso los dejará desconcertados; luego buscaban todo tipo de excusas para salir de la situación, pero con el tiempo eso cambiará y dejarás de ser un objetivo.
\n\n

> Yo sabía soportar esos comentarios, al principio no sabía por qué aguantaba tantos insultos, luego entendí que era porque en mi mente lo veía como algo normal, incluso me los decía a mí misma hasta que alguien me preguntó de frente por qué decía cosas malas sobre mí cuando no eran ciertas, que ellos no pensaban así sobre mí. Debo decir que eso me dejó en shock y avergonzada al mismo tiempo, no supe cómo responderles, solo hice lo posible para cambiar la conversación.
https://images.pexels.com/photos/11943528/pexels-photo-11943528.jpeg
Imagen de

>Luego, al llegar a casa, me detuve a pensar detenidamente en eso y me di cuenta de que no eran mis pensamientos, yo no pensaba esas cosas de mí. Desde ese momento, fui consciente cada vez que hacía ese tipo de comentarios y me frenaba; debo decir que me tomó demasiado tiempo cambiar eso, no fue de la noche a la mañana.

> Desde que fui consciente de ese hecho y comencé a cambiarlo, mi vida mejoró positivamente; me sentía más libre, segura y feliz. Por eso, ya sea que el caso de la persona sea que repetía lo que escuchaba o si lo creaba él mismo, cambiar ese hábito mejorará significativamente su vida, así que los invito a analizar lo que dicen sobre sí mismos.

Gracias por leer

https://images.hive.blog/DQmcbWiLfXdQC69eQCsnyduRBZPQct12Fwh1iXv1wLx7hHP/11.png

English

![usuario ss (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/s-alvarez/23xVeYQ57veW8k4WLqmfunXe7HgJ5nadrSpvc1iZpoB9mxLxw1fTDFBavEuYaZVHVJueU.png)

>Sometimes, without even realizing it, we make negative comments about ourselves, such as, “I’m a mess” or “I do everything wrong.” With these comments—which aren’t exactly positive—we define ourselves and, at the same time, limit ourselves. We are capable of great things; moreover, we are constantly evolving, so we can’t be a mess our whole lives or always do everything wrong.
\n\n

> Often, those comments don’t originate from our own thoughts; rather, we’re repeating what someone else said. Words have power, so if we hear something over and over again, we’ll eventually start to believe it unconsciously, and that will limit our actions and influence the decisions we make. Those words can affect our self-esteem, cause us stress, make us insecure or pessimistic, among other things, which is why we must banish them from our minds.
\n\n

> We often say it so naturally that we aren’t even aware of when we’re saying it, but if we take a closer look, we’ll realize it. Recognizing the problem is the first step; then we’ll have to try to stop saying it. This isn’t so easy because, for many people, these comments have become part of their daily lives, and they say them without thinking. Breaking a daily habit isn’t easy, but it’s not impossible either.
https://images.pexels.com/photos/5910961/pexels-photo-5910961.jpeg
Imagen by

>One important thing I’ve learned is that sometimes people have a different perspective on what constitutes hurtful words, so they tend to say them to everyone without realizing they cause harm. Also, if you don’t respond to hurtful words, people will get used to saying them without restraint because they know there won’t be any consequences. We need to be careful about this and set boundaries so we don’t end up believing what they say.
\n\n

> To deal with that, you can confront the other person and ask them directly whether their intention in saying those words is to hurt you or whether it makes them happy to make you feel bad. At first, this will throw them off balance; they’ll come up with all sorts of excuses to get out of the situation, but over time that will change, and you’ll no longer be a target.
\n\n

>I could handle those comments. At first, I didn’t know why I put up with so many insults, but then I realized it was because, in my mind, I saw it as normal—I even told myself those things until someone asked me straight out why I was saying bad things about myself when they weren’t true, and that they didn’t think that way about me. I have to say that left me in shock and embarrassed at the same time; I didn’t know how to respond, so I just did my best to change the subject.
https://images.pexels.com/photos/11943528/pexels-photo-11943528.jpeg
Image by

> Then, when I got home, I stopped to think about it carefully and realized that those weren’t my thoughts—I didn’t actually think those things about myself. From that moment on, I became aware every time I made those kinds of comments and stopped myself; I have to say it took me a long time to change that—it didn’t happen overnight.
\n\n

> Ever since I became aware of that fact and started to change it, my life has improved; I felt freer, more confident, and happier. That’s why, whether someone is simply repeating what they hear or creating their own negative thoughts, changing that habit will significantly improve their life, so I encourage you to take a closer look at what you say about yourselves.

Thank you for reading

body.title: Inesperado encuentro/Unexpected Encounter (Esp-Eng)
body.body:
Hola, mis amigos de Hive. Espero qye todos estén bien. Hoy quiero compartirles un cuento. Ojalá les guste.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbzjbG9SC4N2ee2tUG2KhJTyD8aSjMtCP4WrzbD9GEaUw/1775861579522.jpg)

>



La noche en Centro Habana apestaba a orína y petróleo. La luna se escondía por momentos entre grandes nubes, parecía que un torrencial caería en cualquier momento. Yolanda venía de un turno de mierda en una paladar, con las manos llenas de grasa y los pies hinchados. En la esquina de Malecón y G, un tipo de camisa arremangada la miró como perro que mira un hueso.

—¿Qué es lo que hay, mulata? —dijo él, con la voz ronca de ron y pitillos prohibidos.

Yolanda le hizo un escaneo de pies a cabeza. Labios partidos, manos grandes, venas oronunciadas, olor a peligro y a poco de comer. Llevaba tres meses sin que nadie le \

, y eso la tenía más tensa que de costumbre.

—Ná —respondió ella, pero no se fue.

Él se llamaba René, o tal vez Pedro o Yosvani. Daba igual. La agarró del brazo con una fuerza que no era cariño, sino hambre de otra cosa. Subieron los escalones rotos de un edificio sin luz. El apartamento olía a humedad y a sábanas sucias. Sin mediar palabra, él la empujó contra la pared. El yeso le raspó la espalda. Yolanda sintió el corazón en la garganta, pero no se quejó. 

La cosa fue rápida, como de animales salvajes, sin caricias, nombres ni preguntas. Solo quejidos, y gritos. Un tira y afloja de dientes apretados y respiración entrecortada. Cuando terminó, él se quitó de encima como si nada, se subió el cierre y encendió un cigarro. Yolanda quedó mirando el techo lleno de goteras. Sintió el dolor y el vacío, ese que siempre le quedaba después de esos encuentros de perros callejeros. Se vistió sin mirarlo.

—¿Te vas? —preguntó él, entre bocanadas.

—¿Qué quieres, que haga café?

Bajó las escaleras a oscuras, con las piernas temblándole. Afuera, el mar del Malecón seguía rompiendo contra el muro, indiferente. Yolanda prendió un cigarro con las manos todavía sucias y pensó: \

. La noche la devoró otra vez, como todas y empezó a llover.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbYDM7bN8xYJtvqhPXXXZphZzyaQni2LRwDKomZipZK7a/img_7908.png) https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ6aNKSbseiaXo55Jhc6ykuymuUcG8J4oNN5euip3wkVH/img_9026.png

> Unexpected Encounter Hello, my Hive friends. I hope you're all doing well. Today I want to share a story with you. I hope you like it.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbzjbG9SC4N2ee2tUG2KhJTyD8aSjMtCP4WrzbD9GEaUw/1775861579522.jpg)

>

The night in Centro Habana stank of urine and diesel. The moon kept hiding behind large clouds, as if a downpour could break at any moment. Yolanda was coming off a shitty shift at a paladar, her hands greasy and her feet swollen. On the corner of Malecón and G, a guy with his sleeves rolled up looked at her like a dog eyeing a bone.

_\
he said, his voice hoarse from rum and cheap smokes.\n\nYolanda scanned him from head to toe. Cracked lips, big hands, bulging veins, a smell of danger and not enough to eat. She hadn't had anyone \
in three months, and that had her more on edge than usual.\n\n_\

she replied, but she didn't leave.

His name was René, or maybe Pedro or Yosvani. Didn't matter. He grabbed her arm with a force that wasn't affection but hunger for something else. They climbed the broken steps of a building with no lights. The apartment smelled of mildew and dirty sheets. Without a word, he shoved her against the wall. The plaster scraped her back. Yolanda felt her heart in her throat, but she didn't complain. 

It was quick, like wild animals—no caresses, no names, no questions. Just moans and cries. A push-and-pull of clenched teeth and ragged breath. When it was over, he got off her as if nothing had happened, zipped up, and lit a cigarette. Yolanda stared at the ceiling full of leaks. She felt the pain and the emptiness, the one that always stayed after those stray-dog encounters. She dressed without looking at him.

_\
\n\nShe went down the dark stairs, her legs trembling. Outside, the Malecón sea kept crashing against the wall, indifferent. Yolanda lit a cigarette with her hands still dirty and thought, \
The night swallowed her again, like every other night, and it started to rain.

body.title: 🐿️ Are You a Gathering Squirrel or a Forest Planter? [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmS9auwhpjQBji4u8rRK7r9s4aRbMKeZHRTCbKv6fsfXeg/Gemini_Generated_Image_5zhhri5zhhri5zhh.png 


In the world of finance, there are two ways to survive. Most people choose the most exhausting one: gathering acorns every day, only to eat them before the sun goes down.

If you stop running, you stop eating. That is the \

trap.

## 🌳 The Secret of the Acorn Tree (Your Assets)

The smart investor—the one seeking freedom on Hive or the stock market—understands that a portion of their acorns isn't for eating; it's for **planting**.

1. **The Gathering Squirrel (Liabilities):** Represented by the stressed robot, works hard, earns money, and spends it on things that lose value. It’s always hungry and always has to run after fleeting coins.
2. **The Planter (Assets):** Represented by the relaxed robot, takes a portion of their earnings and puts it to work. They plant a seed of compound interest (Hive Staking, dividend stocks, ETFs). At first, the tree is small and gives no shade, but over time...

## 💡 The Benefits of Owning a Forest

There comes a day when the planter no longer needs to run across the forest looking for food.

* **The tree works for you:** While you sleep, the tree grows. While you rest, new acorns and golden coins fall from the branches you planted years ago.
* **Storm Resistance:** When winter comes (the bear market), the gathering squirrel panics. The planter simply sits under their trees and lives off what falls.

## 🚀 Your Action Plan Today

Don't try to plant an entire forest today. Just make sure that **one of your acorns today becomes a seed.**

* **Do that DCA:** It doesn't matter if it's a small amount.
* **Increase your Hive Power:** Every vote you cast is water for your tree.
* **Reinvest your dividends:** It’s the fertilizer that speeds up growth.

---

## ✨ Reflection for Today:

Look at your expenses from the last week. How many were acorns you ate, and how many were seeds you planted? The future doesn't belong to those who run the fastest, but to those who have the patience to watch their trees grow.


---

# 🇪🇸 VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL

---
# 🐿️ ¿Eres una ardilla recolectora o un plantador de bosques?

En el mundo de las finanzas, hay dos formas de sobrevivir. La mayoría elige la más cansada: recolectar bellotas cada día, solo para comérselas antes de que caiga el sol.

Si dejas de correr, dejas de comer. Esa es la trampa del intercambio de \

.

## 🌳 El secreto del Árbol de Bellotas (Tus Activos)

El inversor inteligente, el que busca su libertad en Hive o en la bolsa, entiende que una parte de sus bellotas no es para comer, sino para **plantar**.

1. **La Ardilla Recolectora (El Pasivo):** Representada por el robot estresado, trabaja duro, gana dinero y lo gasta en cosas que pierden valor. Siempre tiene hambre y siempre tiene que correr tras monedas voladoras.

2. **El Plantador (El Activo):** Representado por el robot relajado, toma una parte de su ganancia y la pone a trabajar. Planta una semilla de interés compuesto (Staking en Hive, acciones de dividendos, ETFs). Al principio, el árbol es pequeño y no da sombra, pero con el tiempo...

## 💡 Los beneficios de tener un bosque

Llega un día en que el plantador ya no necesita correr por todo el bosque buscando comida.

* **El árbol trabaja por ti:** Mientras duermes, el árbol crece. Mientras descansas, caen bellotas nuevas y monedas de oro de las ramas que tú mismo plantaste hace años.

* **Resistencia a las tormentas:** Cuando llega el invierno (el mercado bajista), la ardilla recolectora entra en pánico. El plantador simplemente se sienta bajo sus árboles y vive de lo que cae.

## 🚀 Tu plan de acción hoy

No intentes plantar un bosque entero hoy. Solo asegúrate de que **una de tus bellotas de hoy se convierta en una semilla.**

* **Haz ese DCA:** No importa si es poco.
* **Aumenta tu Hive Power:** Cada voto que das es agua para tu árbol.
* **Reinvierte tus dividendos:** Es el abono que acelera el crecimiento.

---

## ✨ Reflexión para hoy:

Mira tus gastos de la última semana. ¿Cuántas fueron bellotas que te comiste y cuántas fueron semillas que plantaste? El futuro no pertenece a los que más corren, sino a los que tienen la paciencia de ver crecer sus árboles.

**¿Qué semilla vas a plantar hoy? ¡Te leo en los comentarios! 👇**

body.title: Book review: The housemaid by Freida Mcfadden
body.body:
Mystery, scandal, and a plot twist in my opinion, the perfect kind of fiction. If you're trying to get into reading fiction, I would definitely recommend this book. With only 329 pages, it’s not very long and can easily be finished in a day or two, depending on how much time you have.

It’s fast-paced, easy to read, and has some questionable moments that keep things interesting. I went into the story blindly, which made the plot twist even more surprising. The story also switches perspectives midway through, which I think was a good way to see how everything really played out.

Spoilers ahead:

​

 > ! [Click to reveal] One criticism I do have is that the ending felt a bit predictable. The way he was dealt with, and how everything was resolved, felt a little too convenient and not as impactful as the rest of the story. It took away some of the tension that had been built up earlier on. 

Star rating ⭐⭐⭐

I’d give this a 3-star rating not because it’s bad, but because it feels more like a good, entertaining read than a truly memorable one. It keeps you hooked while you’re reading, but once you’re done, it doesn’t leave a lasting impact. Some parts feel a bit unrealistic, and a few moments rely more on shock value than depth.

body.title: 🖤 Still Figuring It Out
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdbUBBjPyfM7eRuWtm8M38juHNgtHM7hxSAFAHEL7XMxa/IMG_6646.png 

Some days I feel confident.

Other days… not so much.

I look at myself and I’m not sure if I’m proud yet, or if I’m still in the middle of becoming someone I’ll recognize one day. It’s strange being at this stage of life — where you’ve finished one chapter, but the next one hasn’t fully started.

I know what I want. I want to be a lawyer. I want to build a life that feels stable, strong, and mine. But right now, I’m still trying to find the way to get there.

So I take pictures. I post. I try.

It might not look like much from the outside, but for me… it’s part of something bigger. It’s me refusing to stay stuck.

Maybe I don’t have everything figured out yet.

But I haven’t given up on myself either.

And I think that matters more than anything.

Yeah this Phillies offense is looking bad. I've spoken on this in several recent posts and it's only getting more obvious! TWO games in a row of scoring NOTHING. Sheesh. I can't even pinpoint one player whose to blame, the whole lineup has just felt average at BEST, and very recently it's looked awful.

The Phils are now 6-6 and about to play a very competent Arizona Diamondbacks team. The Diamondbacks are sending Michael Soroka out on the mound, and that's not a very exciting thought with this struggling offense. Soroka has looked sharp so far in 2026. Once upon a time seven years ago, Soroka was an All-Star for the Braves and finished sixth in Cy Young voting. 

Soroka has been injured and on a downswing ever since but this could be a comeback year for him. He's only 28 years old and is 2-0 with a 0.90 ERA to start the year. He's in the prime of his career and looking to revive himself. Scary thought to be honest.

Jesús Luzardo is on the mound which is decent, but unless he can hit some homers for the Phillies, it doesn't matter how well he pitches, LOL. 

Let's see if the boys can turn it around in Arizona. I really don't wanna see them drop below .500. Still 150 games left.

It's been rough but I still believe!

body.title: Maybe you didn't loose them... You just kept going forward.
body.body: > #### Success, they say, will cost you friends. At first, that sounds scary. It makes success feel lonely, like something you gain while losing the people you once shared everything with. But as I grow and reflect more on life, I’m beginning to see it differently. Life is a journey. And like every journey, not everyone you start with will finish with you. Not because they are bad people, not because something went wrong but simply because everyone has their own destination. As you climb the ladder of life, you begin to notice that some people stop along the way. Some settle, some find comfort, and some reach what they consider their peak. And that’s okay. That is their destination. But what happens when you haven’t reached yours yet? You keep going. And sometimes, that means leaving people behind not out of pride, not out of wickedness, but out of purpose. Because you owe it to yourself to keep moving, to keep growing, to keep chasing what you believe your life should be. It doesn’t make you a bad person. It doesn’t mean you don’t value the memories you shared or the moments you built together. It simply means your journey is not finished yet. We often misunderstand this part of growth. We label it as “losing friends” when in reality, it’s just life happening. It’s people walking their paths at their own pace. Some people are meant to walk with you for a season, not a lifetime. And that doesn’t reduce their importance, it only defines their role in your story. The truth is, growth sometimes requires separation. Not every friendship will survive change, ambition, or evolution. And that’s one of the hardest parts of becoming who you’re meant to be. But instead of feeling guilty, we should learn to appreciate those moments for what they were, beautiful, necessary, and part of the journey. So yes, success may “cost” you friends… But maybe it’s not really a cost. Maybe it’s just life aligning everyone with where they truly belong. ![759146.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eugenia7499/23uFMPiCDH5f7TjaTmKmc73rawJeRN9eN6XKceDsCrYPTJvLgoWQVNMatNaYXYffa2VFb.jpg) ***[Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/woman-in-black-jacket-walking-on-road-during-daytime-6OIPJZuhCk0)*** > #### Have you ever outgrown a friendship while chasing your goals? How did it make you feel?

body.title: Five Minute Freewrite: analyst of what?
body.body: >In a very remote village called Zulu, there exists a man whose IQ was the highest in the entire village. People would often go to him for answers, and he would often answer to the best of his knowledge. His fame spread so far that even people from the neighboring villages would seek him out for advice and solutions. Everyone started assuming he had an answer to everything, but little did they know that he did not know everything. One hot afternoon, a group of people came to see him and ask him a particular question. The question was “between men and women in the community, who had the highest number”. He was very confused at first because he would need to have the records of people in the community. Now, because he was the wisest person in the community, he decided to inform them about the census and the need to count the total number of people in the community. His community people agree, and that was how the very first census was held in the community. Using the records from the census, he was able to analyze and provide an answer to their previous question. Shortly after, a similar question was asked: “They wanted to know the total number of children being born in the village yearly”. It was at this point that he had to inform the customer that all these kinds of questions can only be answered when they have the appropriate records, and that was how the whole community knows the importance of record-keeping. After several months, the village was developing rapidly, and he sat down on his chair, wondering analyst of what people would call him as he was literally good at running any data as long as the data was correctly prepared. body.title: A Rough Reflection
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYvQsESmQ1VMekZCQErTqNBm8SRpqucX1Nno4KzJwSSJW/eveev.png 



This post isn't going to be warm and fuzzy....In fact, it's kind of sad.

My wife woke up this morning and got a message from a friend of hers.  One of her best friends had passed away completely unexpected.  And while the situation about her passing has many layers, here's the super sad part of this story.

She's leaving behind a son, who is the same age as my middle kid.

Before I get into some commentary on the situation, let me just say that I hurt for her family.  And the thought of this little kid not having their mother in their life at such a young age is devastating.  I will continue to pray for her family and I hope if you are the praying type, you could as well.

As for the death of my wife's friend, this is where things get really tough.  My wife said to me after she shed a few tears this morning...

*\

*

You see, my wife's friend had some serious problems when it came to substance abuse.  So much so that after years and years of counselling and rehab, the addiction eventually took it's toll.  And again, I'm not commenting on the cause of her death because there is still so much we don't know.

But here's the results of the situation, regardless of whether or not she was going through personal battles in her life....

A family is left mourning.  A mother and father buried their daughter today and now a child is going to be raised without a mother.

I mean, this isn't right.

Death isn't right.  Addictions aren't right.  This is not how this world should have ever been.

My wife is really having a hard time with not only the death of her friend, but also how she 'expected it'.  I think she feels guilty that she didn't do enough for her friend but I saw what my wife did do.  She prayed for her, she talked to her, she offered bible studies with her.

At the end of the day, we have decisions to make as human beings.  God gives us free will.

But I don't blame my wife's friend one single bit.  Want to know why? First we all have battles we go through.  And you never know what people are dealing with.  But also I understand this verse in Scripture, and this is the SINGLE biggest reason there is so much evil and death in this world...

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmbSRhFKo2js8oGx1QvaJzzFCeLU95FSdmT1Q7y3GBJP5j/EPHESIANS-6-12-KJV-For-we-wrestle-not-against-flesh-and-blood-but-against-principalities-against-powers-against-the-rulers--04-10-2026_04_37_PM.png 

If you are a believer or not, please read this verse a few times....

Understand what we are up against every single moment of our lives.  It's not God hurting us.  It's not God putting evil in our midst.  It's not our fellow man or woman causing illnesses...Please remember who the father of all this wickedness comes from....

The devil is a roaring lion, looking for everyone he can devour.

This is who is responsible for my wife's friends death.  Did she have a choice to make? Sure but I can never blame anyone for playing the cards they are dealt and sometimes, the devil wins.  Actually most of the time he does in this world.

But here's the promise....Here's the greatest thing you can ever read when you accept Christ as Lord and Savior...

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVdeaXGVaxD5LDsqSdkUekhQ5U7iqghtHFwXKYL1Sq1xt/JOHN-16-33-KJV-These-things-I-have-spoken-unto-you-that-in-me-ye-might-have-peace-In-the-world-ye-shall-have-tribulation--04-10-2026_04_41_PM.png 

R.I.P. T

body.title: If There Were a World War
body.body: > Should I say I don't really like this topic? I won't really say so. We can all agree that such a reality isn't a palatable one nor one that anybody would like to experience. Sadly, a similar reality has befallen some of us in our part of the world. The difference is that this is a war while what we experience is constant insecurity that has claimed lives and caused many to leave their homes forcefully. It might not be at our doorsteps yet, but we've felt the heat and pain. This makes imagining such a situation uneasy. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYn1LM7tCGrzdDxwyjB2pn7b6ugH7hJKECnJWZCr3CsRX/1775859793218.png) Well, no matter how we dread some things, they still happen. We've heard of wars happening before and even in the present day we've heard and seen the outcomes of recent ones which is no news to anyone. War is probably preventable, but the power tussle and control of leaders, and the desire to capture resources, make it inevitable. These are basically major reasons for the wars happening. And to consider what I would do in the event of a war seems then like a viable place to go in one's thoughts. I despise war and wouldn't want it to happen, which I consider we all wouldn't. The cost and effects are painful. I haven't been involved in a war situation directly, so knowing what to do in the event of one seems open-ended to me. Will I join the army that I may protect my family and the lives of others, or would I find a way to safeguard my family and get them somewhere safe? I think the first instinct in such a situation is survival. At this point, it's all man for himself or rather people for themselves. So I presume every family will be doing the same. I know this at least from movie depictions of some of the live stories of these war situations. It's every family trying to stick together and survive, which is what I'll do. We'll need to stick together and find a way to stay alive. It could be hard to do that but it's the most viable and doable option I see and know that many will do. If there are some ways I can offer assistance to the army apart from really joining them, I might do that as well. At this point, it's about surviving and doing the necessary things that could lead to that. To survive individually and as a family, I could try to collaborate with others/other families where or when necessary to have a better survivability. If there's somewhere safe we can keep put, that's where we'll be headed. body.title: DEATHLOOP | First Impressions
body.body:
![1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23zknL3nQgFEpUiFxLj8Z99UKk85CxtHVWetJsofGQhSvzMVWNUX9G1pv9uBAYmuSjKjv.gif)


How's it going, gamers? I hope everyone is doing well. So, I recently started playing DEATHLOOP, a game developed by Arkane Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks, and honestly, I have to say it right off the bat — this game is strange. Not bad at all, not even close to bad, but strange in a way that I didn't fully expect when I first launched it. It's the kind of game that starts picking at your curiosity from the very first minute, and once it gets its hooks in you, well, there's no going back. It's been pulling me in hard, and I'm honestly here for it.

So, without further ado, let me tell you a bit about my first impressions of this wild ride.

**A Strange Story With Time Loops**

![0126 (2)(3).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23xV6F9D18KyjRWFhDVeFcCpsmrESQMfEGZpCrTC7AzCVXmeeddTrNhQ5p2nogrEABM7y.jpg)

The premise of DEATHLOOP is, well, exactly what it sounds like — a loop. A death loop. You're stuck in a repeating cycle on a mysterious island called Blackreef, and the only way out is to figure out how to break it. You play as Colt Vahn, an assassin who wakes up on a beach with absolutely zero memory of who he is, what he's doing there, or how any of this started. And every time the day ends or you die, it all resets. Same beach. Same confusion. Same mess.

What makes the story so interesting — and also so strange — is how it unfolds. Because you're in a loop, you don't get handed a clean, linear narrative from the start. Instead, you have to piece it together yourself, run after run, loop after loop. Notes scattered across the world, environmental clues, audio recordings, and conversations all slowly start to paint a picture of what Blackreef actually is and why Colt is trapped here. It's an almost inverted way of storytelling. You're not being told the story, you're discovering it, and that's a genuinely cool feeling when it clicks.

The island itself is divided into four districts — Updaam, Karl's Bay, Fristad Rock, and The Complex — and the day is broken into four time periods: morning, noon, afternoon, and evening. Each expedition you take into one of these districts uses up one of those time slots, and the behaviors of everyone on the island shift depending on the time you show up. That means figuring out schedules and patterns is a big part of how you'll eventually put everything together.

**Colt Has Many Problems, and One of Them Is Julianna**

![0126 (2)(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23uQxipBohzQmKDyFajGFp4Urt2cudHdkrKrwsE1SbRLaEJaVWB2y6h16MMqYBQTZt2AJ.jpg)

Now, let's talk about one of the most entertaining and equally frustrating parts of this game — Julianna Blake. This woman is, without a doubt, one of the most persistent headaches Colt has to deal with. She's another assassin on the island, and her whole mission is the opposite of yours. While Colt wants to break the loop, Julianna is completely committed to keeping it going. And she will not let you forget it.

What makes Julianna truly special is that she can invade your game. Not just as an AI opponent, but as an actual player-controlled character if you have that option enabled. She can disguise herself as any random enemy on the island, blend in completely, and then the moment you think you're safe — boom — she's in your face. The game even announces her invasion and locks off your exit tunnels until you either deal with her or hack your way out. It's terrifying, especially when you're on a really solid run and things are going well, and then suddenly Julianna shows up to completely ruin your day.

Even when she's controlled by the AI, she's no joke. She's clever, she hits hard, and she has her own set of abilities and powers that make her a legitimate threat every single time. Colt and Julianna constantly bicker through radio communication, and their dynamic is actually one of the most entertaining parts of the game's writing. There's history between them, tension, and a very strange mutual understanding that slowly reveals itself the more you play. It adds a whole layer to the experience that keeps things from feeling purely mechanical.

**You Don't Remember Anything, and You Have to Keep Exploring the Same Clues**

![0126 (2)(4).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/242hUV52xmKnfApS3o9T6oJ86b17VHdmQX1KhQXk9fRjwgfWN1XfAzqoYVScrjbDVZ8Lg.jpg)

Here's where the game gets genuinely interesting from a gameplay standpoint. Colt's amnesia isn't just a storytelling choice — it's a design philosophy. Since he doesn't know anything when each loop starts, and neither do you as a player, you're both discovering Blackreef together in real time. Every document you find, every conversation you overhear, every clue you pick up is building toward understanding how to accomplish the impossible: kill eight specific targets called Visionaries in a single day before the loop resets.

The catch is that the game never fully holds your hand. The first couple of loops guide you gently, but after that, it largely lets you loose on the island to figure things out yourself. And that's both thrilling and occasionally maddening. You'll find a note that points you in a direction, discover a locked door you can't open yet, stumble into a completely unexpected encounter, and realize that every little thing on this island is a potential piece of the puzzle. It rewards curiosity enormously, and every building, every corner, every back alley has something in it worth investigating.

What you do carry between loops is your knowledge — and anything you've locked in using Residuum, which is essentially a resource you collect to preserve weapons, powers, and trinkets from one loop to the next. So while the world resets, your understanding of it grows, and your arsenal can grow with it if you're smart about how you manage things.

**If You Die, You Lose Everything**

![0126 (2)(5).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23y8oQoEjnCyfu38Lf66n37ycJyDVmX35U2s5PN6hCumf3VdXYF5ph3tvBijXZCjFxxJk.jpg)

And here is where the real pressure kicks in. DEATHLOOP has a system that's part roguelite, and it stings in the best possible way. You have two respawn chances within a single run before a third death fully loops you back to the beginning of the day. When you die and respawn, you drop your unspent Residuum, and if you don't get back to pick it up, it's gone. It's very similar to losing souls in Dark Souls — that sinking feeling of watching your resources hit the floor as you go down.

This creates a very real sense of tension, especially during moments when you're deep into a run, you've gathered a ton of Residuum, and Julianna decides that's the perfect moment to make her entrance. The stakes feel real. Losing progress hurts. And that actually makes every successful run feel incredibly satisfying. When you push through a tough district, secure your Residuum before dying, and walk out the other side with new gear locked in, there's a genuine sense of accomplishment that keeps you coming back for more.

**Expecting a Lot More**

![0126 (2)(2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tkjke9WwbiY4JcDrJ1c6UNcRpsTScu2hVPubjVfpjs9ApL7wfY7CV28JfZN8NNkjMik.jpg)

So far, DEATHLOOP has been a fascinating experience. It's not the kind of game you just zone out with for a few hours and call it a night. It demands attention, it demands patience, and it rewards both. The atmosphere of Blackreef is dark, stylish, and dripping with a retro 60s aesthetic that makes every district feel visually unique and full of personality. The shooting mechanics are smooth, the powers and abilities you collect feel genuinely fun to experiment with, and the moment-to-moment gameplay has this great energy to it whether you go in loud or try to sneak through like a ghost.

I still feel like I've barely scratched the surface of everything this island has to offer, and that's exciting. There's clearly a lot more to uncover, a lot more clues to find, and a lot more Julianna headaches in my future. But you know what? I'm here for all of it. So, gamers, I hope you enjoyed this first look at DEATHLOOP. I'll continue in a future post, and trust me, there's going to be a lot more to talk about. See you in the next one!
