body.title: Street Art #875 Legal Wall de Rouen October 2025, Montreal
body.body:
After exploring all the walls of **Garage Crémazie** (see the latest post on this topic: [StreetArt #874](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-874-grils-garage-cremazie-part-vi-montreal)), we return to the **Legal Wall de Rouen** in Montreal to see the latest versions from last year. Today's post is from my visit on October 9th. I need to hurry because I'll probably be able to pass by it again next Tuesday on my way to work by bike.

> *Après avoir exploré les différents murs du **Garage Crémazie** (voir le dernier à ce sujet : [StreetArt #874](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-874-grils-garage-cremazie-part-vi-montreal)), nous retournons au **Mur Légal de Rouen** à Montréal pour voir les dernières versions de l'année dernière. Aujourd'hui, il s'agit de mon passage du 9 octobre. Il faut que je me dépêche car sûrement que mardi prochain, je vais pouvoir enfin y repasser en allant au travail en vélo.*

![Macak & Hacer](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23w2cXTdUXBezqSh3wYSvvDRhTAHnvkaVP26TsDX8of2ihWBqaEUafP336b2zSejqWZrH.JPG)

# ෴ ᴡʜᴇʀᴇ
![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg)

The **Legal Wall de Rouen** is located on de Rouen street at railway level in Montreal's Hochelaga Maisonneuve district, a landmark for StreetArt in the city since 2010.

![Carte.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tHUsG817fcGd37AJb3MXNXkRwrTcRJf5GaAxihpYL3VGLQxuWxbEpwJX7TTXBZGjW5v.jpg)

> *Le **Mur Légal de Rouen** se trouve sur le rue de Rouen au niveau de la voie de chemin de fer dans le quartier Hochelaga Maisonneuve à Montréal, un lieu emblématique du StreetArt en ville depuis 2010.*

🗺️ Position on [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=18/45.53947/-73.55325)

[//]:# (!worldmappin 45.53926 lat -73.55250 long Legal Wall de Rouen 096 october 2025 d3scr)

# ෴ ᴡʜᴏ
![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg)

## Macak

![Macak](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23vhW1HV8uw91eoGFNv7SbQo4KWcSQBBaUQmEYZWaAfTquaWhLH5q5in7xzK4RWmWYVA4.JPG)

The viaduct begins with this artwork by [**Macak**](https://www.instagram.com/macak_mtl/), a regular here with his square letters and cartoon characters, today **Peanuts** featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy. It's always cool to see characters that marked our childhood before heading to the office 😀.

> *Le viaduc commence avec cette oeuvre de [**Macak**](https://www.instagram.com/macak_mtl/), un habitué des lieux avec ces lettres carrées et ses personnages de dessin-animé, aujourd'hui **Peanuts** avec Charlie Brown et Snoopy. Toujours cool le matin de croiser les personnages qui ont marqué notre enfance avant d'aller au bureau.*

![Macak](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23y8jQqS3obAxU6jUjMJKuSNJr1UuxTdVMqHVNN4iH6qVbDatR8q1rVDdZ3uxuZVJZRhx.JPG)

***

## Hacer

![Hacer](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23wWkeCnpUUswvBmQEQ4MQyMuj39ioPRz2PHrceBcNjwzZ4Tqq6bsEJQAdKMrJEiQU5jR.JPG)

Inside the **Rouen Legal Wall**, there's lettering by [**Hacer**](https://www.instagram.com/artgraffiti2023/), who also frequently appears on these walls. I don't know if the swamp monster is his work too. In any case, it's really well done.

> *A l'intérieur du **Mur Légal de Rouen**, il y au un lettrage de [**Hacer**](https://www.instagram.com/artgraffiti2023/), lui aussi souvent présent sur ces murs. Je ne sais pas si le monstre des marais est de sa main aussi. En tout cas, il est bien cool.*

![Hacer Hem](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23wByC7N2JehoxNFmrgi1sTNzDxsKb6XUCazSkrYp9SVkbsn7RouzYugSxWymHCrBmyVZ.JPG)

The monster is followed by lettering by an unknown artist... / **FR** : *Le monstre est suivi d'un lettrage d'un artiste inconnu...*

![DSC09743.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tvD1XqkS39QMVBqwV6Bt7T6Co35vK2exgaPPgFoSRQzBbLEx1ssUppR39ALf33Kn5kk.JPG)

***

## Aldarwin

![Aldarwin](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tvXqosfNUSQGuBMPTQNs9hZegtetyn13L8YoizJjN18w74HJCRBiXUUnpLKCDPyFdYs.JPG)

At the end of the first wall, we find [**Aldarwin**](https://www.instagram.com/aldarwin1/) with a new **bio-organic** monster, as he calls them. And under the watchful eye of **Mr Can Do It**, another unknown piece of lettering (WMD CAKS 🤔), surely a passing artist, as anyone has the right to paint here.

> *A la fin du premier mur, on retrouve [**Aldarwin**](https://www.instagram.com/aldarwin1/) avec un nouveau monstre **bio-organiques** comme il les appelle. Et sous l'oeil de **Mr Can Do It**, un autre lettrage inconnu (WMD CAKS 🤔), sûrement un artiste passage comme tout le monde a le droit de peindre ici.*

![Aldarwin](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tbRUjrHWj4e73ThS3GtVtnmAqgz8bXzPg4k1ixyvfQwZUN7FdeC5VRJ7qoqpHyBjmrw.JPG)

<div class=\

/> > WMD CAKS *** ## Kores & Fasi ![Kores & Fasi](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tkpMF5qJ3tTj8MBycEuT5ioNUQ4PYCUgUrp98J9oQAWoCmxGMTrHpN2N3D1mF3vW4UK.JPG) On the other side of Rue de Rouen, there's another swamp monster, this time the work of **Kores** and [**Fasi**](https://www.instagram.com/fasi785/), a real success with the contrast between the silver lettering and the swampy background. I really like it. **What about you?** > *De l'autre côté de la rue de Rouen, on retrouve un autre monstre des marais cette fois il est l'oeuvre de **Kores** et [**Fasi**](https://www.instagram.com/fasi785/), une réussite avec le contraste entre les lettres argentées et le fond ambiance marécage. J'aime beaucoup. **Et vous ?*** ![Kores & Fasi](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23wWnRqq1bZ7Y6Qpiw1np5PaLYCNQL3hexifDU6EbTDmieThSjEpheXVm2ec1eAhzve2n.JPG) Even more photos to admire the talent of these two artists / **FR** : *Encore plus de photos pour admirer le talent de ces deux artistes...*

/> ## Stack & ISOYA Rec ![Stack Soya Rec](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23vhny4bLpXKFeLY4w1wQKmvCp3gqmT3LFGrTusMd496gaUENiymFnYbwigiAmQptYUBm.JPG) We continue under the viaduct with lettering from [**Stack**](https://www.instagram.com/stack_moolah/) next to [**ISOYA Rec**](https://www.instagram.com/isoyarec/). Nice / **FR** : *On continue sous le viaduc avec un lettrage de [**Stack**](https://www.instagram.com/stack_moolah/) avec à côté [**ISOYA Rec**](https://www.instagram.com/isoyarec/). Sympa...* ## Syrup & Neoner ![Syrup & Neoner](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tkpMCugxJvMGsyfNo4S3awzJ7REVsgDdxfm8V7v54MLQfL1Fio89wh2jTWGcfQNr6F1.JPG) And that's why I really love this place. It's this kind of wall with a mix of styles created by different artists. There's [**Syrup**](https://www.instagram.com/gabsyrup/) with the crow, and below it, lettering by **Neoner**. I don't know if it's a collaboration or just an artist who respectfully added their work. The overall effect is very successful. > *Puis voilà pourquoi j'aime beaucoup ce lieu. C'est ce genre de mur avec un mélange de style fait par différents artistes. On a bien sûr [**Syrup**](https://www.instagram.com/gabsyrup/) avec ce corbeau et en dessous un lettrage de **Neoner**. Je ne sais pas si c'est une collaboration ou seulement un artiste qui a ajouté son travail avec respect. L'ensemble est très réussi.* ![Syrup & Neoner](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tvAwYRaTCRs2cZZXKAb1rfUW18zZFiH9PpMEKeDT6mZZ3FPkw3At4DVMnYMUc1BjXVz.JPG) # ෴ ᴡʜᴇɴ ![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg) * **2025**. ![line_grey.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSj2ThUhewrAjDZMFsx4UjSaXuS84cwHR2anDzyq9KWVh/line_grey.jpg)

/> **෴ ꜱᴏᴜʀᴄᴇꜱ** **Instagram** : [Macak](https://www.instagram.com/macak_mtl/) [Hacer](https://www.instagram.com/artgraffiti2023/) [Aldarwin](https://www.instagram.com/aldarwin1/) [Fasi](https://www.instagram.com/fasi785/) [Stack](https://www.instagram.com/stack_moolah/) [Syrup](https://www.instagram.com/gabsyrup/) **෴ ᴘʀᴇᴠɪᴏᴜꜱ ᴘᴏꜱᴛꜱ** [#874 **Grils** (Cremazie VI)(Cremazie V)](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-874-grils-garage-cremazie-part-vi-montreal)  **>** [Street Art Contest #295 **Amer**... body.title: Bad Weather coming
body.body:
In July and August there can sometimes be pretty bad thundestorms here in Austria and back last year in summer I took this picture of an upcoming thunderstorm when I was driving home from a customer. It really looked pretty bad but then it was only some heavy rain and a lot of wind. Fortunately no hailstorm just water. But If you get some really big hail from a storm like this it can be pretty dangerous. The wind was really heavy and driving home with the car was not really pleasant. But since I was outside on the land not in the city there was not place to hide from the thunderstorm and I had to look that I get home fast. It hit me but only with some really heavy rain, so I had to drive slow on the street since I couldn't see far. 

Another time when I drove with Stefan to the Lake Neusiedler we had a much worse thunderstorm in terms of hail and wind. 


![IMG_20250729_142529.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/florian-glechner/23wfr3r8uG7TCEPHh1zbY13S1W1t2WC9Ex4HM1MM5w4h91GETV9ds1r46jzTQM1sdzQGn.jpg)
*Picture of an upcoming thunderstorm. Picture: Florian Glechner.*

body.body: 1/5 🧵 Artemis II’s most dangerous moment is also the shortest: after a 10-day, 685,000-mile mission, the crew’s fate comes down to a 14-minute plunge through Earth’s atmosphere at nearly 25,000 mph. Space is hard. Coming home is harder.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The return profile is brutal. Orion is expected to re-enter around 7:53 p.m. ET and splash down near 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific, about 80 miles off San Diego. During descent, the capsule will hit roughly 23,864 mph, endure about 3.9 Gs, and face temperatures near 5,000°F. Inside, the crew gets a plasma fire show. Outside, the vehicle gets cooked.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The whole thing hinges on precision. If Orion comes in too steep, it can burn up. Too shallow, and it could miss the recovery zone—or in the nightmare scenario, skip off the atmosphere and get flung back into space. That’s why the mission spent the trip home making trajectory correction burns and checking systems obsessively. Re-entry is basically controlled violence with zero room for sloppiness.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The biggest engineering concern is the heat shield. Artemis I’s shield came back in 2022 with a nasty set of cracks and fractures, which raised obvious alarms. Lockheed Martin and NASA say the design was updated and cleared for crewed flight, but this is still the first real human test of that fix. If the shield works, Orion lives. If it doesn’t, nothing else matters.
body.author: askrafiki

body.title: PEOPLE CAN BE ANNOYING
body.body:
![images (1) (24).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/henrietta27/23w2oL6C7NRzNk2vJUsaXsL7ZW1nTzqFiboSLDaN9JPgk56tdb6NXUfninnLzokiW9uWK.jpeg)
[source](https://www.pexels.com/search/annoying/) 

Have you ever been in a situation where people just because they want to seem nice to other people end up doing things that disrupt your plans and schedule. I believe this is inevitable especially when you walk in an organization that they are different departments that needs to handle a particular thing before it gets approved. People also exhibit different types of character and some of these people do things out of the ordinary that are not even supposed to be.

So it was past our closing time and I stayed back because I had to submit some reports that were necessary to close the week. Other colleagues had gone home but this particular one was still around and he knows that based on protocol it was passed time to attend to any client. I had finished up and was trying to lock the office doors where he came with this person claiming that we should attend to him since he was already here this and that.

Based on the fact that I was still in the office I did not want to seem like a bad person but I made it clear to him that it is not right just because you know someone and wants to help the person does not mean you should jeopardize protocols. Because it doesn't seem fair, if I was not submitting report they would never have met me at that place. 

I just came here to rant about how annoying some people can be when you have a schedule planned and they just come up to mess it up.

Thanks for stopping by my blog.. 

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@henrietta27/people-can-be-annoying-d6o)

body.title: [ESP/ENG] Esmeralda 💚💎  Transformando el dolor en agradecimiento / Emerald 💚💎 Transforming Pain into Gratitude
body.body: > No se si seré la única en el mundo que hace esto, espero que no, pero cuando en mi vida pasan cosas traumaticas o fuertes, me refiero a ;una enfermedad, cárcel, o la muerte, busco la forma de hacer reflexión de eso, en parte me ayuda a mantenerme en el presente y encontrar un motivo por el cual seguir aprendiendo en esta vida, que es la única que tenemos, por cierto. > I don't know if I'm the only one in the world who does this, I hope not, but when traumatic or difficult things happen in my life—I mean, an illness, imprisonment, or death—I look for ways to reflect on them. It helps me stay in the present and find a reason to keep learning in this life, which is the only one we have, by the way. ![Presentación de Historia Museo Proyecto Álbum de Recortes Doodle Marrón.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaYJ32TwpTaUNoLZYiw29os2ciNEsuLUDvy1yVLCkkKhV/Presentaci%C3%B3n%20de%20Historia%20Museo%20Proyecto%20%C3%81lbum%20de%20Recortes%20Doodle%20Marr%C3%B3n.jpg) El día de ayer se murió una tía paterna, que en la niñez era muy cercana a mi, pero, circunstancias de la vida, debido al divorcio de mis papás. En los últimos años solo nos acercabamos por algún cumpleaños, inicio de año, o alguna fecha especial. Por lo que, eso me tiene reflexiva, no puedo hacer que el reloj gire contrario, y por eso anoche estaba nostálgica, porque si, hubiera querido hacer algo diferente, hubiera querido tener una mejor relación con ella, sin embargo, en vista de la situación, no es momento de arrepentimientos, sino de agradecimientos, y pues se que ella de alguna forma, sabe que agradezco lo mucho que hizo para que mi niñez fuera sana y feliz. > Yesterday, a paternal aunt passed away. She was very close to me when I was a child, but due to circumstances beyond my parents' control, we only saw each other for birthdays, New Year's, or other special occasions. So, that's what's made me reflective. I can't turn back time, and that's why I was feeling nostalgic last night. If I had wanted to do things differently, I would have wanted a better relationship with her. However, given the situation, this isn't a time for regrets, but for gratitude. And I know that she somehow knows how grateful I am for everything she did to make my childhood healthy and happy. ![IMG-20260408-WA0084.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVoydcHfD7DHjXmint3X5qtaM4Bq1JBxuLTnMwEGYuYBw/IMG-20260408-WA0084.jpg) Ahora ustedes preguntaran como lo supo, si nunca se lo dije, pues, el año pasado pude verla por unos minutos y aunque fueron solo unos pocos, hoy siento que, el universo conspiró para que ese momento generará en mi corazón sanidad. Además que, el hecho de que haya tenido tan buenas tías, tanto paternas como maternas, me ha hecho entender lo mucho que quiero ser yo una buena tía y estar presente en la vida de mis sobrinos. > Now you might ask how she knows, since I never told her. Well, last year I was able to see her for a few minutes, and even though it was only a few, today I feel that the universe conspired to bring healing to my heart in that moment. Also, having had such wonderful aunts, both on my father's and mother's side, has made me realize how much I want to be a good aunt myself and be present in my nephews' lives. ![IMG_20260410_132805.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZozVoUfJbAFA8szhwYWtRQAxsW9DCgPxb5bS5jE9XfVu/IMG_20260410_132805.jpg) Una forma de recordarla con gratitud es saber que todo lo que hizo por mi, lo hizo desde su amor de tía, esperando recibir absolutamente nada. Cada navidad, carnaval, semana santa, o fin de semana que pasamos juntas, fueron de los momentos más especiales de mi niñez, porque siempre tenía algo especial para hacer conmigo, bien sea, ir a la piscina, pasear a la perrita linda, conocer sitios nuevos, y generar en mi mente infantil recuerdos que jamás se borraran, que mantendré grabados con amor y bastante admiración. > One way to remember her with gratitude is to know that everything she did for me, she did out of her auntly love, expecting absolutely nothing in return. Every Christmas, Carnival, Easter, or weekend we spent together was one of the most special moments of my childhood, because she always had something special to do with me, whether it was going to the pool, walking her sweet little dog, exploring new places, and creating memories in my young mind that will never fade, memories I will cherish with love and admiration. ![IMG-20251221-WA0111.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTAPDgKV1K2mFBpYCPabKymmLsap56kSBc45CCPdUFswQ/IMG-20251221-WA0111.jpg) Por otro lado, ayer desde que la noticia llegó, a mi casa han llegado pajaritos, y es que, desde hace algún tiempo, vengo viéndolos en momentos donde sinceramente necesito saber que hay algo más importante, más grande, que une todo; la divinidad. Justo ahorita que estoy escribiendo, se paró uno casi detrás de mi, y esto me ha trae bastante paz y serenidad, algo que quisiera poder hacer llegar a todos mis familiares paternos en estos momentos tan difíciles, especialmente, a mi papá, y muy específicamente a mi tío Ramón, el esposo de mi tía. > On another note, since the news arrived yesterday, little birds have been coming to my house. For some time now, I've been seeing them in moments when I sincerely need to know that there is something more important, something greater, that unites everything: the divine. Just as I'm writing this, one landed almost behind me, and this has brought me a great deal of peace and serenity, something I wish I could share with all my paternal relatives during these difficult times, especially my father, and very specifically my Uncle Ramón, my aunt's husband. ![Screenshot_20260410_134057_com_hihonor_photos_GalleryMain.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWZN61RYaXLwpMvX6K3xH9pBtmz191xzbbu9yN8CM5SAV/Screenshot_20260410_134057_com_hihonor_photos_GalleryMain.jpg) ![Screenshot_20260410_134310.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeZACLbaYHcwU64mnQVoxgJYzsu242PwiewgUTPNpKwPi/Screenshot_20260410_134310.jpg) Aunque desde ayer al cerrar los ojos solo puedo ver la imagen de la última vez que nos vimos, y por eso les menciono sobre la paz que siento de haberlo vista esa última vez, guardo en mi corazón un lugar muy especial para ella, por eso mi entrada llevará su nombre. Un nombre que mi papá también quiso que yo llevara, como segundo nombre, toda mi vida lo he llevado con orgullo, porque sé el significado, y hoy especialmente se que es por ti. > Although since yesterday, when I close my eyes, all I can see is the image of the last time we met, and that's why I mention the peace I feel from having seen him that last time, I hold a very special place in my heart for her. That's why my entry will bear her name. A name that my father also wanted me to have, as a middle name. I've carried it with pride all my life because I know its meaning, and today especially I know it's because of you. ______ #holosandlotus Fotografía por | Photography by: @mairimmorales, HONOR MAGIC 7 LITE. Banner by | Banner por Photoroom. Collage by | Collage por Canva. Saludos amigos Hivers. . .


Queriendo reflejar reaismo en este paisaje, aplicando luz y sombra con precisión en cada espacio que conforman los elementos del boceto en blanco y negro. Con el lápiz con carbón, el cual es muy cremoso y oscuro fui delineando al inicio suavemente en laslíneas que iba trazando y progresivamente fui poniendo mas fuerza en la mano para dar mas tono y realce en los elementos que aparecen el el dibujo en blanco y negro.


Para realizar el boceto, use una referencia, lápiz con carbón, difumino, sacapuntas y dispositivo móvil para tomar las imagenes durante el proceso.



Proceso. . .





![pais1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRHmRndeoBDtjhQUbmX1rbRzVNH3z7B3FCfqnFyJ8mFdy/pais1.jpg)


![pais2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmToBvJconzCuWE8SsJ216ZNYtvWs7pEHo6YfFzYjC4Lhn/pais2.jpg)


![pais3.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmToBvJconzCuWE8SsJ216ZNYtvWs7pEHo6YfFzYjC4Lhn/pais3.jpg)


![pais8.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWAvBhvMoZ3vomQ5xruwNTyFB5SsPCtz4SxkQwvTsQ4JT/pais8.jpg)

En el dibujo se observan elementos naturales como elementos hechos por la mano del hombre. Se observa en la distancia como el sol se va ocultando y reflejamdo destellos de luz en las suaves olas del mar. También se observa a lo lejos una montaña, nubes, unas mas oscuras que otras en el cielo.

Se observa una casa antigua que en la altura hay una ventana abierta y el brillo de una luz que se refleja desde adentro de la habitación.


Espero que les guste mi contenido. Hasta pronto Dios mediante.

Esta mañana empezamos temprano en el hospital, como de costumbre, pasando visita con esa mezcla de rutina y compromiso que ya forma parte de nosotros. Pero el día tenía algo distinto: decidimos ir al hospital clínico quirúrgico para acompañar a los dos últimos residentes que rotaron con nosotros en su examen pre estatal.


Desde que llegamos, el ambiente se sentía cargado. El nerviosismo de ellos era evidente… y, siendo sincera, imposible no contagiarse un poco. Porque, ¿quién no ha estado en ese lugar? Viéndolos ahí, esperando, repasando mentalmente cada detalle, no pude evitar regresar a mis propios días de residencia, a esa mezcla de miedo, ilusión y ganas de hacerlo bien.


En medio de todo, Yessica y yo nos tomamos una foto. Y en ese instante, más que una simple imagen, fue como abrir una puerta a todos los recuerdos que hemos construido juntas desde que teníamos 18 años. Tantas guardias, tantas historias, tanto crecimiento… y ahí estábamos, todavía compartiendo momentos importantes.


También fue bonito reencontrarme con algunos de mis profesores. Esas caras conocidas que, de alguna forma, siempre traen calma y orgullo. Aunque no te voy a mentir, ver a nuevos residentes que aún no han rotado con nosotros me hizo sentir un poquito fuera de lugar, como si por un momento ya no perteneciera del todo a ese escenario que fue tan mío.


Pero al final, todo valió la pena.


Los muchachos lo hicieron excelente. De verdad, se lucieron. Verlos salir con buenos resultados, con esa mezcla de alivio y felicidad en la cara, fue una satisfacción enorme. Sentí orgullo, como si una pequeña parte de su camino también fuera nuestra.


Y mientras regresaba, pensé en lo bonito que es cerrar ciclos… pero también en lo necesario que es estar presentes en los de otros.


Ahora solo les queda el último paso el mes que viene. Y sé que lo van a lograr. Porque si algo quedó claro hoy, es que están listos… y que todo ese esfuerzo, todas esas noches largas y días intensos, ya están dando frutos.


Y uno, desde este lado, solo puede sonreír… y recordar que, en el fondo, nunca dejamos de ser un poquito residentes también.



# English Version 




This morning we started early at the hospital, as usual, doing rounds with that mix of routine and commitment that’s already part of who we are. But today felt different: we decided to go to the clinical-surgical hospital to be present at the pre-state exam of the last two residents who rotated with us.


From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere felt tense. Their nervousness was obvious… and honestly, impossible not to feel it too. Because who hasn’t been in that place? Watching them there, waiting, mentally reviewing every detail, I couldn’t help but go back to my own residency days—to that mix of fear, excitement, and the desire to do well.


In the middle of it all, Yessica and I took a photo. And in that moment, it felt like more than just a picture—it was like opening a door to all the memories we’ve built together since we were 18. So many shifts, so many stories, so much growth… and there we were, still sharing important moments.


It was also so nice to see some of my former professors again. Those familiar faces that somehow always bring a sense of calm and pride. Although, I won’t lie, seeing new residents who haven’t rotated with us yet made me feel a little out of place, like for a moment I no longer fully belonged to that world that once felt so much like mine.


But in the end, it was all worth it.
They did amazing. Truly. Seeing them come out with great results, with that mix of relief and happiness on their faces, was incredibly rewarding. I felt proud, as if a small part of their journey was also ours.
And on the way back, I found myself thinking about how beautiful it is to close chapters… but also how important it is to be present for others as they go through theirs.


Now they only have one final step left next month. And I know they’ll make it. Because if today proved anything, it’s that they’re ready… and that all those long nights and intense days are already paying off.


And from this side, all you can do is smile… and remember that, deep down, we never really stop being residents.

body.title: Change Yourself, Change Your Life
body.body: /> Change Yourself, Change Your Life --------------------------------- Life does not change by chance—it changes when you decide to change yourself. The way you think, act, and respond to situations shapes your future. If you want a better life, the first step is to improve yourself from within. ### 1\. Take Responsibility for Your Life The moment you stop blaming others and take responsibility, your life begins to change. Accept your mistakes, learn from them, and focus on what you can control. This mindset gives you the power to grow. ### 2\. Change Your Thinking Your thoughts create your reality. Replace negative thinking with positive and productive thoughts. Instead of saying “I can’t,” start saying “I will try.” A strong mindset helps you overcome challenges and move forward. ### 3\. Build Good Habits Success is built on daily habits. Start small—wake up early, exercise regularly, read books, and manage your time wisely. These simple habits, when practiced consistently, lead to big improvements in your life. ### 4\. Step Out of Your Comfort Zone Growth happens when you face challenges. Don’t be afraid to try new things or take risks. Every new experience teaches you something valuable and makes you stronger.

/>

### 5\. Surround Yourself with Positive People

The people around you influence your thoughts and actions. Stay close to those who support, motivate, and inspire you. Positive company helps you stay focused on your goals.

### 6\. Stay Consistent and Patient

Change takes time. You may not see results immediately, but consistency is the key. Keep working on yourself every day, and slowly you will notice a difference in your life.

### 7\. Believe in Yourself

Self-belief is the foundation of success. Trust your abilities and never give up, even when things get difficult. When you believe in yourself, you unlock your true potential.

### Conclusion

If you want to change your life, start by changing yourself. Your habits, mindset, and actions determine your future. Take small steps every day, stay positive, and keep moving forward. One day, you will look back and realize how far you’ve come.

body.title: SURVIVING A WAR
body.body: We do not pray for wars but when they come, what can we truly do? The fact that during world war two, a lot of innocent lives were lost, and even during the recent wars that have been going on, a lot of innocent people have died not because they were fighting, but because they were at the wrong place at the wrong time. Some of them were even in their homes when death came knocking at the door, which shows just how terrifying wars can be. You can never tell where the next explosion will happen and you can never tell how it will even happen. People were going about their normal daily activities when the atomic bomb went off during world war two, kids were in school, and parents were either at home or in their offices when they suddenly stopped breathing.\n\n

/> Photo by [Levi Meir Clancy](https://unsplash.com/@levimeirclancy?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/grayscale-photo-of-concrete-houses-LheHIV3XpGM?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) This is how bad it can be and why I will never pray for war. If I ever find myself in a war area, the first thing will be to leave. If my family is there, we are living the moment I hear the war begins. I do not want to stay to see what happens, I do not care about who wins or loses, I just want my family safe and sound. I believe that the lives of my family and myself is way more important than anything or any protection the world has to offer. I do not want to be a victim of circumstances and mistakes of a government who cares more about power than the lives of its citizens. I do not want me or my family to be a pawn in other people’s war so I will not fight in a war that doesn’t make sense. The only time I will consider fighting for my country is if we are being oppressed, then I know I am fighting for something and whether I live or die, I did it for something that is worth it.

/> I am not afraid to die, I do not just want to do it over something as clumsy as a 100 year grudge between countries. I do not want to continue a streak of fighting and deaths because I believe that if those in government who are setting up the war can not send their kids to the war front, then I should not be there. If they can’t be at the war front themself, then so should I. I believe in justice and not mediocracy. This is the reason why I need to work hard to make sure if something like this ever occurs, finance will never be an issue why we can not leave. But then again, I will prefer if there is no war at all, I will prefer if countries never had to fight, if no one ever held a grudge that could lead to a global or civil war. body.title: Jeong-beom Son: the new Son?
body.body: Mientras Son Heung-min brilla en la MLS con Loa Angeles FC, en Seúl ha surgido otro “Son” que ilusiona a toda Corea del Sur. Jeong-beom Son, atacante de 19 años formado en la cantera de FC Seoul y regresado de la Osan High School, se ha convertido en uno de los nombres propios de la K League 1 2026. Con apenas unas jornadas disputadas, un total de 5 hasta ahora, el joven extremo ya es un elemento importante para el técnico Kim Gi-dong. Su velocidad, desborde y capacidad goleadora han sido clave en el arranque invicto de los capitalinos, que lideran la tabla y aspiran a romper una sequía de diez años sin título. De momento un gol y una asistencia suma en este inicio de curso. Nacido en 2007, Son debutó profesionalmente esta temporada y ya acumula minutos decisivos. Su similitud de apellido y posición con el capitán de la selección nacional ha disparado las comparaciones, aunque el propio jugador mantiene los pies en la tierra: “Solo quiero ayudar al equipo a ganar”. Para FC Seoul y para la selección sub-20, Jeong-beom Son representa el futuro inmediato del fútbol coreano. ![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXkjgqGhLhqQV4ih8eB5dZzqKD91xfUYeQmUgkoPptV16/1000231433.webp) While Son Heung-min shines in MLS with Los Angeles FC, another “Son” has emerged in Seoul, exciting all of South Korea. Jeong-beom Son, a 19-year-old forward who came up through the FC Seoul youth system and returned from Osan High School, has become one of the standout names in the 2026 K League 1. With just a few matches played—five so far—the young winger is already a key player for coach Kim Gi-dong. His speed, dribbling ability, and scoring prowess have been crucial to the capital club’s undefeated start; they currently lead the table and aim to end a ten-year title drought. So far this season, he has one goal and one assist to his credit. Born in 2007, Son made his professional debut this season and is already racking up crucial minutes. The similarity of his last name and position to the national team captain has sparked comparisons, though the player himself remains grounded: “I just want to help the team win.” For FC Seoul and the U-20 national team, Jeong-beom Son represents the immediate future of Korean soccer. body.title: Are Man's Thoughts Or Abilities Limited Before God?//The Old Path.
body.body:
https://youtu.be/yareRqkUYlU?si=BQqVpg6NsBGMY9HR

The natural condition of our being made us to understand that every part of our being has its limit. Human thoughts and abilities are limited in the sight of God, no human wisdom can compete with God's wisdom and no strength or power on earth can prevail without God's sustaining power. God is the beginning and the end, he knows everything about us even before we were born.

The book of **Jeremiah 10:23** made us to understand that the way of man is not in himself, and it's not the man that walket to direct his steps. This means that God is the only one who can direct our steps, so we are not free to think whatever we want to think. Our thoughts and thinking must be regulated by God's wisdom and word. 

So as christians, recognizing human limitations draws our heart closer to God. We should be humble and submissive to God always trusting in his guidance and protection because while man is limited, God is unlimited and his wisdom is infinite.

body.body: 1/5 🧵 The wild part isn’t just the ransom demand — it’s the suggestion that Nancy Guthrie’s family should actually pay **half a bitcoin** just to create a traceable breadcrumb. That’s the core idea here: not paying to solve the case, but paying to see whether the person demanding crypto can be exposed by what they do next. Brutal logic, expensive gamble.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The article centers on former FBI agent Jennifer Coffindaffer’s argument. Her view: send **0.5 BTC** of the **1 BTC** being demanded and watch the movement. If the sender touches it, converts it, or routes it through exchanges or currency off-ramps, investigators may get a fresh lead. In plain English: use the ransom wallet like bait and see who bites.
body.author: askrafiki

body.author: iscrak

body.body: 3/5 🧵 Why she thinks it matters: the case has apparently gone cold. Nancy Guthrie, 84, was abducted from her Tucson home on **Feb. 1**, and the piece says investigators still haven’t produced suspects or meaningful new leads. In that vacuum, even a risky “last breadcrumb” starts to look attractive. That’s the article’s tension: desperate cases make ugly options sound reasonable.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The notes themselves make it uglier. The same anonymous sender reportedly sent multiple messages, including two new ones to TMZ. One claimed Nancy was dead but still offered to hand over the kidnappers on a “silver platter.” Another claimed she was seen alive in **Sonora, Mexico**. That contradiction is the point: the sender may be lying, taunting, profiteering, or all three. Either way, they’re trying to monetize a family’s hell.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 My read: Coffindaffer’s idea is clever, but it’s still a nasty bet. Crypto is traceable in some contexts, sure — but it’s not magic, and paying extortionists can reward the circus. Still, if law enforcement has nothing solid, I get why “buy one breadcrumb” becomes tempting. The article is really about desperation more than bitcoin. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/04/10/us-news/ex-fbi-suggests-costly-way-to-finally-crack-nancy-guthries-kidnapping-case/)

Bajo la Sombra del Leander: Siete Kilómetros de Complicidad


​Caracas ha sido, durante esta última semana, una caldera de asfalto. El calor se ha vuelto un vecino insoportable que no da tregua ni siquiera cuando el sol se oculta tras el Ávila. Sin embargo, hay compromisos que no se negocian, y el entrenamiento de running es uno de ellos. Pero esta no era una jornada cualquiera; era una salida especial al Parque del Este, un lugar que de noche adquiere una mística serena, transformándose en un oasis necesario para el espíritu.
​No iba sola. Me acompañaba una de mis personas favoritas en el mundo: mi hija. Aunque ya cuenta con 15 años y está forjando su propio camino, para mí sigue siendo \

, esa compañera de vida que aceptó el reto de calzarse las zapatillas y ver cuánto podíamos aguantar juntas bajo el sofocante sereno de la noche caraqueña.
​El entrenamiento comenzó con buen pie. Yo, con un poco más de kilómetros acumulados en las piernas y algo más de experiencia, buscaba mantener la consistencia. El aire era denso y pesado, casi se podía sentir la humedad en cada inhalación, pero avanzar al lado de ella hacía que el esfuerzo se sintiera compartido y, por ende, más ligero. Nos movíamos entre las sombras de los árboles y las luces tenues del parque, con el majestuoso Barco Leander custodiando nuestro recorrido desde el lago.
​Hubo un momento de conexión profunda mientras pasábamos frente a la réplica del navío. Recordé que el barco lleva ese nombre en honor al primer hijo de Francisco de Miranda; un gesto histórico de un padre hacia su descendencia que resonaba perfectamente con lo que yo estaba viviendo en ese instante. Allí estaba yo, corriendo junto a mi primogénita, uniendo pasado, presente y futuro en cada zancada.
​Sin embargo, el calor nocturno no perdona. Al alcanzar la marca de los 7 kilómetros, manteniendo ese ritmo constante de 7 minutos por kilómetro, el agotamiento físico llegó a su límite. Mi hija, con la honestidad de quien lo ha dado todo, me miró y me dijo: \

. En ese momento, el cronómetro dejó de ser importante. Lo que importaba era que habíamos cumplido la misión.
​Terminamos sofocadas, con la ropa empapada y el corazón acelerado, pero con una satisfacción que no se puede medir en aplicaciones de running. Estos kilómetros no fueron solo para fortalecer los músculos o mejorar la resistencia cardiovascular; fueron para fortalecer esos lazos inquebrantables entre madre e hija. El Parque del Este fue el escenario de una pequeña victoria personal: logramos nuestros 7 km, vencimos al clima y, sobre todo, atesoramos un momento que, al igual que el nombre del Leander, quedará grabado como un tributo al amor que nos une.

English Version 

Under the Shadow of the Leander: Seven Kilometers of Complicity

​Caracas has been, during this last week, an asphalt boiler. The heat has become an unbearable neighbor that gives no respite even when the sun goes down behind the... However, there are commitments that are not negotiated, and running training is one of them. But this was not just any day; it was a special outing to the Parque del Este, a place that acquires a serene mystique at night, transforming into a necessary oasis for the spirit.
​I wasn't going alone. I was accompanied by one of my favorite people in the world: my daughter. Although she is already 15 years old and is forging her own path, for me she is still \

, that life partner who accepted the challenge of putting on her sneakers and seeing how much we could endure together under the suffocating serene of the Caracas night.
​The training started off on a good foot. I, with a little more kilometers accumulated in my legs and some more experience, was looking to maintain consistency. The air was dense and heavy, you could almost feel the humidity in each inhalation, but moving next to her made the effort feel shared and, therefore, lighter. We were moving between the shadows of the trees and the dim lights of the park, with the majestic Leander Boat guarding our route from the lake.
​There was a moment of deep connection as we passed in front of the replica of the ship. I remembered that the ship is named after Francisco de Miranda's first son; a historic gesture of a father towards his offspring that perfectly resonated with what I was living at that moment. There I was, running next to my firstborn, uniting past, present and future in every stride.
​However, the night heat does not forgive. Upon reaching the 7 kilometer mark, maintaining that constant pace of 7 minutes per kilometer, physical exhaustion reached its limit. My daughter, with the honesty of one who has given everything, looked at me and said, \

At that moment, the stopwatch ceased to be important. What mattered was that we had accomplished the mission.
​We ended up suffocated, with soaked clothes and a racing heart, but with a satisfaction that cannot be measured in running applications. These kilometers were not just to strengthen muscles or improve cardiovascular endurance; they were to strengthen those unbreakable bonds between mother and daughter. The Parque del Este was the scene of a small personal victory: we achieved our 7 km, we beat the weather and, above all, we treasured a moment that, like the name of the Leander, will be recorded as a tribute to the love that unites us.

A sparrow perched on an antenna in the afternoon was captured by my camera; even though it was aware of the camera, it didn’t seem to care. It was enjoying the afternoon atmosphere, basking in the warmth of the setting sun while flapping its wings to shake off the fine dust clinging to its feathers, its feet perched casually on the wire. After finishing cleaning its tiny body, it continued chirping while looking to the right, to the left, and down, as if assessing the situation. Its behavior was so adorable until it was content to stay up there. This portrait of my little friend, this sparrow things became my entry for [PhotoFeed Contest](https://ecency.com/hive-153349/@photofeed/photofeed-contest-wildlife-photography-round-165) by @photofeed

body.body: @luchyl basically yes, but not only nature. Classic landscape photography is rooted in natural scenery, but the genre is really about capturing a place or environment, which is why **urban landscape** is a recognized branch of it too ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landscape_photography), Adobe). So if the frame is mainly about the setting—the road, skyline, river, buildings, atmosphere—it can still count as landscape even with little or no wild nature; your city-focused shots already lean that way in practice [here](https://inleo.io/@luchyl/sweet-treats-on-wheels-photofeed-con...%20%5Btruncated%5D). The cleaner distinction is this: nature-heavy scene = traditional landscape, built-environment scene = urban landscape, person-led moment = street or environmental photography.

body.title: [ENG-SPN] Mudéjar: Beauty, Efficiency, and Medieval Fantasy / El Mudéjar: Belleza, Ahorro y Fantasía Medieval
body.body:
![IMG_4871.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Eos1kCvfXRzZjCz9z6PmdKCSyPhvfHqf6tPuSfvrjtXNsyG8jiFcmFzFBdm5B5Qkshe.JPG)

Not far from Uceda and its inevitably lost Romanesque jewel, the small village of El Cubillo de Uceda surprises us once again with an architectural treasure. While not as highly valued as the Romanesque style, it possesses its own unique beauty and harmonious charm: Mudéjar.

![IMG_4874.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/23tSd7jhnSHEocdWmveYBWDCFEiemk6CbzD1QyvaHjhm1wedSpZ1ZkPWqVT8GDgGUxnMY.JPG)

We are, of course, referring to the Church of Saint Michael, presumably built by Muslim master builders who remained in the area after its reconquest and repopulation. They contributed that touch of Eastern subtlety characteristic of a different approach to architecture, one that also introduced a modern concept resulting in cost reduction.

![IMG_4875.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EocAUxx2ztBuq3HhM5yANdGtQFUB1nGEqSh8kunSdsGurrRT6jEJHGRAQzJf6uyLpt2.JPG)

Indeed, contrary to the high cost of extracting large blocks of stone from the quarries and their subsequent transport, the use of lighter materials, such as brick, represented an innovation and a reduction in costs, as we have mentioned. In many places in Castile—we are leaving aside Aragon, where this style triumphed, increasing the artistic and cultural value of numerous towns and cities—it led to its adoption. Sometimes, as demonstrated in the church of Saint Michael de Olmedo, it coexisted with the Romanesque style, achieving, in cases like these, curious combinations, certainly not lacking in creativity and imagination. This church in El Cubillo de Uceda is one of the most remarkable examples of this style in Guadalajara.

![IMG_4877.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Epfohe7qfh5pKvJDdPEtqTo6MaxbxPGVVQitxLKvpa5EcpAZiegd8wzgX3ppWDXUAjK.JPG)

No muy lejos de Uceda y su joya románica inevitablemente perdida, el pequeño pueblo de El Cubillo de Uceda vuelve a sorprendernos con un tesoro arquitectónico, que, aunque no tan valorado como el románico, no deja de tener también su propia belleza, no exenta, en absoluto, de armónico encanto: el Mudéjar.

![IMG_4891.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Eo6PhySEfGGiSkRPaxGgXvpg7qQ6ziYjaSZYcHmNLyYcMdRiyKrZyKWVDY76WxJAkbD.JPG)

Hablamos, por supuesto, de la iglesia de San Miguel, levantada, presumiblemente, por alarifes musulmanes que permanecieron en el lugar después de que éste fuera reconquistado y repoblado, aportando ese toque de sutileza oriental que caracteriza a una forma de concebir la arquitectura desde otra perspectiva y donde se podría añadir que introdujo, además, un concepto moderno derivado en el abaratamiento de costes.

![IMG_4893.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/Eo6PixjxFmZxX2CmsuQ2kRbW8cQfTRQMdaGs4JzkWa6b2yYXAH8rRk61bKDCuMwtPts.JPG)

En efecto, contrariamente a lo costoso que resultaba extraer de las canteras los grandes bloques de piedra y su consiguiente trasladado, la utilización de materiales más ligeros, como el ladrillo, supuso una innovación y un abaratamiento de costes, como hemos dicho, que, en el caso de muchos lugares de Castilla –dejamos aparte Aragón, donde este estilo triunfó, aumentando el valor artístico y cultural de numerosos pueblos y ciudades- supuso una adopción, que, en ocasiones, como se demuestra también en la iglesia de San Miguel de Olmedo, convivio con el románico, logrando, en casos como estos, curiosas combinaciones, no exentas, en absoluto de creatividad y fantasía, siendo, precisamente esta iglesia de El Cubillo de Uceda, uno de los ejemplos más notables de este estilo en Guadalajara.

![IMG_4903.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EqUdPfnbDhZhm26juG3ssnJ6yj4Fx6GrCEfiFaWFXrrm2GiqPkVWnrUkXPcYpfZV2kZ.JPG)

body.body:
>Apologies for any sloppiness, no time to proofread properly.

Due to regular life stuff, I missed the [NY Times article](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/08/business/bitcoin-satoshi-nakamoto-identity-adam-back.html) about researching Satoshi's ID. That's actually good because by the time I read it there had already been a couple of days for people to react, and yawn. 

I admit, the \
question intrigues me and I'm a sucker for each \
. The NY Times one did lead me to a question I'd like to ask, maybe someone could offer thoughts.\n\n**Is this [2015 \
post](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/6EC9DDF352DC4838AE9B088AB372428A25E1F42A@DS04/)? really from Satoshi?** I thought I was fairly up on Satoshi's writings (I put together \
) and a 2015 post certainly was not on my radar. I know the \

post on Bitcoin Talk is questionable as to its authenticity. I assume this post has the same question marks, maybe more. I will say that when I read it, it does not read with the same voice as other Satoshi writings. 

But, anyone have any thoughts on this?

#### Some other thoughts

Aside from that question, I'll share some rather random thoughts that occurred after reading it.

I was reminded of couple of psych 101 concepts while reading the NY Times piece: confirmation bias and heuristics. The writer is connecting dots in the work. Yes, he builds a case, but it looks like he's trying to build the case. Like an D.A. who has a hunch as to who did it, the prosecutor goes about gathering evidence that the guy is guilty and builds a case. But, he's arranging the dots that align into the picture. It read as though the picture was not arranging itself. Confirmation bias suggests that when a dot, a piece of information suggested it was Adam Back, that info was included. But, anything suggesting otherwise is simply ignore...it must be wrong. When we look for evidence and then find some that backs up what we think, we take it to heart, all while disregarding evidence to the contrary which may have just as much merit. 

And, heuristics. The author is not going to create shock waves pointing to Adam Back (or Nick Szabo). That's like saying, \

There are definitely things about Back that could be lined up as dots to suggest he's Satoshi (same with Szabo). And yet, I'm reminded of the psycho 101 heuristics.\n\nAvailability heuristics says we make a decision based on the ease of gaining information, particularly info that confirms our bias. There's a lot of info on Adam Back and it's rather easy to gather a lot via the internet. The author of the article actually interviewed Back on a couple of occasions. Back is \

and I give him credit for talking and doing interviews and whatnot. He's available; his dots are there to be connected. By contrast, what if Satoshi was exactly what he says: someone in hiding, nameless, a no-name, someone you'd never heard of before (unlike Back or Szabo). How available would that person's info be? Then, how could be compare person X's writings and thoughts to Satoshi's public writings and thoughts? The availability heuristic suggests that human nature is to take what is easily available, run it through our confirmation bias, and then accept that as true.

Also, I think the representative heuristic might be at play here. It has to do with numbers, probabilities. I'm reminded of a mental exercise from David Myers' textbook on cognition that went like this: 

>A person is short, slim, and likes to read poetry. Is this person most likely an Ivy League university professor of classics who enjoys poetry or a truck driver?
>
>It's immediately tempting to think Ivy League professor. We stereotypically picture a small, nerdy bookworm of a fellow. But, in terms of numbers, there might only be 40 Ivy League classics professors, half are slim, half of them like poetry. So, only 10. But, the mental exercise figures there are 400,000 truck drivers. Only 1/8 are slim, but that's 50,000. And only 1 in 100 like poetry, so that's 500. So, the odds are that the short, slim poetry lover is a truck driver.

Regarding Satoshi, the investigators typically start with the usual suspects then start dwindling from there. The NY Times and the NY Mag author below started with a spreadsheet of 100. They started with the usual suspect then began narrowing. I think anyone involved in an investigation will tell you that if you show five or six suspects to a witness, the witness will pick the one they think fits. But, they neglect to \

someone who is NOT in the lineup...which could be thousands or millions of people. 

In this case, we have 100 usual suspects, 100 short, slim Ivy League classics professors. What if Satoshi was from the other group, he's not in the lineup of usual suspects? Let's do some representative heuristics and cast a wide net. There are 8 billion other truck drivers out there. Let's start whittling down...

Required qualifiers/disqualifiers (traits we know Satoshi had): 
- trained in C 
- \

leading up to October 2008

Supposed traits (but not absolutes):
- had cypherpunk or libertarian leanings? 
- had some academic training
- had an understanding of economics
- at least age 50 now (due to double spacing after sentences and Hungarian notation in coding)
- fluent English with both British and American usage
- calm, polite, \

\n\nA comment to the NY Times article referenced [this article from 2025](https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/bitcoin-satoshi-nakamoto-benjamin-wallace-book-excerpt.html). It raised something I'd never heard of: Hungarian notation in coding. I had to look it up -- it's a way of naming variables that was used in the 1980s and 90s. This meshes well with the double spacing after sentences trait. It suggests to me that Satoshi is about the age that Adam Back is (55). In [\

](https://crrdlx.vercel.app/kicking/), I guessed he was born around 1968 (which would make him 57 or 58 today). Personally, I think there's something to this double space and Hungarian coding angle. It's like trying to speak without your native accent, you can't do it.\n\nI realize it's uncool to share \

, but I don't care, I 'm not cool. I used the short Ivy League professor vs. truck driver method to whittle down numbers of possible Satoshis.\n\nIt got the list down to ~800 possible Satoshis. 40 were \

and likely on the 100 list on the spreadsheet, so, ~760 possible Satoshis we've never heard of. See the chart.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/crrdlx/23t8B2n4CJiw6jDbzMEGZ186BX9vymxVR4k4npmsVvxXMzsCGza7WRQirHCvDzdHBNDAQ.png

A second opinion AI using the same prompts came down to 5,000 possible Satoshis. It estimated that of the 5,000, it wondered how many would be \

that is, they wrote enough or talked enough about this type of thing for a researcher to find them digging around on the internet. Interestingly, the number they came up with was about 100 - exactly the number on each of these two spreadsheets to start out (while neglecting the unseen larger number of possible Satoshis).\n\nSummed, I think it's very possible, maybe even probable, that Satoshi is someone we've never heard of. In a way, naming one of the people that is on \

is actually kind of safe. Can you imagine a reporter picking Bill Jones who lives two houses down the street and putting out an expose saying as much in the NY Times? Can you imagine the legal backlash that would come at the Times for putting that person in the spotlight and possible danger? This kind of happened already with Dorian Satoshi Nakamoto, right?

One more thing that intrigued me regarding all this is [Jameson Lopp's tweet](https://x.com/lopp/status/2042192286281298112?s=20). I don't know if he knows something no one else knows, but it is interesting how he says...if you know, you know to not tell.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/crrdlx/23tSz3RGag8bPWkGCmiEqMauspni1sbPGAPyTqogZVAbk5TwUyMBC2TiTPRstUnj9vBhe.png

First, Lopp has the God-given IQ, technical skill, research skill (I think his work [is strong suggesting Hal Finney was not Satoshi](https://blog.lopp.net/hal-finney-was-not-satoshi-nakamoto/)) -- seems \

as he puts it to perhaps have an Easter egg. I wondered, why would you not tell if you knew or had a strong clue that others might use? I see three options: (a) the safety issue, (b) legal issues, and (c) it'd wreck bitcoin. The safety issue seems straightforward: ID Satoshi and he/she or family is in jeopardy from thieves. This fits with Lopp's security expertise. The possibility of wrecking bitcoin is Satoshi's ID leaks is juicier. How could this info wreck BTC?

- Revealing Satoshi might wreck bitcoin by undercutting the mystery and ethos of Satoshi. By putting a human face on Satoshi, warts and all, the mystery is gone and he's off the pedestal. It's like what they say about meeting your hero. Frankly, I don't put much toward this. Maybe for a short period it could impact bitcoin if, say, if Satoshi was now a street drunkard, but in the long run, bitcoin don't care. Bitcoin gonna bitcoin.
- Revealing Satoshi might have legal implications not only for Satoshi but for the leaker. If a jurisdiction found out about that much money being \

and if you were holding information that helped keep that money hidden...well, I don't know. I'm no lawyer, so I don't know. But, that much money brings attention. \n- Revealing Satoshi might prompt him to do something drastic with his million-ish coins. What if Satoshi said, \

This fits with the safety idea. Along these lines, Lopp actually recent posted a prayer asking Satoshi to please publicly burn (not airdrop) his coins. Publicly owning that many coins would be like walking through the worst part of any city at night flaunting your Rolex watch. It won't go well. 

. lopp's idea - if you know, you know why you keep quiet (he has the raw IQ and tech ability; why shouldn't? wreck bitcoin (Satoshi might flood his stash in market, might be an idiot/criminal), safety, other?
. personality types: humble/quiet, ego/brash, nerdy/recluse/conspiracy theorist, 
. I think AI has as good of a chance as any to crack the case...it can quickly scan lots of evidence, metadata, timestamps to either qualify or disqualify people (like Lopp did with Hal)

body.title: Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)
body.body:
# Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)

![zig-banner.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

### What will I learn
- You will learn how `build.zig` replaces Makefiles, CMake, and other build configuration;
- the `std.Build` API for declaring executables, libraries, and test targets;
- build options: debug vs release, target triples, optimization levels;
- adding dependencies and linking C libraries from the build script;
- custom build steps for code generation and asset processing;
- the `zig fetch` and `build.zig.zon` package management system;
- conditional compilation and build-time configuration via options;
- organizing multi-binary projects with shared libraries.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

### Difficulty
- Intermediate

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Zig Series`):
- [Zig Programming Tutorial - ep001 - Intro](https://hive.blog/programming/@scipio/zig-programming-tutoroial-ep001-intro)
- [Learn Zig Series (#2) - Hello Zig, Variables and Types](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-2-hello-zig-variables-and-types)
- [Learn Zig Series (#3) - Functions and Control Flow](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-3-functions-and-control-flow)
- [Learn Zig Series (#4) - Error Handling (Zig's Best Feature)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature)
- [Learn Zig Series (#5) - Arrays, Slices, and Strings](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-5-arrays-slices-and-strings)
- [Learn Zig Series (#6) - Structs, Enums, and Tagged Unions](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions)
- [Learn Zig Series (#7) - Memory Management and Allocators](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators)
- [Learn Zig Series (#8) - Pointers and Memory Layout](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-8-pointers-and-memory-layout)
- [Learn Zig Series (#9) - Comptime (Zig's Superpower)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-9-comptime-zigs-superpower)
- [Learn Zig Series (#10) - Project Structure, Modules, and File I/O](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io)
- [Learn Zig Series (#11) - Mini Project: Building a Step Sequencer](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-11-mini-project-building-a-step-sequencer)
- [Learn Zig Series (#12) - Testing and Test-Driven Development](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-12-testing-and-test-driven-development)
- [Learn Zig Series (#13) - Interfaces via Type Erasure](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-13-interfaces-via-type-erasure)
- [Learn Zig Series (#14) - Generics with Comptime Parameters](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-14-generics-with-comptime-parameters)
- [Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig) (this post)

# Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)

Welcome back! In [episode #14](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-14-generics-with-comptime-parameters) we explored Zig's generics system -- which is really just comptime parameters in disguise. We built generic functions with `comptime T: type`, returned types from functions to create generic data structures like `Stack(i32)`, inspected types at compile time with `@typeInfo` and `@hasDecl`, combined multiple comptime parameters in `FixedRing(T, capacity)`, and saw how `anytype` provides lightweight polymorphism. That covered the compile-time side of Zig's abstraction story. Combined with the runtime type erasure from [ep013](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-13-interfaces-via-type-erasure), you now have both tools for writing polymorphic code.

But there's one piece of the puzzle we've been ignoring this entire series. Every single program we've compiled used `zig build` or `zig test` -- and those commands read a file called `build.zig` that we never wrote ourselves. We either ran `zig init` and used whatever it generated, or compiled single files with `zig build-exe`. Well, that changes now. Because once your project has more than one source file, once you need to link a C library, once you want to produce both a debug and release binary, or once you pull in a third-party package -- you need to understand `build.zig`. And the good news is that `build.zig` is not a config file in some DSL. It's Zig code. Real Zig code, using the same language you already know, with conditionals and loops and error handling and all the rest.

Here we go!

## Solutions to Episode 14 Exercises

Before we get into the build system, here are the solutions to last episode's exercises on generics. All code is complete and compilable -- copy, paste, `zig test`, done.

**Exercise 1** -- Generic `MinHeap(T)`:

```zig
const std = @import(\

. You give it a name, a root source file (the entry point), the target platform, and optimization level. This returns a `*Compile` step -- a node in the build graph. It doesn't compile anything yet. It just registers the intent.\n\n`b.installArtifact(exe)` says \

(`zig-out/bin/` by default). This is what makes `zig build` produce an actual binary you can find.\n\nThe `run_cmd` and `run_step` block creates the `zig build run` subcommand. `b.addRunArtifact(exe)` creates a step that executes the compiled binary. `run_cmd.step.dependOn(b.getInstallStep())` says \

(which means compiling it first). This dependency chaining is how the build graph works -- steps depend on other steps, and the build system figures out the right order.

The test section does the same for `zig build test` -- compile the test binary (which includes all `test` blocks from the root source file and its imports), then run it.

## Build modes and optimization

Zig has four build modes that you select with `-Doptimize=`:

```zig
const std = @import(\

mode for most applications -- you get good performance while still catching bugs that slip through testing. If an out-of-bounds access happens in production, you get a stack trace in stead of a silent memory corruption.\n\n**`ReleaseFast`**: maximum optimization, safety checks disabled. The compiler assumes your code is correct and optimizes accordinly. An out-of-bounds access is undefined behavior -- it might crash, it might silently corrupt memory, or it might appear to \

and then fail mysteriously later. Use only for performance-critical inner loops where you've already validated correctness with `ReleaseSafe`.

**`ReleaseSmall`**: optimized for binary size, safety checks disabled. Useful for embedded targets, WebAssembly, or anywhere binary size matters more than raw speed. The compiler trades execution speed for smaller output.

The practical difference between these modes is significant. I've seen `ReleaseFast` binaries run 5-10x faster than `Debug` on computation-heavy workloads. But `Debug` catches bugs that `ReleaseFast` turns into silent corruption. My workflow: develop in `Debug`, test in `ReleaseSafe`, profile in `ReleaseFast`, ship in `ReleaseSafe` unless profiling shows the safety checks are a bottleneck (they rarely are).

## Linking C libraries

One of Zig's biggest selling points is seamless C interop, and the build system is where that happens. Want to use zlib for compression? sqlite3 for a database? SDL2 for graphics? It's a few lines in `build.zig`:

```zig
const std = @import(\

,
    },
}
```

To add a dependency, you use `zig fetch --save` which downloads the package, computes the content hash, and adds the entry to your `.zon` file:

```bash
zig fetch --save https://github.com/zigzap/zap/archive/refs/tags/v0.2.0.tar.gz
```

The hash is a content hash of the entire package -- if the upstream tarball changes (even by one byte), the hash won't match and Zig will refuse to use it. This gives you reproducible builds without a lock file. The hash IS the lock.

Then in `build.zig`, you consume the dependency:

```zig
const std = @import(\
, ...)` fetches the dependency (using the URL and hash from `.zon`) and builds it with the given target and optimize options. `exe.root_module.addImport(\
, ...)` makes it importable in your source code as `const zap = @import(\

);`. That's the entire workflow. No `npm install`. No `cargo add`. Just `zig fetch --save URL` and a few lines in `build.zig`.

The package system is still evolving (Zig 0.14 made several improvements), but the basic flow is stable: declare in `.zon`, fetch with `zig fetch`, consume with `b.dependency()`, import in source.

## Custom build steps

Here's where `build.zig` being real Zig code truly shines. You can define custom build steps that run arbitrary logic -- generating source files, processing assets, running code generators, anything you can express in Zig:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{version.build_time});
}
```

This is a simple example but the pattern extends to anything: generating Zig code from a schema file, embedding binary assets as comptime-known byte arrays, running a pre-build linter, etc. Because build steps form a **dependency graph** (step B depends on step A), the build system automatically figures out the correct execution order and parallelizes independent steps.

A more practical example -- running a tool that generates source code before compilation:

```zig
const std = @import(\

at runtime, but literally removed from the compiled output. This is conditional compilation without preprocessor macros. Just Zig.

## Cross-compilation

Cross-compilation in Zig is a first-class feature, not an afterthought. You don't need a separate cross-compilation toolchain. The Zig compiler IS the cross-compiler:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, core_module);
    test_step.dependOn(&b.addRunArtifact(server_tests).step);
}
```

The `core_module` is shared between all three binaries. Change something in `src/core/lib.zig` and all three get recompiled. Change something in `src/server/main.zig` and only the server is recompiled. The build system tracks dependencies at the file level, so incremental builds are efficient even in large multi-binary projects.

This is also where the project structure from [ep010](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io) comes together. Modules (`@import` with file paths) organize your source code. The build script declares how those modules are assembled into executables and libraries. The two systems work hand-in-hand: modules define code boundaries, the build system defines compilation boundaries.

## The build graph mental model

Here's the key insight that ties everything together: `build.zig` doesn't DO anything directly. It **describes** a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of steps. When you run `zig build`, the build system:

1. Calls your `pub fn build(b: *std.Build)` function
2. Identifies the target step (default: the install step, or whatever you pass as `zig build <step-name>`)
3. Walks the dependency graph backwards from that target
4. Executes steps in topological order, parallelizing independent steps

This is why the order of calls in `build.zig` doesn't matter much. You can declare the test step before the executable, or the run step after the install. The dependency graph determines execution order, not the source order. Every `step.dependOn(&other_step.step)` call adds an edge in this graph.

The `zig build` command with no arguments runs the default install step. `zig build run` runs the \
step (which depends on install, which depends on compilation). `zig build test` runs the \

step. You can define as many named steps as you need -- `zig build lint`, `zig build docs`, `zig build deploy`, whatever makes sense for your project.

## Exercises

1. Create a `build.zig` that builds two executables from the same `src/` directory: `app` (from `src/main.zig`) and `tool` (from `src/tool.zig`). Both should share a common module from `src/common.zig`. Add a `run-app` step and a `run-tool` step so you can do `zig build run-app` and `zig build run-tool` separately. Also add a test step that runs tests from all three files.

2. Add a custom build option `--Dlog-level=` that accepts an enum value (`info`, `warn`, `error`). Pass it to the source code via `addOptions()` so that `@import(\

).log_level` is a comptime-known enum value. In `main.zig`, use a `switch` on this value to conditionally compile different logging behavior -- the unreachable branches should be eliminated by the compiler.

3. Set up a `build.zig.zon` and `build.zig` that pulls in `zig-clap` (a command-line argument parser) as a dependency. Wire it through `b.dependency()` and `addImport()`, then write a `main.zig` that uses clap to parse `--name` and `--count` arguments. Verify that `zig build run -- --name hello --count 3` works end to end. (You'll need an internet connection for `zig fetch`.)

## Dusssssss, wat hebben we nou geleerd?

- `build.zig` is a Zig program, not a config file. Your build configuration uses the same language features you already know -- conditionals, loops, functions, error handling.
- `zig init` generates a starter `build.zig` with standard target/optimize options, an executable step, a run step, and a test step. Understand these default pieces and you can extend the build to do anything.
- Four build modes control the safety/performance tradeoff: `Debug` (safe + slow), `ReleaseSafe` (safe + fast), `ReleaseFast` (unsafe + fastest), `ReleaseSmall` (unsafe + smallest). Develop in Debug, ship ReleaseSafe unless profiling says otherwise.
- C interop goes through the build system: `exe.linkLibC()`, `exe.linkSystemLibrary(\

)`, and `@cImport` in source code. The build system finds and links C libraries; `@cImport` generates Zig bindings from C headers.
- Package management: declare dependencies in `build.zig.zon` (content-hashed for reproducibility), fetch with `zig fetch --save`, consume with `b.dependency()` and `addImport()`. No lock file needed -- the content hash IS the lock.
- Custom build steps (code generation, asset processing, pre-build tools) integrate naturally because build steps form a dependency graph that the build system resolves automatically.
- Build options (`b.option()` + `addOptions()`) pass comptime-known configuration from the command line to the source code. Dead branches are eliminated entirely -- this is conditional compilation without preprocessor macros.
- Cross-compilation is built in: `b.resolveTargetQuery(.{ .cpu_arch = .aarch64, .os_tag = .linux })` builds for ARM64 Linux from any host. No extra toolchains. Zig ships its own linker and bundled C standard library for every target.

We've now covered the full compilation pipeline. Next time we're looking at something lower-level -- how Zig handles sentinel-terminated types and C strings. If you've been wondering why `[*:0]const u8` has that colon-zero in it, or how Zig's string handling differs from C's null-terminated convention, that's what's coming ;-)

### Thanks for reading!

body.title: Find the Odd Out Indie Horror Game Review and Let’s Play
body.body:
Horror games are quite the rage for the last few years. I attribute it to the rise in ease of use in game engines such as Unreal Engine and Unity Engine, among others. Short games have to be focused and horror is a fun genre that works extremely well in a limited time frame and an overall small game. Find the Odd Out is one of those spot the difference style horror games. Unlike more mainstream variations such as Exit 8, another spot the anomaly game, Find the Odd Out is limited to literally a hallway. That is more than enough to make you jump.

Limited Space Horror Doesn’t Have to Be Limited in Scope

Find the Odd Out is an indie game through and through. The graphics are not going to challenge Crimson Dessert or anything. Honestly, they don’t have to. The graphics that are there are subliminally unsettling and that is part of the charm. As mentioned already, you are limited to a hallway with doors on one side. Your goal is to peek through the peep hole and look at each room. There is something different about one room and you must spot that difference. Entering the one room that features the anomaly will let you advance to the next level. Each level has different rooms and a different number of them to peek in on. https://youtu.be/6V2xFEh5mFk

Horror with No Blood or Guts

Most horror games rely on blood and guts to get frights out of players. Find the Odd Out is not like that. There is no blood or guts that I could find. There was a decapitated doll on one level but that is a toy. Not a person. Your controls are limited to moving around with the WASD keys, familiar to anyone that has played many PC games. You can highlight the peep hole to look or highlight the door handle and click to enter that room. There is a stranger at the other end of the hallway, maybe they are in their own game as well? They are a source of jump scares though so keep an eye on them. I don’t want to ruin the fun of Find the Odd Out so I will stop here as far as describing what you may encounter. Just pay attention to the small details even though they are not a guarantee at spotting the anomaly. Find the Odd Out is a short game. I think I beat it, or lost depending on how you look at it, in just over five minutes. [The itch.io page](https://araishi.itch.io/find-the-odd-out) says total playtime is about 5 to 10 minutes though “winning” conditions are nowhere to be found. If you want a family safe horror game to play with younger fans, then Find the Odd Out might fit the bill. Just watch the first couple of minutes of the video embedded above and you will have all the information you need to make an informed decision. Find the Odd Out is free so you cannot beat the price for a few minutes of scares.

body.body: @luchyl that looks like a **staghorn fern** (*Platycerium*), an epiphytic fern that grows attached to tree trunks instead of rooting in soil; the round green “shield” frond hugs the bark, while the longer antler-shaped fronds hang outward, which is the giveaway [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platycerium) [Wisconsin Horticulture](https://hort.extension.wisc.edu/articles/staghorn-fern-platycerium-bifurcatum/) [NC State Extension](https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/platycerium-bifurcatum/). The dry brown parts are older basal fronds, and they’re not a problem by themselves — they help protect the plant and trap moisture and nutrients. I don’t have a clean InLeo nature thread to cite for this specific plant right now, but the ID itself is pretty solid.

Steem advented in 2016 at #3 on Coinmarketcap.  Since then social media has become the largest sector of the global financial markets while Steem, and now Hive, have continued to plunge in the rankings.  The reason Hive continues to shrink while the social media market continues to grow is that >90% of rewards from the rewards pool are extracted by the whales that possess >50% of stake voting for witnesses.

If Hive well rewarded good creators for publishing content on Hive, those good creators would stay on Hive, and their good posts would attract new users that see good creators happy they publish on Hive.  That is all we need, and until we have that we will not have what we need to grow and attract investors.  The problem for Hive is that the current government can only retain it's total control if it retains >50% of stake voting for witnesses, so they do not want to lose their lock on governance by diluting their controlling stake with new investors that will then be able to vote that stake for witnesses.

We could be #1 in the social media rankings, and on Coinmarketcap, and all we need to do is reward good creators well so they are happy they are posting their good content on Hive, and that will attract new users, which will attract investors because Hive is a growing platform that is a good investment opportunity.  Nothing else we do will suffice, and unless we do that we will continue to shrink and discourage new investment.

Gone So Soon! The day of one's birth usually full of rejoicing and songs of praises, but the day of one's death is full of pains, sorrow and grief! Death the very opposite of life - where is your sting!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdjhUjYJJLtz6XrFi67Tp92kUqkRj3A32PWx6Zarj5VpP/img_20260410_182239.jpg)

On Wednesday 8th April 2026, the call of my dad woke me up! When I picked up the call, he said \

I didn't wait to ask him much because the voice was so faint, so I prepared and rush down to Ikot Ekpene. Bought him some drugs and checked his heartbeat. I stayed for some hours and found out that he is relief before I returned to Uyo. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeW3BJYZe2BW13uwcrSDRf9TERV8WFtnJ1JbxZa2heeSx/screenshot_20260410_180224_com.android.calendar.jpg) Today, 10th of April 2026 by 5.55am his call woke me and I quickly picked it up only to hear a female voice telling me to come as far as I can, that my dad has been rushed to the general hospital and was rejected, right there I knew there is a problem. My brother and others took him to five different hospital but with no solution, at last he was confirm death! I felt as if the whole world has crumble over me as I close my eyes several times and open again and again only to realize that I am not day dreaming but the very sad reality of life. So the 10th of April 2026 has recorded itself as the saddest day in my life where the very cold hands of death took away the pillar of the family. Looking at my mum and siblings crying, sobbing, wailing and calling out to him while he remains mute is a mental pictures that will remain indelible in my memory. As I watch his corpse deposited to the mutualry, the taught of not seeing him again, going back home without him, pull a painful and heavy outbost of tears within me, and I create this post, I can't even give a vivid explanations of my mental state as heavy drops of tears keeps rolling down my eyes. Oh Death, where is your sting, what a sad reality of life! ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWBnQr2j3XG9X9oCsPNefuPJkDE7tvHjQL3h3CjWWFt9t/img_0.7231599284278845.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV5nZmjVoFbV3JEYH1hrVhXVyy6BgW3CaYCNz4G1hEnt8/img_0.5512112418065316.jpg) I remains @oasiskp2 #aliveandthriving #iamalivechallenge #ecency #pepe #neoxian #pob #cent #meme #archon #lifestyle
