title.title: Que hago para mantener o procurar mi salud? \\ What can I do to maintain or take care of my health?
title.body:
En la comunidad @holos-lotus la salud integral de las personas es primordial en todo los aspectos físico, emocional, mental, espiritual y haberse celebrado 7 de abril, Día mundial de la salud, fecha dedicada a concientizar sobre la importancia de cuidar la salud en todo el mundo, la amiga @damarysvibra nos invite a participar y reflexionar en su nueva iniciativa que pone en foco el bienestar humano y su conexión con el entorno, las emociones, los vínculos, los buenos hábitos en pensamientos, acciones que seguimos y hacemos en pro de nuestro bienestar cada granito de arena que hagamos cuenta. >In the @holos-lotus community, the holistic health of individuals is paramount in all aspects: physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual. With the celebration of World Health Day on April 7th, a date dedicated to raising awareness about the importance of health care worldwide, our friend @damarysvibra invites us to participate and reflect on her new initiative. This initiative focuses on human well-being and its connection to the environment, emotions, relationships, and the positive habits in our thoughts and actions that we follow and take for our well-being. Every little bit helps. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRPNHv11Mw3NpzDazbWUrtbbje15QkAjA6kn3TzBx1Djy/1775823096258.jpg) **Que hago para mantener o procurar mi salud??** Combinar la medicina con mi estilo de vida, soy hipertensa debo consumir una dosis de pastilla diaria, pero mi estilo de vida influye mucho en mi bienestar, para eso camino en la mañana una hora o hora y media, cuando no puedo caminar me ejercito en la casa, mis comidas balanceada y bajas en sal, evito las grasas saturadas, no fumo, no bebo, bueno solo un poquito y en ocasiones especiales, tomo mucha agua, duermo bien, socializo, leo, escribo, bailo, conecto con la naturaleza, evito confrontaciones, salgo a pasear a los centros comerciales, el campo y plazas, llevo a mi nieta al parque jugamos corremos, reír mucho, ir a la peluquería por lo menos una vez al mes a consentirme( con mi cabello, cejas o uñas, una de las tres cosas, pocas veces todas juntas ), cuidar mi salud mental (manejo de estrés), orar mucho, distracción (juegos de mesa) regulación de uso de redes sociales, poner límites sanos y claros, chequeos médicos cuando mi cuerpo me da señales, actitud y gratitud positiva, son hábitos o acciones que ayudan a mi mente y cuerpo a mantenerse fuerte, activos y funcionando bien, me ahorro visitas al médico, malestares y preocupaciones, mi cuerpo es el santuario que voy a ocupar toda la vida se merece toda mi atención y bondad. >**What do I do to maintain or take care of my health?** I combine medicine with my lifestyle. I have high blood pressure and must take a daily dose of medication, but my lifestyle greatly influences my well-being. For this, I walk for an hour or an hour and a half in the morning. When I can't walk, I exercise at home. I eat balanced meals that are low in salt, I avoid saturated fats, I don't smoke, I don't drink—well, only a little and on special occasions—I drink plenty of water, I sleep well, I socialize, I read, I write, I dance, I connect with nature, I avoid confrontations, I go for walks to shopping malls, the countryside, and parks, I take my granddaughter to the park where we play and run, I laugh a lot, I go to the hairdresser at least once a month to pamper myself (with my hair, eyebrows, or nails—one of the three, rarely all at once), I take care of my mental health (stress management), I pray a lot, I have distractions (board games), I regulate my social media use, and I set boundaries. Healthy and clear, medical checkups when my body gives me signals, positive attitude and gratitude, are habits or actions that help my mind and body stay strong, active and functioning well, I save myself visits to the doctor, discomfort and worries, my body is the sanctuary that I will occupy all my life, it deserves all my attention and kindness. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNtGNayMPLwUxEV88S97PSemRdiSQ92PdcMW5aUkaAvBP/1775823126793.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdAXN6sJDLGkVpNiSSqqJ1RPh96U3S3gxT8qHpe7hZtnS/1775823371296.jpg) Aun así pienso que cuidar de nuestra salud va más allá simples hábitos diarios, es esencial revisiones médicas periódicas para prever o atender las señales de nuestro cuerpo, ahí es donde lo fácil se vuelve imposible y entra en acción las finanzas, mucha gente no tiene ni siquiera para comerse una comida completa como hace para ir a un centro de salud a hacerse chequeos preventivos, es verdad que existen servicios de salud pública donde cuesta conseguir una cita para ser atendidos, luego los exámenes, análisis y medicamentos costosos imposibles de cubrir, en Venezuela tenemos una fuerte crisis de salud que nos obliga a cubrir nuestras emergencias y no siempre tenemos como asumir dicho gasto es por eso que siempre vemos muchas personas pidiendo dinero para ayudar a un familiar, amigo o conocido, el 7 de abril me parece un día propicio para reflexionar que tenemos derecho a vivir una vida digna, merecemos un sistema sanitario que nos sostenga a todos por igual, que sea capaz de regular, controlar y garantizar los recursos necesarios para los centros de salud pública, infraestructura, medicinas y personal médico, merecemos ser escuchados, acompañados, amparados y recibir herramientas para alcanzar nuestro bienestar integral. >Even so, I think that taking care of our health goes beyond simple daily habits. Regular medical checkups are essential to anticipate or address our body's signals. That's where what seems easy becomes impossible, and finances come into play. Many people can't even afford a full meal, let alone go to a health center for preventative checkups. It's true that there are public health services where it's difficult to get an appointment, and then there are the expensive tests, analyses, and medications that are impossible to cover. In Venezuela, we have a severe health crisis that forces us to cover our emergencies, and we don't always have the means to do so. That's why we always see so many people asking for money to help a family member, friend, or acquaintance. April 7th seems like an opportune day to reflect on the fact that we have the right to live a dignified life. We deserve a healthcare system that supports us all equally, one that is capable of regulating, controlling, and guaranteeing the necessary resources for public health centers, infrastructure, medicines, and medical personnel. We deserve to be heard, supported, protected, and given the tools to achieve our overall well-being. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTGSs3x9VrsnLKDTCYbGMcz4y2bm6iBNM9ydofRxoAc57/1775823329437.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUpvzPGrAfhFYuhhEMSMA9KLGXYfnj5nHLvMGwTn4VXi8/1775823294797.jpg)
>

title.title: The Artistry of Coleus Vibrant Hues and Intricate Patterns
title.body:
![20260409_062259_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23tvqBkwCzzDBQkVKEciFuEXiosHxjADPBAmJtwUUcRfBCuarvR69s6zG9LwXBkt4dsSP.png)



Lets talk about these amazing plants you see in the pictures the Coleus If you are a plant lover or even if you just appreciate something beautiful and colorful you are going to love these guys.



![20260409_062300_0001.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23yd7nfoRK8r4HxHMTa24aDkmZ3qVT1NGDvEAWLNgzAWipxvoM78n4GmhtarKJXynFBkF.png)

​
They are seriously like natures own little works of art and they bring so much life to any spot they are in. What makes Coleus so cool is all the crazy colors and patterns you can find on their leaves.



![20260409_062301_0011.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23uQy6PCZJf4RVYX5uFAwggfdpAYQC1R26GrY1BLgAZRTTFBj3zYygjvXKVCJvFGEwDDp.png)

​
Forget about plain green these plants are wild. Youve got deep rich purples that almost look black mixed with bright magentas and even some creamy yellows.



![20260409_062301_0010.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23xL51yvX5bjr6EmdhXisXrqaLwjawiLJhWrMQaY8Nq4n8rphsHmerDPhDByAcb779Siy.png)

​
Then there are the greens  from super bright almost neon lime green, to a dark foresty shade. And they dont just sit there in solid blocks of color. 



![20260409_062301_0005.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/242NirG1BAyaXAB9LoeeEf43YPgVTmu8jpjV3tnaanVEhXbf6ADnQN122km4ziRRgf8xL.png)


​
You will see splashes streaks and swirls almost like someone took a paintbrush and just had fun. Some leaves have a bold color right in the middle with a totally different color around the edges,l making them really pop.



![20260409_062301_0009.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23wgQCqnze5JLp9s3e1q44qoNnWP7Z81rXn23EmqDJyHdQrZB1T83gRHfUq4osMSK1mwA.png)

​
Its like each leaf has its own unique design. And its not just the colors. Look closely and you will see that the leaves arent always perfectly smooth and flat.



![20260409_062301_0008.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23vsUkxScGz4BVKmu8SwKFvdy6GhqTYvejMonjpZ1yWcg6R1tuUHL45DYsPZuG5fEFoxy.png)

​
Some of them have these cool ruffled or scalloped edges giving them a bit of a wavy textured look. It makes them even more interesting to stare at.



![20260409_062301_0007.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23wMeaTKxR1b4r7SnxJ4XSLhnoFAt9E4g32bEnKSyfsamALjECc6jYr578NxRzBdPvRCr.png)

​
The veins on the leaves are often a different color too which adds another layer of detail to their already intricate appearance.




![20260409_062301_0006.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23uFW8Rpx1a4jSWJDUDvYt7gTx6g4x92NqtNh16hJZMzsj6tKRSTS1sXcFzca78deMAFM.png)


​
The best part about Coleus is that you dont need flowers for them to be pretty. Their leaves are the showstoppers. This means they stay colorful and vibrant all season long. 




![20260409_062301_0003.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23xpEfrkB6G7iig7NkAt2RVhFNJUTGpNSMxta63NbmPyGRpChp7aHHyNUSMqCyVVezck4.png)


​
You can put them in pots hanging baskets or right in your garden bed, and they will instantly brighten up the whole area. They are pretty easy to take care of too which is a huge bonus.



![20260409_062301_0002.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23uFUAAQpxN1hSjNjTiuR71R1UBzNz9ttPNvRbxkMUAbkdqUVoST9SMcxFDCk4J159nyZ.png)

​
Just give them some good light though some varieties prefer a bit of shade water them regularly and watch them do their thing.



![20260409_062301_0003.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rodavlas/23xpEfrkB6G7iig7NkAt2RVhFNJUTGpNSMxta63NbmPyGRpChp7aHHyNUSMqCyVVezck4.png)

​
They come in so many different varieties that you could probably fill your whole garden with just Coleus and never get bored. If you are looking to add some serious wow factor to your space,l these plants are definitely the way to go.

title.title: More Garden Work - April 9, 2026@goldenoakfarm
title.body:
![Finishing amendment mix formulas crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EowEgVfhVnyG9b9wtkbyE81qL5aYPsgmv9kG29bAgLjDwKM7CSQwMP8AdcSUhegVJVv.jpg)

On Thursday morning I was up around 6AM and got a load in the dishwasher. I got my post up and my soil test results came in. So I spent an hour or so working up the amendment mixes sheets.

My poor brain cell was finished at the end, so I probably better check the math on Friday morning. I got another load in the dishwasher and my #2 intern arrived at noon.

![Big garden now collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23wX9a77Qe5VvzBZNYfDJ4TNQpkDfKcAiXAWFBYYWqhteBVxXc8vZQLqH88c6h4xWS2nC.jpg)

We went out to show her what needed to be done. First we went to uncover the rhubarb. There were no shoots…  Upon closer inspection, something had eaten them!!  I’ve grown rhubarb in this spot exactly the same way for 2 decades, and nothing ever bothered it. Sigh….

But nothing had bothered the garlic and she went along the rows, uncovering the shoots stuck under hay.

![Garden work collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23y94BpZLdXopkxkK95iRxCXMrh9jmYMtnf28hzyavJMTBwTXAuhNCzm3Y7M8BpDnV5np.jpg)

Her other jobs were to get the protective spirals off the Little Trees and Little Trees II; cut down the tall stuff in the Fence gardens; and to start the cleanout under the azalea.

She got carried away with the Fence gardens and cleaned them right out! She made it down around the corner and decided she’d gone overboard. So she moved over to the azalea and got the weeds and some of the grass out.

She plans to come back on Friday and finish these last 2 jobs. We also have to move some of the new green wood so we can get to the rest of the dry wood in the shed.

![West gardens collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xyZSaUC74yq8V2JSZ7KMRs8a2LmUQbmhnPQ6sQXEBYyNWfUq72CF5HTkruUSRAxBcKK.jpg)

I’d hoped to get out to these gardens on Thursday, but it was still too cold and windy. So I finished the laundry, cleaned up the kitchen and watered some of the seedlings.

My #4 helper arrived at 1:30PM and I sent her shopping. I didn’t get much of anything done during the afternoon. She got vacuuming and floor washing done when she got back.

She said at her house, in addition to the tulips, the critters had eaten 2 of her roses, and her yucca plants during the winter. She attributes it to loosing her indoor/outdoor cat last year. So she’s hoping to find an indoor/outdoor cat to replace him.

As we were talking about this, she looked at my tulips that weren’t looking so good, and pulled a leaf. It came right out! Something has been after the tulips too in my garden! Sigh…

![Little Trees - forsythia collage text crop April 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23rBBwXuzEHqmDrG7E6sfXG99rVZ9bxx5ZsXeeQ1SQNqP56mQTnyBcurVfuB3oJPtiFMT.jpg)

I watched the rest of David Attenborough’s ‘Life of Mammals’ before starting small fires in both stoves as it was to be mid 30’s during the night. I was in bed shortly after 8PM.

It’s to hit high 60’s on Friday, so I am planning to get out to those gardens around 11AM when it has warmed up. My #3 helper will arrive around 12:30PM. She will bring the screens up from the cellar and we will get them all washed. That way I’ll be ready if they ever assign someone to do the windows.

I’ve also got the clean up the kitchen and feed the seedlings and water house plants on Friday.

So another busy day…

![Mini bio framed Jan 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xyn876JURgHHjsp757ZTvXeEEBjdDeLXWynRcLCeuqwPPsqtEtXTosSPyKZdAgWivJB.jpg)

title.title: Money Matters: My Youngest Sister's Money Masters 101 Experience
title.body:
> Growing up, I thought I already knew money. I knew cash… and I knew there was this thing called a 'card'. That’s it. I didn’t even know what kind of card it was or how it actually worked. All I know is that you just swipe it. As long as the payment goes through, it's done 😆 Looking back now, it's funny, but at the same time, it made me realize how little we actually knew about something so important. So seeing kids nowadays, including my youngest sister and my newphews & nieces, learn about money this early makes me really happy for them. Last December, my youngest sister, Bunbun, was invited to attend Money Masters 101. It's a financial literacy class for kids.
![IMG_8452.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/Ep1aqU1VHSwnby8hXvGoBpidcb53uGyeskvwvV2Vh5Vsbh1uh2qAzUSPTxcg1FRhZNc.JPG)
Image from [Street Smart PH Facebook Page](https://www.facebook.com/p/Street-Smart-PH-61577679085721/) It’s an event by Street Smart PH, a passion project that aims to help Filipino kids and teens for “adulting” by teaching them practical life skills early on. I actually love their concept. Most of the time, we only learn these things when we're already forced to deal with real responsibilities. They partnered with KasKasan Buddies, a finance community that helps Filipinos use their money smarter, especially when it comes to credit cards, spending habits, and financial decisions. Usually, events like this come with a fee (around ₱400+ per class), but this one was extra special because Bunbun got invited for free through our relative, J, who's part of the KasKasan Buddies management team. Of course, she wasn’t going alone. Bunbun, my nephew Rusell (who's also my godchild), and my niece Leah, were all attending. Since the venue was just nearby, at The Loft in BGC, I decided to come with them. I was also curious about what they were going to learn.
![pics.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23xp2TapkP2v5hCiHqo2BJRMNG65Cyu5G6FqeV9KWtMmAE6qeNxF7sdbVxveVPxSKCs59.png)
It actually rained that day, so our plan to arrive early didn’t really go as planned. Good thing J reassured us that it was okay and told us to just head inside since they weren’t starting yet and were still waiting for other kids to arrive. When we got there, the atmosphere was actually very welcoming. There were already a few kids inside, some with their parents or guardians, while others were already chatting and making new friends. It didn’t feel intimidating at all, which I think is really important for events like this, especially for kids. One of the reasons we let Bunbun attend classes like this is to interact with other people and make new friends. J gathered them and started explaining what the class was about in a very simple and engaging way. ####
The Kit That Got Them Excited
Before anything else, they were given their own Money Masters 101 kit. | ![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23wqnamYxapjsNCSg5aQHMg9nT6RTXN7Ut4t3h6S6zqaDW4Pohh4xjZTJzhwjUvaRayoK.png) | ![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23tvitsS9Wd7aKBYJsoX6qcFEv4H1Tamjr3sMRWy9MBxZJLsdFLddoKmbwD2MzyeqSiYM.png) | | - | - | The kit included: - A basic calculator - A sample checkbook - A 68.6k ipon challenge coin bank - A weekly planner notepad - A Money Masters 101 activity notebook - A financial literacy activity notebook What I liked about it is that it wasn’t just for display. Those are things they could actually use even after the class. It made the whole experience feel more practical, not just something they attend and forget after.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23tmSXUPpvzQpRgHdfT1AzL6VcgDN1C18pgRPfohKU2Dhdp2oK3A8426u7css49Ak4rYu.png)
I noticed how the kids immediately started flipping through the notebooks, checking each item, and asking questions. ####
What They Learned
The class itself covered the basics but in a way kids could actually understand and apply. They talked about: 💰 **Saving** 💰 This was Bunbun’s favorite part because she got to draw what she’s saving up for. They were asked what they’re saving for, and since it was December, most of them said Christmas gifts. Some also shared that they’re saving for their dream toys. They talked about why saving money is important, even at a young age, and even learned about big and small saving goals, which I think is really nice for kids to understand this early.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (4).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23u673qMwZvSf4U2JBzcMVkcGzV63gq5cmZiM8A2JgrFaFX7ydxMyq4W81JyDvy9Kzrun.png)
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (5).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23w2sDCoyW9G8eg6bv5s8q2jqdacRBxM5YWmyXZPnVT5ev4m7Ew3yAo4siqam9QKh7orv.png)
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (8).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23tvkXLPtQ5TQVABgVTP1uKgmbLKZ32gEwvfyDTwrC2M1UhCinLWQ8BbRiG6EcCegpJ3v.png)
📊 **Budgeting** 📊 They were given paper money cutouts and got to try budgeting it on their own. Some went all out with spending hahaha while others chose to share most of their money. Kids will be kids!
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (7).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23tvnqMSfKCXfCok5P5KAZ4nXCueN8wR5MSPRiEk4nXBke1AMweXjCxKg6nrqXz6628sF.png)
What I really liked about this class is how they encouraged the kids to think of simple ways to divide and manage their money. They also introduced the idea of allocating for needs, wants, and savings. I really appreciate this because it’s something we usually learn much later in life or sometimes not at all.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (10).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23uR3BVbkNP6ggYFWtwM5E6NkdaHMbCuFwG38SmThSYrdMEyQPsu5qAATwB2z9Ka6fhhf.png)
🏦 **Banking Basics** 🏦 This is probably one of my favorite parts. They explained in a simple way how banks work, why people save money there, and how it helps keep their money safe. The kids were also given a sample checkbook and passbook, and learned how to use them, which I found really nice and helpful.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (3).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23w2siaJCLQn2WPD5jgsQHqYrteSJ1EdAD11NehjBcW8HrXtnkXKen7NQpcp3B75JaNUR.png)
💳 **Credit vs Debit Cards** 💳 This is actually my favorite part even if I’m not the target of the class 😆 They explained the difference between credit and debit cards in a really simple way, something I definitely didn’t understand when I was younger. The kids even got to make their own sample card, where they learned the parts like the account number, expiration date, CVV, and signature.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (9).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23wC9VKZkMfDKf4WXcXLgjpCUcp9GoKod7bpQKTANbmA9xdKDixDjDT4ePntC6MKv75ya.png)
| ![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (12).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23wgPgs5gVdB1ZAmqeoZoeeoT9CTQCYxiA7xzhQYzXKKq37byAPoqSpiUbKR3RpRDnPt8.png) | ![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (13).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23vhyZF4rgPsHUJcpYbHE7tMLDgq37XNRrDSM6k52q91c47xusJakDrcu67gCreyhiy3y.png) | | - | - | What I loved most was that the class wasn’t just pure lecture. The kids were doing activities, writing in their notebooks, and actually participating. It wasn’t boring at all. They were engaged the whole time.
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (6).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23uQrMXacTKKo8cXuKjZe1hXp6tW7kzya4fZ8vMCy5n1nhbhrxFW715g8MeX3fp3tKQUC.png)
They share their answers to questions and they help each other (there were group activites about bugeting). While they were busy with their activities, I couldn’t help but reflect. Back then, I thought swiping a card was just swiping a card. I had no idea where the money came from, how it worked, or what the consequences were. Seeing them now, learning about saving, budgeting, and even understanding cards at such a young age made me realize how important this kind of education is. Imagine how different things could be if we all learned this early. ####
Why This Matters
Financial literacy is one of the things that people often overlook until it becomes a problem. It’s not something we shouldn't only learn when we’re already earning, paying bills, or dealing with financial stress. It should start early. When kids understand money at a young age, they grow up with better habits and stronger decision-making skills. They become more mindful of how they spend, save, and value money. I’m really glad Bunbun got to experience this and even happier that Rusell and Leah were there too. As someone who got to witness it firsthand, I can say that classes like this are more than just workshops. They’re a great head start for kids to understand the real world a little better. I also didn't expect I'd learn something from it and reflect this much. I kinda wish I had this when I was younger. The class ended with them taking photos with their certificates. Such a cute and proud moment to see!
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (11).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23uFZw8Zk6Z68sN2vhm22FJNBt5GHZcNhtbpdekQf9Z6giLwVcg6S86F41fo6KBtdrv8H.png)
---
**Would you let your kids (or younger siblings) attend something like this?**
--- I appreciate you reading this all the way through. Thanks for your precious time~ ---
![Copy of Simple Modern Explore the City Travel YouTube Thumbnail (15).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cthings/23uQxfQXmd7pBpa4JECzBMCXEco6kYZAfYstdmkpAF4pm921kAWkWBxYTqW5NqfNNEWU7.png)

title.title: Adventures In Homesteading (Day 613)
title.body:
Hello Everyone!

**Missing the writing mark, Getting some supplies, The handy wagon, A little hiking & A rooster on the mend!**

Alright, I wound up going to sleep early last night instead of doing any writing... and told myself that I would do it when I woke up again. Knowing that it would be a gamble on whether I woke up after a few hours (or in the morning) did not make much difference to me... because I was too exhausted to worry about it.

Basically, I took a nap late in the day but only slept for a few minutes... before waking back up, feeling super hungry and then deciding to order some supplies. I could have gone longer without supplies... but having mainly been eating canned goods lately... I really needed something else because the sodium (from the canned food) was starting to get to me.

Since there was no way I was going to try carrying all the groceries (and jugs of drinking water) from the top of the driveway to the studio with my foot injury... I would need the wagon. Which meant that I had to get the rainwater bailed out of it, dry it out... and then haul it to the top of the hill before the delivery driver arrived.

Getting my sore foot into my muck boot sure did not feel all that awesome... but once the boot was actually on... walking around was not *too* difficult (or painful) as long as I was not on an incline... which pretty much everything here is on! Aside from lugging the wagon up and down the hill, the tricky part was bailing the water out of it into a small rainwater barrel... because I had to keep hiking back and forth between the two with the bowl I was using as a bail.

Thankfully the wagon has those 'side walls' on it... and its handle is setup the way that it is (to make it easy to steer on a slope) because once I had it full of groceries... I was able to let the wagon (with the groceries in it) push against me... as I slowly ambled down the driveway. It worked out rather well doing that particular maneuver... but every other step (where I had to put weight on my injured foot) caused a shooting pain... and had I not been able to lean on the wagon... I would have undoubtedly lost control of it.

Anyways, I did not really get much done earlier in the day... but I did force myself to hike around a little bit to take in the scenery, get some sunshine and see what all is growing around the place. I was also hoping to maybe 'walk it off' some with my foot injury... but I am unsure how successful that I was with that... regardless of ending my walks the moment that my foot gave me any real trouble as far as 'intense' pain goes.

Late in the afternoon, once I knew that I could walk around without too much hassle... I moved the silkie rooster from the dog crate in the studio to the dog yard where the chicken coop is. After feeding him all those walnuts, he made quite the recovery... and after around twelve hours of him 'looking better' I decided that it was best to see how he would do outdoors again.

I did have some concerns about him being weak... and not being able to defend himself against predators (or have the wherewithal to notice a nearby bird of prey) so I made sure that Emily the hen was in the dog yard when I put him in there. It was a bit of a gamble on whether he would attack her (like he has before) but I figured that she could defend herself just fine *and* would protect him to some degree or another regardless of his rude behavior.

As it turns out, his recent experiences seem to have given him a small 'attitude adjustment' because he was not super interested in doing more than making some 'conversational' noises at her. She of course, was not having it at all... gave him a wide berth and (from what I could tell) is not going to forget how much he has harassed her in the past.

On a different note, I continued my writing routine of working on that fictional material and although I did not get a whole lot more written... I did get the bulk of the material edited and proofread again. As I am writing on that material, I am also breaking it up into chapters to make the editing a little less daunting... and to make it easier to 'fill in' (or expand upon) different parts of the story... without having to do so inside one large unbroken body of text.     

All the extra writing does not 'fill the void' of wanting to be gathering soil, planting stuff and generally continuing my gardening endeavors... but it has been good for my overall morale. Which is probably going to *keep* improving as I get all my new writing routines dialed in, keep squeezing in a few hikes each day and (once this foot heals) doing a bunch of projects that need doing while the weather is fair.

Well, I think that I am going to wrap this up and get on with the editing and posting phase of things. I hope that everyone is doing well. Ta ta for now.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXyKJekZTEkYdNHc8iXPceRgqX9H7eWgCZDkGzhCck374/img_20260409_155039606.jpg)</center>
<center>*The leaves are returning to the tulip poplar trees!*</center>

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ1QYpkWKQCZRm9fG13ph7ACLBXm88MkwEvuKtN535xDz/img_20260409_155242292.jpg)</center>
<center>*I am so glad that Yang the rooster is feeling better!*</center>

<center>**Thanks for reading!**</center>

<center>**Please check out the [Homesteading Community](https://ecency.com/created/hive-114308)!**
</center>

<center>***Cheers! & Hive On!***</center>

title.title: Quote of the Day 10th April 2026 – Polanski’s nutter attraction machine.
title.body:
![quote-marks-.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23xVgWydLDQNhfmmZ7HYvUGUivaEwC44cXqChiPZdaveamrhZrXxKWa8QWxWME86Y3c3r.jpeg)



Support for the Green Party has grown remarkably during the past year.  Like the Liberal Democrat party in the past the Greens have managed to suck in a lot of support from demographic sectors that are not very politically minded.  This is probably why the Greens were able to take over a constituency like North Herefordshire a seat that would normally be one where the Lib Dems would have a chance.  Like the Lib Dems the Greens have become the party that Britons uninterested in the machinations of politics choose to vote for.  If you didn’t like the ‘Big Two’ parties then you’d probably plump for the Lib Dems but now those same voters are choosing the Greens. These types of voters, the unaware, those disinterested in political policy, the middle class hippies have flocked to the Greens like flies that rush to a freshly laid cow pat.

The problem for the rest of us, those who are sceptical of the Greens is that the party has become a warehouse of some of the worst people in British politics.  As well as the open borders nutters and the science ignorant hippies who believe that we don’t need fossil fuels the Greens have become a home for the worst of the worst of British Islamists.  In short the Greens have become an Islam party with some greenwashing painted over the top. 

Part of the reason why the Greens have done well in terms of support is, in my view, because this party is not as scrutinised by the media and the commentariat as a party like Reform or the Tories or other parties are scrutinised.  The Greens have been able to be all things to all men and have got away with it because not enough people have dug into this disgraceful party that has become a sort of political fly paper for fraggles. 

Victoria Freeman on the X platform told it like it is with the Greens and said:

\

Ms Freeman is correct here.  The Greens are now the party to go for if you hate Jews or are an Islamist nutcase or have nursery school levels of economic knowledge or believe in ‘out there’ stuff such as abolishing police and prisons or believe that women can have penises.  What the Greens have become is far far worse than what the Labour Party under Jeremy Corbyn became. At least in Corbyn’s Labour there were decent Labour members and MP’s who stood up to Corbyn but in the Greens there’s little in the way of any internal pushback against Polanski and his far left and Islamist nutjob supporters.

I agree with those who say that increased scrutiny by the media and others of the Greens might be the lance that pops the foetid boil on the face of British politics that the Greens have become.  After all we have seen this boil popping before with the neo-Nazi British National Party (BNP) who, after their leader was allowed on the BBC’s Question Time programme, lost massive levels of the support that they had got because the BNP had spoken about migration problems that the mainstream parties refused to speak about.  This deflation of the BNP occurred because we could all see how the BNP’s leader Nick Griffin floundered and flustered his way through the Question Time programme allowing him to appear as he really is, which is an extremist.

We need more scrutiny and more critical questioning of the Greens and their potential policies.  By doing that we might see the Greens losing a lot of the casual support that they’ve gained by riding on the vibes that the Greens are not like all the other parties.  I believe that once the Polanski crowd are shown to be economically illiterate and politically dangerous then a lot of their casual non Muslim support might well melt away.  Everyone needs to pick apart every statement from the Greens and their candidates in order to show the country that this party of Jew hating Muslims and economic incompetents cannot be trusted with high office.

> **_Hello beautiful people! I hope you're all doing great and if you're not, you will be soon!_** Getting back into portrait drawing, I chose another one I did a few months ago using traditional media and converted it to digital. It was a Holozing fan art piece, so I hope you like it. I’ve actually been thinking about creating a sort of series of digital drawings, where I convert all the sketches I do in graphite or watercolor to digital and see what they look like in that format. > **_Hola gente bonita! ¡Espero estén súper bien todos y si no lo están, pronto lo estarán!_** Retomando nuevamente la creación de retratos, escogí otro que hice hace unos meses atrás en tradicional y lo pase al digital, fue un fan art de Holozing, así que espero les guste. Realmente ando pensando en hacer una especie de serie de dibujos digitales, en done paso de tradicional al digital todos aquellos dibujos que llegue a hacer en con grafito o acuarelas y verlos hecho ahora en digital. ___

___ This was the traditional drawing I did that I wanted to convert to digital, since I loved how it turned out so much and wanted to see it in digital form; it was a portrait that I really liked when I drew it. > Este fue el dibujo en tradicional que hice y que quise pasar al digital, ya que me encanto demasiado como quedo y quería verlo en digital, fue un retrato que me gusto mucho cuando lo hice.
![IMG_20251124_142918.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oscurocactus/23tHCPruV25rbYtCzHk3esta9h54y4Z8ejtXRFPtVhb7BzkPvSNwwChQuVCrfC2yrTd7N.jpg)
The first thing I did was transfer the drawing to a new layer in Clip Studio Paint and digitize the sketch. I made a few minor adjustments to the anatomy, and once that was done, I added a base color layer in this case, the skin tone. > Lo que hice primeramente fue pasar el dibujo a una capa nueva en el clip studio paint y sacar el boceto en digital. Le arregle ciertas cositas mínimas que tenia en cuanto a anatomía y cuando lo tuve hecho, lo que hice después fue agregar una capa base de color, que es este caso fue el color de la piel. ||| |---|---| |![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oscurocactus/23tSirjPoUgW1CxSjeVzGmgg2WTdmUK5Bp2jP4j4crLHC7dMb65tq37ksvF3SkmUNyLEh.jpg)|![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oscurocactus/23tSqoK5fFjFFfwgxAzAH6eTveLiSiB1AdL3K1k6PiGwvVwTzgH1A8HfJPob8VibsPnyW.jpg)| After that, what I do next is add each base color for each element in the drawing. Then I start adding details all over the face. > Luego de eso, lo que hago después es ir agregando cada color base para cada elemento en el dibujo. Seguidamente comienzo a agregar los detalles en todo la cara. ||| |---|---| |![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oscurocactus/23w31xGtVbPcS4iozG5s6Mor4Sk8BtraJGc8mqAKm1wGq3EMHvQQitZBEtpGKqjki23v4.jpg)|![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oscurocactus/23wqy3htxiSKxu1i55orYjbc7n6WU121tvu2B3ZfWcmJPhkdwQGKAoQ9mTd6TdCbThD4h.jpg)| The truth is, I always start by working on the face, because that’s my weakness so much so that it’s what I’m best at drawing faces. title.title: Taking Stock
title.body:
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXeYLBitjtaFYoUwpwaRvEgdseitpaXQhNKn2vraAsjdH/PXL_20260327_173009771.webp)

---------------------------

We are right around halfway through the NCAA softball season now.  If you have been following me this week, you got an update on two of my favorite teams, the Tiffin Dragons and the Radford Highlanders.  Radford is back in action on ESPN+ tonight around 6 PM EST if you are interested in catching that.  I know that's what I will be watching!

Meanwhile, the rest of the field continues to move along.  Including the Division I power schools that usually get the most attention at the national level.  While mid/majors like Radford occasionally get their chance in the spotlight, it's the players from the formerly mentioned power conferences that usually have the name recognition on a national level.  It's also many of those players who go on to play at the professional level in the newly created league or for the Olympic team that will be making its debut in two years at the next summer games.

I was watching the game between Iowa and Iowa State the other night and it was an absolute slug fest.  I think in the short span of 15 to 20 minutes that I had it on, there were at least three or four home runs hit between the two sides.  That's part of what makes softball so exciting.  The fact that the bases are so much closer together also gives you a lot of strategic running compared to what you might see in baseball.  

It's funny the number of people who don't know what the difference is between the two sports,  and while there are many similarities, there are also definite nuances that make each one special unto itself.  

Right now Texas Tech is sitting in the top spot among the rankings with a record of 38-2 and something like a 17 game winning streak under their belt.  Oklahoma sits in the number 2 spot at 38-3 with Alabama close behind riding a 6 game winning streak and a 35-3 record.

Rounding out the top five we have Texas and then Nebraska.  I'm actually happy to see Nebraska doing so well. I might have to write a separate post about it, but they have been having a banger year as far as sports go.  

For the rest of the top ten we have Arkansas, Florida, UCLA, Florida State, and then Tennessee.

Arizona followed by Virginia Tech who Radford just faced the other day comprise the 11 and 12 spots with Texas A&M, Georgia, and Mississippi rounding out the top 15.

Finally, the rest of the field in order includes Duke, Oregon, LSU, Washington, Oklahoma State, Virginia, Central Flordia, Stanford, South Carolina, and Grand Canyon.  

Personally, I'd like to see a few more Big Ten schools in there, but what can you do.  It's actually a little surprising that Michigan isn't in the mix as they generally have a  pretty good team.  In fact, it doesn't look like they have even received any consolation votes this week.  

It's going to be interesting to see how much movement there is as we head into the conference tournaments and then the national tournament.

title.body:
Good morning warriors! Today I decide to post something different from my usual battles excapades.I did opened some foundations chests 🧰 and got lucky with some of the cards I opened.



**Splinterlands is no walk in the park, but that's what amps up the excitement.A winning strategy weighs stats, abilities, rulesets, mana caps, and beyond. That's why you must factor them all into your deck building. Toss in strong cards to boost your setups, and push hard to rack up as many victories as possible**! 🔥

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfSPs7mdQTibbmM14FAFzfH3G8oSxj9S92L9K6qezy6GQ/1767438490904.jpg)




I have been shuffling the battles between frontier and modern ranked.Opening of gifts/chests is something I always look forward to.Look at what i got today:

title.title: Facing War Without a Plan, But Not Alone
title.body:
It's a scary prompt really, one that I have never really thought of in all my thinking and desires to grow in life. I've never imagined having to be on a run to save my life and that of my family in a country that once felt safe enough for me not to run for my life. I know some parts of the country are already facing this somehow and it is scary. I've only read of wars in books or seen it in movies, I've never really tried to imagine how devastating or scary it will actually be to be present in a war zone fighting to come out of it alive. Honestly, I wish I won't need to answer this prompt and just kneel to pray to God that such a thing never happen because I have got no plan. But just in case! At a worst scenario! War breaks out... I'd be super clueless what to do in the first minutes into the war. I suppose, the news about the war outbreak will be everywhere before it actually does but if that were not the case here, it would be double of my clueless self going around with my family trying to get safety. ![file_000000003a64720a81ae8fdf9e4483c9.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/23uQveBsiu5pRPcwH1raSp4qoCoN96uygNJNMEDzECNXAsFPKQApdnawcmRXNhxwPpbe5.png) There's absolutely no way I'd be opting in to join the army as a way of being a good citizen to save my family, I don't even see how that would save them. Mind you, it is not that I know how exactly I'll save myself and family when I don't join the army but I feel it's way better to be with my family till the last moment should incase it all goes bad. My focus will definitely be on getting my family to somewhere safe, I believe my family will also have that as a priority so we would brainstorm together to provide the amount of safety we can come up with and flee from the war zones or hide safely to not get killed in the war. I can picture us go from clueless to frightened to building safety. There are no specific actions or measures I can share right now that I'll take to help my family survive but one thing I know for sure is, we would stick together as a family all the way. I've never been a fan of movie stories where they all go separate ways in hopes of being safe at last, many lose their lives that way. But we could stick together and play safe till it ends or we run away.

title.title: On the subject of differences in religious observances among Jews.
title.body:
![Magen Dovid.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23vhuRY5DYQEMKPpjdoKdTCrHHmmz7QV6wpEQHtwPs2953o4QBcmxkKwExJFAQdWoJnti.jpg)



During the Chol Hamoed period of Passover, the in-between days that lie sandwiched by the Yom Tovim or real holy days of the eight days of Passover, when things like work or commenting on social media are permitted, there was an interesting discussion on the X platform.  To roughly summarise this conversation, it was reacting to videos of young, secular background American Jews trying to mark Passover in their own way.  It was not in any way a method that would be acceptable to those who are Orthodox Jews.  These young Jews were eschewing the bread and other leavened products that are forbidden at Passover and were eating Matzah instead, but with non-kosher meat and with meat mixed with dairy products, something that caused conniptions among the more observant Orthodox Jews who viewed it.

Now these young Jews could be from one of the non-Orthodox paths within Judaism where the individual has the task of deciding what  parts of Judaism is meaningful to them and working out how each Mitzvot speaks to them as an individual and that includes the commandments regarding Kashrut.  This sort of Judaism whilst still Judaism because of its belief in one deity, is markedly different from Orthodox Judaism in its practises.  There will always be disagreements between those on the Orthodox Jewish path and those on the non-Orthodox path.  That’s just how it is and might be a subject for a future article.

On the other hand they could be Jews who have just had very poor teaching about Jewish thought and practises or who are hundreds of miles away from a Jewish community or shops.  No matter what of these scenarios is correct, the degree of opprobrium directed at them was a little more divisive than it should have been.  

These young Jews, who might have been trying to reconnect with Judaism from a very low knowledge point were relentlessly criticised by those who were more observant than them but others, including one of my favourite Jews on the X platform, The Jewish Meme Queen, took a more tolerant and I believe a better attitude to these young Jews.

She said:
*
I am a huge supporter of being respectful to all Jews, especially ones that are less observant than myself. Folks, they are watching us. They see the mean comments. Be kinder. Being orthodox doesn’t equal hating on other Jews.*

Spot on there Jewish Meme Queen.  I agree with her on this one.  The reasons I agree are two-fold.

The first is based on Jewish Meme Queen’s comments in that it is unkind of highly observant Jews to mock and criticise those who for various reasons are less observant of the many rules of Judaism than they are.  She’s correct in saying that the young Jews in the videos and those like them are watching the behaviour of their Orthodox critics and seeing their mean comments and making a decision about how they see Orthodox Judaism based on the negative behaviour of their Orthodox Jewish critics.  The conduct of these Orthodox Jews and the nature of their criticism might not have given a good impression of Orthodox Judaism to these young Jews. 

This sort of behaviour from Orthodox Jews is a baseless hatred of one Jew for another and that to me is not on.  I have vehement disagreements with other Jews over issues of politics for example, but I would rarely if ever cut them off totally over these issues. I might criticise them or call them out over some aspect of political idiocy but I would not completely cut them off as there’s always the chance that continued contact with them might create in them the desire for repentance/Teshuvah.  For example: The idiot Jew who bangs the drum for some foolish political current might one day in other circumstances and with the acquisition of more knowledge, choose to disassociate themselves from their former political idiocy.  There’s got to be a way back into the broader Jewish community for such people and it’s unlikely that ostracism will achieve that aim.  You’ve got to leave room for people to learn, to grow up, to examine themselves and what they believed and to follow a path of Teshuvah.

The second reason why I am in agreement with Jewish Meme Queen is because although these young secular-Jews are doing the completely wrong thing, they are doing it for the right reasons which is to connect or reconnect with their heritage.  They are trying to reconnect to the Passover story even though they are doing so from a very low knowledge base and doing the wrong thing because of that.  Those Orthodox Jews who criticise these secular Jews acknowledging Passover don’t seem to consider that these Jews doing what they see as the wrong thing, might be coming to the festival for the very first time, having been brought up in highly secular families and away from any Jewish community.

These secular Jews who get the strict religious rules of Passover wrong are not people who I will condemn.  They are trying to mark this momentous festival in the way that they choose or are able to or with the limited knowledge and access to the wider Jewish community that they have.

We as Jewish communities must make paths for people to come back to Judaism and especially make room for those of Jewish heritage who, since the 7/10 Pogrom, have started to acknowledge their heritage and wish to return to Judaism or become engaged with Judaism for the very first time in their lives.  For many Jews 7/10 wasn’t something that made some secular Jews want to hide their Jewish heritage deeper than they already did, but instead became something that made them acknowledge that they were Jews and therefore subject to the same threats as other Jews. The hatred exhibited on 7/10 backfired on those who carried it out, instead of driving diaspora Jews into hiding, it made them far more Jewish than they’d ever been before and has also created more Jews associating with the Jewish community (7/10 also sparked an uptick in non-Jews choosing Judaism but that’s a different story for later).  These Jews reached out to Judaism as a religious concept for support and wished to mark the Passover festival in the best way they could and they did so even though their knowledge was but random shards of information.  These secular Jews who may have been coming to the Passover story for the very first time in their lives, should not be condemned but instead welcomed and gently guided into more knowledge.

I have no right to stick my beak into other men’s souls or berate them about not following the Mitzvot/Commandments the correct way.  I’m not perfect and am in no position to lecture others, for example in the depths of winter I top up my coal fire on a Friday night with more coal and poke the fire even though the rules say I shouldn’t stoke the fire on Shabbat.  My thinking that this is a lesser sin than relighting the fire in the morning myself or have to bother our lovely Shabbas Goy firelighter to relight it.  Just as I’m not perfect neither are those Orthodox Jews who have criticised these secular Jews in this instance, we’ve all got failings, we all fall short, we all backslide, we all sin and we don’t always get things right.  I went to a very liberal community Seder this year and the spectrum of observance was amazing, it was so varied that it was like a microcosm of all the world’s Jews.  You had people like my wife and I who do our utmost to avoid Chametez/leaven during Passover and do the full changeover of plates thing.  However there were also Jews who at the Seder who popped out to the bar and came back with pints of Guinness and sat back down at the table, even though beer is considered as Chametz and therefore forbidden.

I did not think badly of such people.  Sure they were living their lives and doing what they did in a manner which is different from what I do, but the key point for me is that they turned up.  They could have stayed away and considered the Seder as ‘not for them’ but instead they turned up.  They turned up to hear the story of how Hashem rescued the Jewish people from Egyptian servitude and think for themselves how they would have acted if they were there in the place of the ancient Israelites.  On that day of Passover, these non-observant Jews turned up and stood with the Jewish people even though they were not what Orthodox Jews would class as observant, I could not condemn them for their lack of observance because these Jews turned up and were counted.

The online discussion regarding these possibly secular Jews and their interpretation of Passover and my experience of a very liberal Seder brings up for me a big question and it’s this.  Who is the better Jew the person who fulfils all that they can of the ritual commandments but who ignores all the ethical ones or the Jew who ignores the ritual commandments but who fulfils all the ethical commandments?  Ideally both would be present in the same person but not everyone is a Tzadik or a Rabbi or even religiously knowledgable, most are ordinary people struggling through life and they might be able to keep some of the ritual and some of the ethical commandment as best they can.  If they can keep both the majority of the ritual and ethical commandments then great, that’s admirable but there are a lot of Jews out there who try to do all the right moral things but are quite happy to chow down on a bacon sandwich. I’m certainly not going to dunk on these people as they are as Am Yisrael as anyone else but just do things a little differently and quite possibly not to my taste.

Don’t slag off the secular Jews when they get things wrong, talk to them with kindness and impart to them knowledge in a manner that doesn’t shame either the one who imparts knowledge nor the person who is receiving knowledge. We can do better than that.  We have enough enemies in the world already without creating more enemies by being divided by pointless and destructive internal baseless hatreds.

## El sueño del camarón

Sonia soñaba con contener una dotación eterna de camarones. Le gustaban tanto que investigó la forma de tener una granja de ellos, pero terminaba comiéndose los toros antes de que se pudieran reproducir.

 -Sonia comandos camarones son como insectos-

-Lo sé, son como cucarachas del mar, pero es que son tan deliciosos-

Sonia caminaba tranquila cerca de los alrededores de su casa cuando una multitud de camarones gigantes la rodeó, entre ellos también había muchos animales similares a insectos. Este  parecía el fin para Sonia.  Pero ella no se asustó. Se recogió el vestido con ambas manos y comenzó a comérselos a todos con gran gusto.

Unos días más tarde, Sonia empezó a concertyrn uno de ellos...

## The Shrimp's Dream

Sonia dreamed of having an endless supply of shrimp. She loved them so much that she researched how to have a shrimp farm, but she always ended up eating the shrimp before they could reproduce.

\

Sonia was walking peacefully near her house when a swarm of giant shrimp surrounded her. Among them were many insect-like creatures. This seemed like the end for Sonia. But she wasn't scared. She gathered her dress with both hands and began to eat them all with great relish. A few days later, Sonia began to conjure one of them...

Poor John. It's not easy being a pirate. People make assumptions about your character.

I don't understand Hollywood's weird fascination with pirates. They sail around killing people and taking their stuff. How did they become the romantic anti-heroes?

Actually, Fantomah doesn't know a lot about the world. She's the guardian of Africa and it is unclear if that responsibility extends to the coastlines of Africa. If it does, then most of her pirate experience would be dealing with Somali pirates. Of course, most of those have resettled in Minnesota now, so again, she probably hasn't had many run-ins lately.

Gold necklace with a blue topaz stone. Really accents her hair and her eyes. Yes, he's a pirate, but c'mon, that's a pretty thoughtful gift, right?

Maybe this is the beginning of a serious romance? Robert Louis Stevenson is rolling over in his grave right now.

title.title: Fresh Catch: A Simple Blessing to Be Grateful For  🙏❤
title.body:
Hello everyone!

Hope all are safe and well! 😊❤🙏

Today, I just want to share another simple blessing in our life. Something that may look ordinary to others, but for me, it is already a big reason to be thankful. 😊❤

We are blessed again with fresh food on our table. I feel so grateful for my parents who continue to catch fish for us. Their effort and hard work never go unnoticed. Even in the simplest way, they always make sure that we have something to eat every day.❤

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPoqVKft7kD3bZbjMyczVGLwDiMqYBmotnotPfXNpx7aJ/20260410_092247.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPnYFdHVifTUv2sB21z56UFgPpg2muLTQPrMAL8Q5Uo3b/20260409_092727.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPBj5B3VysssraKL86g4WFKUBo6iqZc2Tqz8hNJnx2w9Z/20260403_195418.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNqh2cZew68tweCsYASS1GxMrqxqoaftTjY4arkx6zDpC/20260403_195435.jpg)

Seeing these fresh catches reminds me of how life in a simple home can still be full of blessings. Not everyone gets to have fresh fish straight from the sea, and I truly appreciate that we have this kind of provision. ❤🙏

It’s been three days already that only the three of us are at home: my father, my mother, and me. Because of that, the fish that my parents bring home is more than enough for us. Sometimes, we even have extra that we can save for the next meal. 😊❤

In moments like this, I realize how important family is. We may not have everything, but we have each other. We share meals together, we support one another, and we continue to live each day with gratitude in our hearts.❤🙏

I also admire my parents even more. Despite their age and the challenges of daily life, they still go out and do what they can to provide for us. Their strength and dedication inspire me. It reminds me that love is not always shown through words, but through actions and sacrifices.😊❤

This simple blessing also made me reflect on how often we take things for granted. Food on the table, especially fresh and enough for everyone, is already something to be thankful for. There are many people who struggle to have even one proper meal a day.

That’s why I choose to appreciate moments like this. A simple catch of fish becomes a reminder of God’s provision. It may not be grand, but it is enough and sometimes, ***enough*** is already a blessing. 😊❤🙏

As I continue my journey, especially after everything I’ve been through these past days with my injury, I am learning to focus more on the good things, no matter how small they seem.😊❤

Today, my heart is full not because of something big, but because of something simple, real, and meaningful. 😊❤🙏

Have a Blessed Friday everyone! 😀😀😀💖💖💖

Thank You Lord for the blessings and love!

Be grateful in every little/simple things and you’ll find happiness you ever wanted! 😀😀😀

Everyday is worth to be grateful of!

Praying for the safety and wellness of all.

Heal Our Land Oh God!

Lovelots,
@shikika

title.title: Visiting Punta La Cruz Beach, Venezuela / Visita A La Playa De Punta La Cruz, Venezuela [ENG-ESP]
title.body:
>

Hi, Hivers.

Hey everyone, how are you all doing? I hope you're doing great. I wanted to share these photos from my trip to Punta La Cruz Beach—I don't think you'll want to miss this story. Well, this is where we pick up from where we left off at the Guanta pier, Boats leave from here for different beaches, as I mentioned. We were heading to Punta La Cruz, which is inside Mochima National Park. It was a cloudy day, but I was hoping the sun would come out. Let’s say we left around 11 a.m. from the pier. We had arrived early but were waiting for passengers. On the way, you can see a cement factory, which is also a source of pollution for the area. Once we were underway, we began to see the spectacular turquoise contrast of the water. Let’s say the trip takes about 10 minutes. During the high season, we’re told that there are boats constantly coming and going; on the way, one was heading back to the pier. By the time we got there, we took some great photos regardless of the weather. Luckily, there was a restaurant there that happened to be open that day, and we ate some dogfish empanadas—what a treat! Empanadas from eastern Venezuela are known for their sweet dough. They told us we had to be back at the pier by 5 p.m., but we enjoyed that little slice of paradise. I took the first few photos and then went for a swim, hahaha. The best moments are meant to be enjoyed—that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t take photos, I give this beach a 10 out of 10—I really liked it, and best of all, there were few people there; we had the place to ourselves. I hope you enjoyed this post; see you later. Thank you all Note: These photos were taken from my phone and edited In: Canva

>Separators
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eve66/Eo1xMomvJcSXykCUmKVLbudYQNVwyFPkvdXB9WDpP1BhiWPr69fWLfYJPZNmTQzBFdH.png

Hola Hivers.

Hola mi gente como se encuentran espero que muy bien, quería compartir estas fotos de la visita a la playa punta la cruz no creo que te quieras perder este relato.
Bueno esta sería la continuación desde el punto de partida que era el muelle o embarcadero de Guanta, aquí salen lanchas para distintas playas como les dije, íbamos a punta la cruz que está dentro del Parque Nacional Mochima, el día estaba nublado yo tenía esperanza que saliera el sol, digamos que salimos a eso de las 11 am de allí del muelle habíamos llegado temprano pero esperando por pasajeros, en camino se ve una industria cementera que a la vez es un factor contaminante para el lugar, ya en camino se comienza a ver ese contraste color turquesa del agua algo espectacular, digamos que el paso son como unos 10 minutos calculando, en un día de temporada nos comentan que eso es lancha que vienen y van en el camino iba una de regreso al muelle.
Hasta que llegamos al lugar, unas fotografías de la mejor manera posible no importa el clima que estuviera, estaba un restaurant allí por suerte ese día abrieron, y nos comimos unas empanadas de cazón que delicia las empanadas del oriente de venezuela se caracterizan por su sabor dulce en la masa, nos avisaron que a las 5 de la tarde era el regreso al muelle pero disfrutamos de ese paraíso yo tome las primeras fotos y luego me fui a bañar jajaja los mejores momentos se disfrutan no quiere decir que no se tome foto, a esta playa le doy 10 de 10 me gustó mucho y lo mejor de todo habían pocas personas teníamos el lugar para nosotros, espero les haya gustado esta publicación, nos vemos luego.

Gracias a todos.

Hello, Fellow Travelers

I immediately set off for Bartın, my hometown, which I hadn’t visited in a long time, after receiving a wedding invitation from my best friend. I’ve mentioned before that I’m from Bartın.  As a child of the Black Sea, setting foot on the land where I was born once again truly excited me. I was absolutely spellbound by the ever-changing landscape of the Lava Columns in Güzelcehisar, Bartın. 

[//]:# (!worldmappin 41.63196 lat 32.18019 long  d3scr)

>Merhabalar Gezcinci Dostlarım

>Uzun zamandır gidemediğim memleketim Bartın'a en sevdiğim arkadaşımın gönderdiği düğün davetiyesiyle hemen yola çıktım. Buradan sizlere Bartın'lı olduğumu söylemiştim.  Bir Karadeniz çocuğu olarak doğduğum topraklara tekrar ayak basmak beni açıkçası heyecanlandırdı. Özellikle Bartın Güzelcehisar'da yer alan Lav Sütunlarının değişen coğrafyası karşısında adeta büyülendim. 

![IMG20260401152605.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPVYMPxuVpUF14JsqCTtMhzefJauxBXF8Y2BZ4jsfq6Qr/IMG20260401152605.jpg)

When I was young, my siblings and I used to visit Güzelcehisar often. Located about 40 minutes from the center of Bartın, the town is a small, charming seaside village. The Black Sea’s distinctive scent is immediately noticeable as soon as you step onto the shore. The myriad shades of green and the sea’s wild yet equally captivating nature are clearly visible in Güzelcehisar. On the way from Bartın to Güzelcehisar, the Black Sea’s famous winding roads, with lush green mountains on one side and the deep blue Black Sea on the other—a sea that, despite its small size, evokes a sense of infinity...

>Güzelcehisar'a gençliğimde kardeşlerimle beraber sık sık giderdik. Bartın merkeze yaklaşık 40 dakika uzaklıkta olan kasaba, küçük şirin bir sahil kenarıdır. Karadeniz'in o kendine has kokusu, kıyıya indiğinizde hemen fark edilir. Yeşilin binbir tonu,  denizin hırçın ama bir o kadar da büyüleyici hali Güzelcehisar'da çok net görülüyor.  Bartın'dan Güzelcehisar'a giderken Karadeniz'in o meşhur kıvrımlı yolları, bir yanda yemyeşil dağlar, diğer tarafta ise ufakta sonsuzluk hissi veren masmavi Karadeniz...


![IMG20260401152503.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZGocMrAtZx8y2taXhDamrjtctHfZvNyd7irK43QykWvS/IMG20260401152503.jpg)


![IMG20260401152213.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPc3LsYc2j94fCWbJ9difEsaAENtJWpc3jxCLc1NjNZvt/IMG20260401152213.jpg)


![IMG20260401150133.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcMcrFdSaMU6csyjNH7mopx9bBjmkUvtvG7v68fdUh2UJ/IMG20260401150133.jpg)


![IMG20260401150445.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeYxBgcPW4VPNUYqhHZuVQugga82GTMJfHiBdc1SRP64D/IMG20260401150445.jpg)

As we approached Güzelcehisar, the landscape of the town suddenly changed. You leave behind those crowded stone houses and step into nature. The road narrows a bit. You make your way through the greenery, now shrouded in silence. I had come here three or four times years ago. But I had never felt quite like I do now—as if I were on a journey of discovery. You reach the town by descending winding, narrow roads from the side of a mountain. When you reach the bottom, you come upon a round, stone-paved square where a flower-adorned round sign bearing the name “Güzelcehisar” greets you.

>Güzelcehisar'a yaklaştıkça, şehrin coğrafyası bir anda değişiyor. O kalabalık taşlı evlerinden sıyrılıp, doğanın içine giriş yapıyorsunuz. Yol biraz daralıyor. Sessizliğe bürünen yeşilliğin içinde ilerliyorsunuz. Seneler öncesinde buraya üç dört kez gelmiştim. Ama şimdiki gibi, kendimi  adeta bir keşif yolculuğunda ki gibi hissetmemiştim.  Kasabaya, bir dağ yamacından kıvrımlı ve dar yollardan  aşağıya inilerek ulaşılıyor. Aşağıya indiğinizde, Taşlı yuvarlak bir meydanda Güzelcehisar'in adının yazdığı çiçekli yuvarlak bir tabela ile karşılaşıyorsunuz.


![IMG20260401144933.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdjYgotWuKyc9LKKb39DBEYkTb3aqriQdRFavtev6SUvV/IMG20260401144933.jpg)


![IMG20260401145024.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSt8cTLH1cCAsmFbWeo3HRGgBTsG6F88V7ioSHEXj7gFb/IMG20260401145024.jpg)


![IMG20260401144749.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYm65QXgnPWrrGJUUaqtxEzKRVBX7LCfSaRgShMaWcWsm/IMG20260401144749.jpg)


![IMG20260401145621.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma7wqEkaNTi5NzbwaGoEFzT1EAvETX9cYXV2DgeRRm4fS/IMG20260401145621.jpg)

To allow visitors to walk along the entire coastline, they’ve built a boardwalk made of wooden planks. The sea looks serene and calm. Behind the coastline, there are open, unpaved areas covered with green grass. Dotted across these areas are a few detached houses, as well as guesthouses and businesses that haven’t yet opened for the season. As you head inland from the coast toward the hillside, you come across neighborhoods and villages. 

>Kıyı şeridini baştan sona kadar kıyıdan yürüyerek görebilmek için ahşap tahtalardan oluşan şeritli bir yol yapmışlar. Deniz masum ve sakin duruyor. Kıyı şeridinin gerisinde bir bölümü yeşil çimenlerden oluşmuş, topraklı boş araziler var. Bu arazilerin üstünde birkaç  müstakil evle, henüz sezonunu açmamış olan pansiyon ve işletme bulunuyor. Kıyı kesiminden içlere yamaca doğru gidildiğinde mahalle ve köylere rastlıyorsunuz. 


![IMG20260401145802.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWkaNFTgueMK2Amr6g4fCnWrCfiDyWeWY7eLiJrm5CiFz/IMG20260401145802.jpg)


![IMG20260401145757.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTZMhdfmJvQH83fnhcyLMDGmddXqhosBX4iknTPF5zRH7/IMG20260401145757.jpg)


![IMG20260401145655.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdX9U81XNTv3gtTDheywYXb5b353SdMWeMoqAc5z1GrMc/IMG20260401145655.jpg)


![IMG20260401145111.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfZXhpkKRd2qW2QV7dftBszHTHHDpM11MGbu8tJUUh1yc/IMG20260401145111.jpg)


![IMG20260401150052.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbWTKTKrQJ28AUiKu3LJFvmfHjMNqn7wuFR4nKLJNCryn/IMG20260401150052.jpg)

The Lava Columns are located at the very beginning of the coastline on the left side. The Lava Columns consist of rock formations unlike anything seen before, rising from the sea like a wall. The coastline stretches for approximately 1 km. The beach is smooth and fine-grained. The rocky cliffs, which begin at the western end of the beach, extend from the coast all the way to the beaches of Güzelcehisar and Mugada. Estimated to be approximately 80 million years old, these columns become one of the most visited spots in the region, especially during the summer. 

>Lav Sütunları kıyı şeridinin sol tarafında en başta bulunuyor. Lav Sütunları denizden duvar gibi yükselen daha önce hiç görülmemiş kaya şekillerinden oluşuyor. Sahilin yaklaşık  1 km'lik kıyı şeridi var. Kumsalı pürüzsüz ve ince yapıdadır.  Kumsalın batı ucundan başlayan kayalıklar kıyıdan Güzelcehisar ve Mugada sahiline kadar uzanmaktadır. Yaklaşık 80 milyon yıllık olduğu tahmin edilen bu sütunlar, yazın özellikle bölgede en çok ziyaret edilen noktalarından biri haline geliyor. 



![IMG20260401152652.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmb42KUoUbmF3nUEshgQckVYX9mcCpVF1K8s2ZTYZXz8ju/IMG20260401152652.jpg)


![IMG20260401152514.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ3iKwyrosuUj6TfaajRN2duXrat5N1KBQTD46TmQ9hD9/IMG20260401152514.jpg)


![IMG20260401152301.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQyge7E9ZKbWGEowNGV9AZSDcb2sHJMiKEsr52MPsWsFS/IMG20260401152301.jpg)


![IMG20260401152722.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZ3eQuNaFEr2jA711W8jvH4ZxYEACA9vAASu3852fL4cj/IMG20260401152722.jpg)


The sand on the beach is so smooth and pure that the damp grains on the ground seem to be bound together. It makes you want to run barefoot from one end to the other. It’s so perfect for writing that you feel like scribbling something down. This sand is very different from the sand of the Aegean and Mediterranean; there isn’t a single pebble to be found. The waves lapping at the shore meet the Black Sea’s delicate, pure sand. The powerful, rhythmic sound the waves make as they crash against the shore can be felt throughout the walk. As the wind blows gently now and then, the sound of waves from afar blends with nature’s fresh, salty, and complex scent, instilling a sense of peace within you. 

>Sahilin kumu o kadar pürüzsüz o saf ki; yerde nemlenmiş kum taneleri birbirine bağlanmış gibi görünüyor. İnsanın bir uctan bir uca çıplak ayakla koşası geliyor. Yazı yazmaya o kadar müsait ki insanın içinden bir şeyler karalayası geliyor. Bu kum Ege ve Akdeniz kumlarından çok farklı, üzerinde hiçbir çakıl taşı bulunmuyor. Kıyıya yanaşan dalgalar, Karadeniz'in o narin ve saf kumuyla karşılaşıyor.  Dalgaların kıyıya vururken çıkardığı o güçlü ve ritmik ses, yürüyüş boyunca hissediliyor.  Rüzgar arada hafif hafif eserken uzaklardan  gelen dalga sesleri, doğanın o taze tuzlu ve karışık kokusuyla birleşip, insanın içine bir huzur işletiyor. 

​
![IMG20260401151614.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZRBnxKxLWtYh8EW4mpRMPz6bKVJUgBJDBamZmhJ5R5Nd/IMG20260401151614.jpg)


![IMG20260401151611.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSF3N3XKU33jWco34ghiBcXN6D8aVWBBwR5gkX9Eic7e9/IMG20260401151611.jpg)


![IMG20260401151414.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmf2DVe5xoCukocoobLcto2Jk5WJTEtNJZpRaGP3XyEbD5/IMG20260401151414.jpg)

![IMG20260401151759.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfTzPbzZYu4fSTbhCQ5vRiwpeqoih1H5tGb59GrQ1ky1H/IMG20260401151759.jpg)


![IMG20260401151639.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSfak2TYfGMA2uhJcCeLxrXKGh9Hz5pXnDcoNd1jUWpsR/IMG20260401151639.jpg)

The wooden promenade along the shore of Güzelcehisar seems to have become an integral part of the town. At both ends, slightly elevated circular viewing areas have been created. As you walk along the path, there are short stairways leading down to the beach. Small cabanas have been placed along the way for those who wish to rest. 

>Güzelcehisar'ın kıyısındaki ahşap yürüyüş alanıyla kasabayla özleşmiş gibi duruyor. Her iki uçta, hafif yükseklikte yuvarlak  seyir alanı oluşturulmuş. Yol boyunca yürüdüğünüzde, sahile inilen kısa merdivenli geçiş alanları mevcut. Dinlenmek isteyenler için küçük kabinli oturma alanları koymuşlar. 


![IMG20260401150515.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSAu3dpSF4RVqd48meAsrbavtXgPnZUgCLkq1X4K6kxdT/IMG20260401150515.jpg)


![IMG20260401152351.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNyyNo8no2PvDWtsATXvk2HWDJTvDbSP4wYUrCBp1bjjn/IMG20260401152351.jpg)


![IMG20260401152319.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYYazdvkVa1zXnz5UFGxp1oZ38ivUeuRruC1MsNPn2jyg/IMG20260401152319.jpg)

![IMG20260401150034.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVBWrRD8VsxXLaJnSxoLHBxaqUdTxNV94JavNyrCrSRpy/IMG20260401150034.jpg)


![IMG20260401145820.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdJJS4qnfPdXA6jdgVZeKWh1yb1vWgZGXpB9i3sSyhw5d/IMG20260401145820.jpg)

![IMG20260401145116.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY8EKED1TU7qpJSffbVFrMU9fHbyDLkrDdwZFZA1Ntu4s/IMG20260401145116.jpg)

I walked along the wooden boardwalks all the way to the water’s edge to examine these columns up close. These columns stand as if they were giant stone columns carefully arranged by nature. Giant rock formations, reminiscent of geometric shapes like hexagons and pentagons, are lined up side by side, rising from the seabed and extending along the shore. As the waves crash against these columns, a frothy spectacle unfolds that evokes a sense of harmony within. Beyond being a natural wonder, the Basalt Columns also demonstrate just how powerful and profound time is. Standing there and gazing at the towering rock formations, even the thought that this formation took millions of years to create fills one with an indescribable feeling. 

>Ahşaptan yapılmış yürüyüş yollarında en kıyıya kadar yürüyerek bu sütunları yakından inceledim. Bu sütunlar sanki doğanın özenle dizmiş olduğu dev taş kolonları gibi duruyor. Geometrik şekillerden altıgen ve beşgeni anımsatan dev kayalıklar yan yana dizilerek denizin dibinden kıyı boyunca yükselerek ilerlemişler. Dalgalar bu sütunlara çarptıkça insanın içinde bir ahenk duygusu uyandıran köpüklü bir şölen oluşuyor.  Lav Sütunları bir doğa harikasının olmasının yanında zamanın ne kadar güçlü ve derin olduğunu da gösteriyor.  Orada durup öylece yükselen kayalıklara baktığınızda bu oluşumun milyonlarca yıl olduğunu düşünmek bile insana tarifsiz bir duygu veriyor. 

​

![IMG20260401145840.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcxugCf3DVoakVFEELRmwhjKmPjKVHiQFkwFXrBQEkARD/IMG20260401145840.jpg)


![IMG20260401145929.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTthovfkGK17x8qzthnWUBD7JAyP6S2tqsHUjgw9wN3y3/IMG20260401145929.jpg)

![IMG20260401150149.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd5hYU8nbZzAorrqQkSsK69g2nD6Rx7sgT3GdejMePPAS/IMG20260401150149.jpg)

![IMG20260401152729.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWzPt5geqLZqZZv249EMtk5nNMTmjEY5Kd1G79XYgAMsQ/IMG20260401152729.jpg)

![IMG20260401152029.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSEDNYGTCsESt9ne9pcn5o8LBHmwFDX6v4Fa16EhdZoof/IMG20260401152029.jpg)

Of course, Güzelcehisar isn’t famous just for its iconic lava columns... The warmth, kindness, and distinctive Black Sea hospitality of the people living in the village are among the most important elements that define the spirit of this region.  I’m not saying this just because I’m from the Black Sea region. I’m saying this as someone who has lived here and seen it firsthand. The Black Sea’s cuisine, with its unique flavors, and the cultural values of a people living in harmony with nature also make this town and this region special. 

>Güzelcehisar sadece bu meşhur Lav Sütunlarıyla ünlü değil elbette... Köyde yaşayan insanların sıcakkanlılığı, yardımseverliği ve Karadeniz'e özel misafirperverliğine de bu yörenin ruhunu tamamlayan en önemli detaylarından biridir.  Bunu kendim Karadenizli olduğum için söylemiyorum. Bizzat yaşayan ve gören biri olarak söylüyorum.  Karadeniz'in mutfağı o kendine has lezzetleri ve doğayla iç içe yaşam süren halkın kültürel değerleri de bu kasabayı ve bu yöreyi özel kılıyor. 

![IMG20260401150139.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeEGorFQt9NKtrnGrmXEaJA3Wp4Z5kkmgQ2ipBwLFwWdH/IMG20260401150139.jpg)

​
![IMG20260401151030.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPCia5Kfe8emx8RT7sV2Fo4L8oEdNNjDYeKk9Ur7HnGTu/IMG20260401151030.jpg)



![IMG20260401155659.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWpmx8BkphkAfGaenBEtg48dSqR8HzPsmgLPErW4CwStz/IMG20260401155659.jpg)


![IMG20260401155807.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZDFbftdY85PuVnkV7igvqfi26YMHGbzXupRnWcy7QLJ4/IMG20260401155807.jpg)

![IMG20260401152133.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNRawnfEVnNCAJhbMJVspP5Mp3G6JYXbN2mwHvGJZeyFi/IMG20260401152133.jpg)

As I bid farewell to such a beautiful natural wonder in my own homeland, a bittersweet ache wells up inside me.  Perhaps some journeys aren’t about seeing a place. They are journeys of longing that take us back to our childhood in the very lands where we were born. In Güzelcehisar,  that feeling was a treasure hidden deep within my heart. Wishing everyone a wonderful weekend. 

>Kendi memleketimde böylesine güzel bir doğa harikası güzelliklerden ayrılırken, içimde buruk bir acı oluşuyor.  Belki de bazı yoculuklar bir yer görmek için değildir. Kendi doğduğumuz topraklarda bizi çocukluğumuza götüren hasret yolculalıklarımızdır. Güzelcehisar'da  benim içim o his kalbimin derinliklerinde saklı kalmış bir hazineydi. Herkese iyi hafta sonları dilerim. 

​
![Passenger777.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRJC4twuaVWbv36cmAFG8Gc1LTcYxXa4qaoW3kqzgJRx8/Passenger777.gif)

>Instead, people seem destined to become more emotional and use their feelings to inform their behaviours, even if they are invalid, misaligned, and ultimately in service to creating wealth for the few.

That's seems like the default state of everyone, making emotional decisions, I mean. And it's had to change. The leopard can't change its spots, like they say. 

Though I believe something can be done to help us act by logic instead of emotions, most of the time. But never all the time.

Like I've always said, man's greed is the primary obstacle to good governance in the society. Because of it, people who get into public offices, do so for their own pockets. 

There are still a few selfless people though, who could govern primarily for the welfare of the masses, but getting them into political offices is just the problem.

 And you know what? A good number of them also turn to greediness when they taste political power.
