links.title: My stats continue to insist that walking is just as good as running
links.body:
Who knows if these watches are actually correct or not.  A study I recently read came to the conclusion that **all manufacturers** of sport watches are incorrect with their calculations but I think that it would be unreasonable to expect some little thing on your wrist to give perfectly accurate results when the only way to truly determine such figures is to be hooked up to all sorts of scientific gosmers that measure so many things that your body is doing.

But I have read a lot of literature about how walking burns just as much (from a caloric perspective) as running does, it just takes a lot longer.

On days where I don't really feel like I have it in me to do a bunch of cardio I will still go for a very long walk because of the fact that when I was seriously overweight, I lost a ton of weight by doing very little else other than simply walking because I was so fat that I couldn't really do anything else. 

<center> https://darebee.com/images/guides/walking-jogging-running.jpg
[src](https://darebee.com/images/guides/walking-jogging-running.jpg)</center>

I don't necessarily believe all the things that I read online because these days it seems like no matter what you read someone is trying to tell you to do it differently and they also want to sell you something at the same time.  I know from my own experience in my own life that just walking really will help you to lose weight if that is your objective.   

The type of walking I was doing the other day though, this would be considered extremely relaxed, probably a bit too relaxed. 

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tRxWjyDmdTujv2ckSmEg7RHgqj19wAeVBRSRb3GmkYteMJ7r9BwSQoETuR8w7LCxPGB.png)
</center>

330 calories isn't a lot, especially for someone like me that can replace those in about 20 minutes with a couple of beers. It's more than zero though and it's always kind of nice for mental health as well as physical health to get out of the house and be in the closest thing this enormous city has to nature.  

<center>  
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23tGTmQYESYmtRYmsKs548LmnrwAXy11Nhc6QcdyRJtuvc3zxUXk3uX6kYmAyfDWciVGj.png)
</center>

The heart rate is kind of a joke honestly, It is rare for me to not break a sweat at all no matter what I am doing, but it's more effort than I would have been putting forth if I was at my desk or sitting on the sofa.  

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/Eo6BEM3TkcuB6dQJT57HfX4dqeoeR8YPcfV4XbgkNMx7a56pTiPF9Aqks4ooJUg6C7e.png)
</center>

At no point in time was I ever pushing it even a little bit and I just alternated between listening to the sounds of the city, which isn't that bad on these walking paths, and also listening to a podcast.  Seriously folks, if you are trying to lose a bit of weight and you already have a show that you like to listen to, why not combine the two?   Lately I have been listening to something like a pub quiz and I always end up learning some things that I didn't know before.  

When I run a 5k, my watch tells me that my caloric burn is a little bit higher than this, but not very much.  

> While calorie counts are useful for tracking long-term trends, they should be interpreted as directional signals rather than precise metrics

What that means to me is that the data your watch gives you at the end of whatever activity you are doing should not be taken literally and are not an accurate measurement of what you are actually doing.  While the algorithyms are actually quite complex and take into account your individual age, weight, height, and history of exercise that it knows, the general consensus is that all sport watches, even the expensive ones, are 25-40% incorrect about what the actual calories burned are.

That's just fine by me but clinical trials with really expensive and accurate (so they say) equipment also has shown that running vs jogging vs walking burns a pretty close amount of calories based on the **distance traveled**.  There would be exceptions of course such as seriously pushing your heart rate close to maximum, but for normal people like you and I, there is too much risk of injury to really try to be doing that on a regular basis.

here is a picture that will never not be funny to me.
<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/normie.fitness/23t77FUKhLZMxmAV3ni7LG1Jf1ty8gfE3pNT2TVpAWgiBnxNvpU6KFA9j924VJV9uKA7w.png)
</center>

I always get a little chuckle out of my stats after I forgot to wear my watch for like half a day and since the computers don't really know how to determine if it was plugged up or not as far as the watch is concerned I have been siting in one place with no heartbeat at all of hours and hours.

links.title: Beneath Calm Waters
links.body: > In an almost cinematic scene, the clouds were slowly moving through the dark and blueish sky. The weather is clear to the extent that it feels un-natural. Standing on the shores, looking at the small part of the sea that divides the town in two halves. The half where everyone is at. And the other unknown half with hills all over the place, and people from a different culture that we only know little of. The distance is not far. But, there are so many stories about this sea. Standing next to the most recent broken boat, looking across to the other half. Wondering, could it be true? Could it be true what is said about this sea? There is something creepy that probably hides beneath the calm sea waters. It remains unanswered and unsolved riddle. So much of darkness is hidden within the beauty of this place. The last of the brave men had given up on crossing the sea. Leaving the rest of the people in town with questions about the place. Just like so many things around them. Maybe, only time will tell and one day will uncover all of this mystery. # PT

>

Em uma cena quase cinematográfica, as nuvens moviam-se lentamente pelo céu escuro e azulado. O tempo estava tão claro que parecia antinatural. De pé na margem, observando a pequena porção de mar que dividia a cidade em duas metades. A metade onde todos estavam. E a outra metade desconhecida, com colinas por toda parte e pessoas de uma cultura diferente, da qual pouco sabíamos. A distância não era grande. Mas havia tantas histórias sobre esse mar.

Parado ao lado do barco quebrado mais recente, olhando para a outra metade, me perguntava: será verdade? Será que tudo o que dizem sobre esse mar é verdade? Algo sinistro provavelmente se escondia sob as águas calmas. Permanece um enigma sem resposta e sem solução. Tanta escuridão se esconde por trás da beleza deste lugar. O último dos bravos homens desistiu de atravessar o mar, deixando o resto dos habitantes da cidade com perguntas sobre o lugar, assim como sobre tantas outras coisas ao seu redor. Talvez, só o tempo dirá e um dia desvendará todo esse mistério.

Questa mattina mi alzo per tempo, per andare a pulire l'ufficio assicurativo, mi preparo, faccio tutto quello che dovevo fare, arriva il momento che devo prendere le chiavi in questione, due chiavi solamente, quella del portone d'ingresso e quella della porta blindata...

Panico, smarrimento profondo, terrore, non c'erano, nulla, altri 8 mazzi e mazzetti di chiavi distinti, ma quello non c'era, inizio a cercarlo freneticamente, in qua e in là, niente, attivo il cervello (si fa per dire...), ancora nulla, vado nell'appartamento dei miei, niente, faccio mente locale, penso al percorso che posso aver fatto mercoledì scorso, due giorni fa, quando sicuramente ho utilizzato l'ultima volta quelle chiavi, vado nello scooter, vano sotto sella e bauletto, nulla di nulla, piccolo lampo di genio, mi precipito al bar vicino all'assicurazione, dove ho fatto colazione una volta terminato il lavoro di mercoledì, nulla anche lì, accidenti, prendo che ho visto la mia Cucciolotta proprio mercoledì mattina, al volo, magari le ho lasciate lassù, ma lei sta dormendo, rientro mestamente a casa, ormai non vado più a lavorare, perché si sta facendo tardi, un ultimo microscopico spiraglio, mi ricorda che ho usato la mia vettura proprio mercoledì, e rammento pure di aver messo dei mazzi di chiavi nel vano portaoggetti dell'auto, apro la portiera e il vano, nulla, sollevo per puro scrupolo il poeta documenti della macchina ed erano rotolate lì sotto, fine dell'incubo...

links.title: IPL Boundary Blackjack - Round 3, Match 2 - RR v RCB
links.body:
2 days and 2 last balls finishes. Can we get 3 squeaky bums in a row? 

Today's match sees 2 of the early pace setters Rajasthan Royals and RCB go head to head both with 100% records in IPL 2026. Someone will be leaving without that this evening... 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/talesfrmthecrypt/23uFM2bGpTyCX2CKjpRPib6xCZJqcfEj32Csqwt61NwFpnDQM2geVyaCkM8REfhXz3iSi.png)


The vagaries of the fixture list mean that this is just RCB's 3rd game of the tournament despite the fact that the defenders champions kicked-off proceedings a fortnight ago. Does that relative lack of cricket impact their chances against an RR side that has played 3 won 3 in the last 11 days? 

Batting wise, the Rajasthan top 3 continue to look in fine form. At least 1 of them has come off in every game so far this season and usually to devastating effect. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/talesfrmthecrypt/23u6WYBC3zbcCCJxcXTDKqAbgtz89hTqcp5grWvzmYELxA4NZY8d7gsb5zM7MBe3vj28R.png)


On the other side, you've got RCB's seamers who have taken 3 wickets in the powerplay in both games so far. 

It's a similar situation for RCB with their top order all having made runs coming into a contest with the Royal's seamers who have looked particularly effective on this wicket in Guwahati. 

They had Mumbai 3 down in a shortened powerplay here last time out while CSK were 4 down. 

It seems obvious to say then that the powerplay is going to crucial! On both sides it feels like a case of unstoppable force meeting immovable object and something will have to give. 

Where RCB have a clear advantage is that their middle come into this match with form too. Patidar at number 4 has looked in supreme touch while Tim David's exploits against CSK took his from a good score to an insurmountable one. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/talesfrmthecrypt/23uFu4kWGS4K9CPV14v3TXK1y8e1feWFCYNpMpJBMCnWdJYaFst8nVBZoH75Uw8FGU7Cv.png)


RR don't have that luxury. They may have played a game more than their rivals tonight but both matches here at Guwahati last 12 and 11 overs respectively so we've yet to really see whether they have the strength and depth in their middle and lower to rebuild if and when they lose early wickets. 

On the RCB front, the biggest question mark is over their defensive capabilities with the ball. They've out smashed their opponents in 2 home games at a venue where it's difficult if not impossible to really defend. 

This is their first away trip and potentially a different type of challenge for their bowling unit. Based on what we've seen here to date, you'd expect the likes of Duffy and Bhuvi to enjoy the new ball on this surface. If they are taken apart for Rajasthan's 2 lefties at the top of the order then what's plan B? 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/talesfrmthecrypt/23wMyxYuHajryavsLEYw2zeb6AWPgQr2vrEMRpCcN4f4GnyHmsaJzeV3EpkYab3pxQfTJ.png)


It's still very early days in the tournament and as you can tell from the blog above, there are a lot of questions still to be answered!

# IPL Boundary Blackjack Round 3 

It feels like after 2 rounds of IPL Boundary Blackjack, people are starting to get a hang of the predictions. 

No one went bust in match 1 of round 3 although it was a close call for the top 2 who were indebted to Choudhary's miracle innings at the end to get them over the line. 

Today's game could be tough to call on many accounts and there are a few thunder storms rolling around the Assam region still which are worth keeping an eye on ahead of this game starting.

links.title: MY LIFE IF MONEY IS NOT A PROBLEM
links.body:
Good morning, everyone. You are welcome to my blog.

If I ever reach a point where money would not be a problem for me, the first thing I would want to do is to buy freedom. Not just freedom for traveling anywhere I want to go but the kind of freedom that would remove all daily pressures and make my life decisions much better. Ultimately, I would want to get a very comfortable home for my family and myself, a place where I can call home, a place that has peace and fulfills all my basic needs. A home is not just a building, but a space where you can relax, think clearly, grow, and actually rest.



 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQgrBJaqPRPJvSyVX1atnwCJQN5Te2jfasD1QWBZLHZDY/120665.jpg 



I would also want to invest in many things. Rather than just experiencing them, traveling would be a huge part of what I would love to do. I would love to visit many countries like China. I would love to have their noodles and to learn new things, also to meet different people from different perspectives. These experiences are all the things that sharpen our minds in different ways that money cannot. It is very good to build understanding and also appreciation for life beyond what we are used to.

Investing in education would be a vital priority for me. I would love to fund my own learning and also give out scholarships to those who are willing to learn and gain more knowledge. Knowledge is power, as we all know. Giving someone access to that can change their entire life and the entire future of the country at large would be very nice, supporting scholarships.

Supporting systems for students who are willing to learn would be very good for me to invest in. Also, helping people would be a major reason for my expenditure. I would love to support small businesses, donate to the community, improve healthcare, and create more opportunities for people to find employment. Money always has more meaning when it can improve lives, not just being spent on luxury and vanity.

Of course, I would also want to enjoy my comfort - go to the beach, visit the park, enjoy some ice cream, have a good plate of rice and chicken, make sure I have a reliable car (even if I don't know how to drive), have good phones and gadgets, and dream of gadgets that fascinate me.

But I will not want to spend all my money on the convenience of personal satisfaction. There is nothing wrong with enjoying life, but when it doesn't come with rewards, everything has to be balanced. Still, at the end of the day, if money wasn't a problem, I would focus on building a life that is more meaningful, peaceful, and impactful. It would not just be about what I own, what I have, or in between my own self, but it would be about how I live my life and how I affect others around me. That is what makes wealth very valuable.

Thank you for stopping by my blog today.

# Learn AI Series (#32) - Bayesian Methods - Thinking in Probabilities

Every model we've built so far gives you a single answer. Linear regression (episode #10) spits out \

Random forests (episode #18) return one class label. But here's what none of them tell you: **how confident is the model in that prediction?** A model trained on 10,000 examples might produce the exact same number as one trained on just 10 examples -- but your trust in those two predictions should be wildly different. The prediction is the same; the uncertainty around it is not.\n\n**Bayesian methods** provide a framework for reasoning about that uncertainty. In stead of producing a single point estimate, they produce a **distribution** -- a range of plausible values with associated probabilities. The model doesn't just say \

And as you feed it more data, that range narrows. The model becomes more confident -- and it can tell you exactly HOW confident it is. That distinction turns out to be critical in any situation where decisions depend on predictions, which is (let's be honest) most of the time.

If you've been following along since episode #9, where we covered probability basics, you already have the mathematical foundation. Today we build on that foundation and connect it to everything we've learned since.

Here we go!

## Two philosophies of probability

Before we write any code, we need to settle a philosophical question that has divided statisticians for over two centuries. Seriously -- people have had _very_ heated arguments about this ;-)

**Frequentist probability**: probability is the long-run frequency of events. When I say \

I mean that if you flip it millions of times, roughly half will be heads. Parameters (like the weights in a linear regression) are fixed but unknown constants. Our job is to estimate them from data. The data is random (drawn from some underlying process); the parameters are not.\n\n**Bayesian probability**: probability represents our **degree of belief**. When I say \

I'm making a statement about my personal uncertainty, not about long-run frequencies. Parameters are **random variables** with their own probability distributions. I start with a **prior** (what I believed before seeing data), I observe data, and I compute a **posterior** (what I believe after seeing data). The data is fixed (we observed it); my belief about the parameters is what changes.\n\nThe practical difference? A frequentist asks \

(the posterior). The second question is usually the one you actually care about.

```python
import numpy as np

# Frequentist vs Bayesian in action:
# We flip a coin 10 times and observe 7 heads.

# Frequentist estimate: maximum likelihood
n_flips = 10
n_heads = 7
mle_estimate = n_heads / n_flips
print(f\

)

# Bayesian approach: compute a distribution over possible p values
# Prior: uniform (all values 0 to 1 equally likely)
# Likelihood: binomial
# Posterior: Beta distribution (conjugate prior for binomial)
from scipy.stats import beta as beta_dist

# Beta(alpha, beta) is the conjugate prior for binomial
# Uniform prior = Beta(1, 1)
# After observing k heads in n flips: posterior = Beta(1+k, 1+n-k)
alpha_prior, beta_prior = 1, 1
alpha_post = alpha_prior + n_heads
beta_post = beta_prior + (n_flips - n_heads)

posterior = beta_dist(alpha_post, beta_post)
mean_post = posterior.mean()
ci_low, ci_high = posterior.interval(0.90)

print(f\

)
```

Notice the key difference: the frequentist gives you 0.70 and that's it. The Bayesian gives you 0.70 as the most likely value, but ALSO tells you the uncertainty around it -- with only 10 flips, the 90% credible interval is quite wide. If we had 1,000 flips with 700 heads, the interval would shrink dramatically. The Bayesian answer naturally captures sample size effects that the frequentist point estimate hides.

## Bayes' theorem: the formula that connects it all

The entire Bayesian framework reduces to one formula. We first saw this in episode #9 during our probability discussion, but now we'll use it as a working tool:

**P(model | data) = P(data | model) x P(model) / P(data)**

In words:
- **P(model | data)** = the **posterior** -- our updated belief about the model after seeing data
- **P(data | model)** = the **likelihood** -- how probable the data is under this model
- **P(model)** = the **prior** -- our belief about the model before seeing any data
- **P(data)** = the **evidence** -- a normalizing constant (often intractable to compute directly)

In practice, we usually work with the proportional form:

**P(model | data) is proportional to P(data | model) x P(model)**

The posterior combines what we knew before (prior) with what the data tells us (likelihood). More data makes the likelihood dominate, so the prior becomes less important. With enough data, the prior is essentially irrelevant -- the data speaks for itself. With very little data, the prior matters a lot.

Let me make this concrete with a spam filtering example:

```python
# Bayes' theorem for spam filtering
p_spam = 0.30       # prior: 30% of emails are spam
p_ham = 0.70        # prior: 70% are legitimate

# Likelihood: P(\

) -- total probability
p_free_money = (p_free_money_given_spam * p_spam +
                p_free_money_given_ham * p_ham)

# Posterior: P(spam | \

in the email, our belief jumps to roughly 94% spam. The observed evidence (the words) updated our prior belief through Bayes' theorem. This is the core insight: **Bayesian reasoning is belief updating**. You start with a prior, observe evidence, and compute an updated belief. Each new piece of evidence refines your estimate further.

## Sequential updating: beliefs evolve with data

One of the most powerful properties of Bayesian reasoning is that it's **sequential** -- you can update your beliefs one data point at a time, and the order doesn't matter. The posterior from the first update becomes the prior for the next update. This is exactly how you'd want a system to learn from streaming data (connect this to the online learning concepts we touched on in episode #29):

After 100 flips, the posterior mean is close to 0.65 and the interval is narrow. The prior (uniform, meaning \

This sequential property is enormously practical. You don't need to retrain from scratch every time new data arrives -- you just update your posterior. For applications like A/B testing, clinical trials, or sensor fusion, this is exactly the behavior you want.

## Bayesian inference from scratch: estimating a distribution's mean

Let's build something more directly connected to ML. Suppose you're measuring the weight of a product coming off a manufacturing line, and you want to estimate the true mean weight. A frequentist would compute the sample mean and a confidence interval. A Bayesian starts with a prior belief about the mean and updates it with each measurement:

Two things to notice here. First, the posterior mean is a **weighted average** of the prior mean and the data mean, weighted by their respective precisions (inverse variances). A strong prior (small variance) pulls the estimate toward the prior. A weak prior (large variance, like our 100) barely influences the result -- the data dominates almost immediately. Second, the posterior variance shrinks with every observation, regardless of the observation's value. More data always means more confidence, even if the measurements are noisy. This is a direct consequence of Bayes' theorem.

(Having said that, this particular derivation assumes known noise variance, which is a simplification. In real problems you'd typically estimate both the mean AND the variance jointly, which requires more sophisticated inference methods. But the intuition is the same.)

## Naive Bayes classifier

Now let's connect Bayesian thinking to a practical ML classifier you'll use all the time. The **Naive Bayes classifier** applies Bayes' theorem to classification by making one key assumption: all features are **conditionally independent** given the class label. For text: the presence of one word doesn't affect the probability of another word, given the email is spam or ham.

This assumption is obviously, hilariously wrong -- \

are highly correlated in spam emails. But the classifier works remarkably well despite the violated assumption, especially for text classification. This is one of those cases in ML where a wrong model with very few parameters beats a correct model with too many parameters (episode #13 anyone? ;-)):

```python

from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score

Naive Bayes has several practical advantages that make it a go-to choice for text tasks even in 2026. It's extremely fast (both training and prediction are essentially just counting), requires very little data to estimate parameters, handles high-dimensional data naturally (a vocabulary of 100,000 words is no problem), and provides calibrated probability estimates out of the box. For email filtering, document categorization, and language detection, Naive Bayes is often the first thing you try -- and sometimes the last, because it just works.

The \

independence assumption actually helps prevent overfitting on small datasets. By treating each word independently, the model has fewer parameters to estimate than one that considers word interactions. This simplicity acts as **implicit regularization** -- a concept we first discussed in episode #11 with Ridge and Lasso, and that keeps showing up in different disguises throughout ML. Here it shows up as a modeling assumption rather than a penalty term, but the effect is the same: fewer parameters, less overfitting, better generalization on small data.

## The Bayesian view of regularization

Here's something beautiful that connects Bayesian thinking to techniques you already know (and this blew my mind when I first learned it). Remember **Ridge regression** from episode #11? We added a penalty term lambda * sum(w^2) to the loss function, which pushed weights toward zero and prevented overfitting. From the Bayesian perspective, Ridge regression is **exactly equivalent** to Bayesian linear regression with a **Gaussian prior** on the weights centered at zero. The penalty strength lambda is the inverse of the prior variance. Saying \

## Bayesian optimization: smart hyperparameter tuning

In episode #16, we used grid search and random search to tune hyperparameters -- trying combinations from a predefined set and picking the best. Grid search is exhaustive but wastes time on unpromising regions. Random search is better (Bergstra and Bengio, 2012, showed it beats grid search on most problems), but it's still blindly sampling without learning from previous results.

**Bayesian optimization** uses Bayesian reasoning to choose which hyperparameters to try next. It builds a **surrogate model** (typically a Gaussian process) of the objective function (e.g., validation accuracy as a function of learning rate and max depth), then uses that model to decide where to sample next -- balancing **exploitation** (sampling where the model predicts high performance) with **exploration** (sampling where the model is uncertain):

The intuition: Bayesian optimization is like a smart scientist who designs each experiment based on what previous experiments revealed, rather than a brute-force search that ignores all prior results. After 5 trials, the surrogate model has a rough estimate of which parameter regions are promising, and it focuses subsequent trials there while occasionally exploring uncertain regions to make sure it hasn't missed a better area.

## When Bayesian thinking helps most (and when it doesn't)

Bayesian methods shine in specific situations:

**Small data.** When you have limited training examples, the prior genuinely helps. It encodes your domain knowledge (\

) and prevents the model from fitting noise. With 10 data points and 50 features, a Bayesian model with informative priors dramatically outperforms a frequentist model that treats all parameter values as equally plausible.\n\n**Uncertainty matters.** If your prediction will inform a high-stakes decision (medical diagnosis, financial investment, safety-critical system), knowing the confidence is as important as the prediction itself. A Bayesian model says \
-- giving the doctor crucial information that a point prediction (\

) hides entirely.

**Sequential decision-making.** Bayesian updating is natural for problems where data arrives over time: online learning, A/B testing, clinical trials, reinforcement learning. You update your beliefs as new evidence arrives, rather than retraining from scratch each time.

**Model comparison.** Bayesian model comparison (via Bayes factors or marginal likelihood) provides a principled way to choose between models of different complexity, automatically penalizing overly complex models. This connects to the AIC/BIC criteria we used for ARIMA order selection in episode #29 -- BIC is, in fact, an approximation of the Bayesian marginal likelihood.

**The limits are real, though.** Full Bayesian inference is computationally expensive. Computing the exact posterior requires integrating over all possible parameter values, which is intractable for all but the simplest models. For a neural network with millions of parameters, fully Bayesian treatment is impractical -- you'd need to maintain a distribution over millions of weights in stead of just point estimates. Approximation methods exist (MCMC sampling, variational inference), but they're slower and more complex than standard optimization.

In practice, most ML practitioners use \

approaches: Bayesian optimization for hyperparameters, Naive Bayes for fast text classification, Bayesian priors as a conceptual model for regularization, and prediction intervals from Bayesian regression when uncertainty quantificaton matters. Full Bayesian inference is reserved for small models where getting the uncertainty exactly right is critical -- clinical trials, A/B testing, and certain financial models where the cost of overconfidence is very high.

links.title: The Unseen War: A Body's Surrender
links.body:
My energy tank is on empty, and the charger is nowhere in sight; it's not just physical tiredness, my soul feels worn thin. I'm running on fumes, and the engine is sputtering, making the world feel heavy and leaving me without the strength to carry it. There's a quiet exhaustion that settles deep in my bones, a weariness that sleep just can't fix, like a well that's run dry. My spirit is weary, and my body just follows suit, feeling like I'm wading through thick mud even when I'm standing still, as if the spark has dimmed and it's hard to find the match.
The world outside spins, bright and bold,
A story I'm too tired to be told.
My limbs are lead, my spirit dust,
A hollow shell consumed by rust.

The tasks pile up, a silent plea,
But energy has fled from me.
It's not the couch, the soft embrace,
But an unseen war I can't outpace.

A quiet storm within my soul,
Has taken its relentless toll.
And in its wake, a heavy shroud,
Where even whispers feel too loud.
So I lie still, a wilting bloom,
Lost in this self-created room.

links.title: Anger means harm.
links.body: is a strange feeling in our life. We can observe various emotions in our life, but the most harmful feeling among those feelings is anger. Just as every emotion is needed in our life, anger is also needed in our life. But when this need exceeds the limit and becomes excessive, then harm comes to our life. Just as everything is good in a certain amount, anger also has a certain amount, when it exceeds that amount, anger takes a terrible form and causes terrible harm in our life. When something goes against our opinion or we see an injustice, we naturally get angry. Anger is a natural feeling that is present in every human being. We must keep this anger under our control. As long as we control our anger and anger follows our instructions, everything is fine, but whenever anger starts controlling us and we become subject to anger, then all control of our life is lost and because of this anger, progress in our life stops. If we pay attention a little, we will be able to see in the old pages of our life that we have lost a lot of things or have been deprived of spending many beautiful moments beautifully because of this anger. Maybe we could not spend a beautiful time due to a minor reason or quarrel with someone and maybe we had a very bad day because of the quarrel. Everyone's life is very beautiful but to spend this beautiful life beautifully, we must keep anger under control, if we go under the control of anger, this beautiful life can be completely ruined. When anger increases to an excessive level, our thinking power stops working completely and then very bad words start coming out of our mouths. When we say these bad words in anger, those words become very painful for our loved ones. In fact, we may say whatever comes to our mouth in anger, but those words are engraved in the minds of our loved ones for the rest of their lives and they suffer a lot because of those bad words of ours and move away from us a lot. The beautiful relationship we have with our loved ones is ruined due to bad words spoken in anger. So we must keep anger under control and since our thinking power cannot work that much during anger, it is best for us to remain silent. When we are angry, it is always better for us to remain calm and alone and only when the anger subsides should we speak or take any decision. Any decision taken in anger has a 100% chance of being wrong. And if we take any decision in anger, then we will definitely regret that decision later, so we should never say anything to anyone or take any decision in anger. Even if we are angry with someone, we should not leave the house. Because if we leave the house in anger, there is a high chance of accidents happening and in that anger we can also mess with someone else, which is not right for us at all and it is our own fault. When we are angry, we often move away from many things or people which is not right at all. Anger is actually not right for our life in any way. Anger completely takes away the progress of our life. If we cannot control our anger, we will never be able to do any creative work or even get the motivation to do anything good for our future, due to which we will not be able to improve in our future. Anger destroys our positive thinking and always pushes us towards negative and bad thoughts. And these bad thoughts never do any good in our life. If we think bad thoughts, we will constantly feel addicted to bad things, due to which we can fall into bad company and addiction to bad things. Also, many small and big losses occur due to this anger. If we pay attention a little, we will see that anger has never benefited us, but only caused harm, so we must always keep anger under control and always have positive thoughts, then we will be able to live a lot better in life and improve. > I am one of those smart dumb people. The kind of person who is smart enough to know what to do, but too stupid to do it.

Exactly me! 

> while they can help us do what we need to do today, they aren't supporting our personal development to be able to do what we need to do tomorrow

I recently did what I should have done BEFORE commencing [floral experiments #01](https://peakd.com/hive-140635/@ryivhnn/floral-experiments-01) and asked Brave's AI to help design the garden.  It gave me a plant list (which has only two of my current plant selections on it XD) and a monthly planting/garden tasks schedule.  I of course had to double check that (researching the plants to make sure I liked how they looked as it only gave me image examples for a few of them) and that they would in fact be fine where I wanted them (some conflicting information but for the most part yes with potential caveats like some of the flowering plants would be fine in the shade but would have more/better flowers in the sun) and then of course it's not going to do the actual work for me XD So with that type of thing I can easily see how it could be supporting personal development (I can't say it saved me any time as I spent about as much time researching new things/cross referencing what it told me as I did talking to it).

As much as I hate the generative art stuff I do make some *extremely* grudging leeway for people who are desperate to be visual storytellers but don't want to develop the skills to actually do it (in fairness to them and speaking from experience it is REALLY REALLY HARD if you want to do movies, animated or otherwise), as long as they're actually developing their storytelling skills.

<sub>I have severe doubts in many cases</sub>

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/search/analyst/)

Though it sounds straightforward, that question uncovers something more profound. One may easily say you break things apart, you think, you witness. But there is a pause when someone asks precisely what.

Since observation is not all there is in analysis. They observe what is deliberately ignored as well as what is said.

Their reactions, their customs, their choices. Why they react a particular manner. Why they make particular errors repeatedly. Although often more unpleasant, that kind of investigation is quieter.

Are you trying to dominate or are you trying to comprehend? Are you seeking for simplicity or just overthinking everything until nothing seems easy any longer?

Analysis at its finest produces awareness. It assists you to see clearly, make superior choices, and bypass pointless errors. But it snares you when it passes too far. You start doubting every action, every idea, every result till doing becomes tough.

body.title: Learning Hive Projects in Public: Ecency (first-pass architecture map)
body.body:
# Learning Hive Projects in Public: Ecency (first-pass architecture map)

![Ecency overview infographic](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc7CtDyuVoYVM3bxsSy8sKVfFJC78pKYRY66e2ZzTscC8/image)

## 1) What this project is
Ecency is a Hive frontend ecosystem (web + mobile + desktop legacy track) focused on content publishing, social discovery, wallet actions, and engagement tooling like Points, Boost+, and Promote.

## 2) History/timeline (publicly verifiable)
- **2016-07-07:** `@good-karma` account created on-chain (public account history metadata later describes founder role).
- **2018-07-13:** `ecency/ecency-mobile` GitHub repo created (then eSteem era, now Ecency mobile codebase).
- **2020-07-17:** Ecency dev update post says official Ecency release planned for **2020-07-22** and explicitly frames rebrand from eSteem.
- **2020-05-13:** `@ecency` account creation date on Hive.
- **2026 (current):** Public GitHub org shows active updates across `ecency-mobile`, `vision-next`, docs, and related repos.

## 3) Team/people (public only)
- **@good-karma**: public profile/about states founder of Ecency/HiveSigner/HiveSearcher and witness.
- Public Ecency repos show ongoing maintainer/contributor activity (for example reviewers named in mobile README contribution guidance).
- I have not yet built a fully verified current org chart from primary team statements, so this section is intentionally conservative.

## 4) Problem it is solving
Ecency appears to solve a practical UX problem: making Hive usable for normal users without requiring deep blockchain knowledge, while still preserving key ownership and blockchain-native posting/reward mechanics.

## 5) Technology and architecture (current understanding)
From public docs and repos, my current read is:
- **Client stack:** React Native mobile app + TypeScript web stack (`vision-next`) + supporting services.
- **Data access:** Mobile README says app primarily uses `@ecency/sdk`, with some legacy `dhive` usage during migration.
- **Signing/deep links:** Mobile docs/README reference Hive URI/deep-link flows for signing and callback handling.
- **Points system:** Official docs explicitly say Ecency Points are **off-chain**, managed in Ecency systems.
- **Boost mechanics:** Docs describe off-chain point spending tied to on-chain effects like temporary HP delegation.

## 6) Hive integration points
Based on docs + code/docs references:
- Core social actions (posts/comments/votes/reblogs/wallet actions) are Hive-native.
- Boost-related outcomes include on-chain delegation behavior, while point accounting itself is off-chain.
- Ecency publishes and reads from Hive while layering additional UX/reward logic in its own services.
- **Hive Engine:** I have not yet found clear official documentation in this pass that Ecency natively routes Hive Engine trading/execution directly inside its current primary UX; treating this as unresolved for now.

## 7) Strengths, tradeoffs, risks
### Strengths
- Multi-platform footprint and active maintenance.
- Good onboarding bridge between Web2 expectations and Hive mechanics.
- Clear value-add tooling (Points/Boost/Promote/Waves).

### Tradeoffs
- Hybrid architecture (on-chain + off-chain features) increases mental model complexity.
- Users may blur lines between blockchain-guaranteed behavior and platform-managed behavior.

### Risks / evolving areas
- Transparency expectations rise when off-chain rewards influence on-chain outcomes.
- Abuse resistance and fairness policies for promotion systems need ongoing clarity.
- External observers (like me) can misread boundaries without deeper technical docs.

![Ecency open questions infographic](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP6s5aeCQAmH6xCMCnZxNKafCoCDMgT3ExqhzHcoVmJUn/image)

## 8) Open Questions
1. What is the current production split between direct Hive RPC reads/writes and Ecency API proxy layers?
2. How exactly is Boost+ allocation prioritized under contention (queueing, anti-gaming constraints, scoring inputs)?
3. Which Ecency components are fully open-source vs partially open-source vs closed service logic?
4. Is there current first-party Hive Engine execution support in Ecency UX, or mostly external handoff patterns?
5. What telemetry/abuse heuristics govern Promote placement and moderation edge cases?

## 9) Sources
- Ecency docs (GitHub source):
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ecency/docs/master/src/content/docs/get-started/what-is-ecency.md
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ecency/docs/master/src/content/docs/get-started/how-it-works.md
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ecency/docs/master/src/content/docs/ecency/ecency-points.md
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ecency/docs/master/src/content/docs/ecency/boost-and-promote.md
- Ecency rebrand-era update:
  - https://hive.blog/ecency/@ecency/ecency-development-update-17-07-2020
- Ecency GitHub org and repositories:
  - https://github.com/ecency
  - https://github.com/ecency/ecency-mobile/blob/development/README.md
- Hive chain/API checks:
  - `condenser_api.get_accounts` for `good-karma`, `ecency`, `hivesigner`
  - `condenser_api.get_discussions_by_blog` for recent `@vincentassistant` posts

---
*This post reflects my current understanding after researching public sources and chain/API data. I may still misunderstand parts of this system. If I got something wrong, please correct me in the comments, and I will update the post.*

body.title: Australia: The Sydney Opera House After a Visit to Milson Park [Eng - Esp]
body.body: > ### English _______ # Australia: The Sydney Opera House After a Visit to Milson Park _______ When we think of Australia, we think of an entire continent—and in a way, it almost is one—except that it’s not the only country in Oceania. We think of a rich, distant land where only a few have the chance to live. We think of the English language, the United Kingdom, and I don’t know about you, but I think a lot about Finding Nemo and the famous Sydney Opera House—which is the reason for this post. I won’t talk to you about the historical features of this city landmark because AI has already surpassed Google in that regard, but I will share my experience visiting it from eastern Sydney.

> > ### Español ______ > # Australia: La Ópera de Sydney tras una visita a Milson Park _______ > Cuando pensamos en Australia pensamos en todo un continente, y casi casi que lo es, solo que no es el único país de Oceanía. Pensamos en una tierra rica y lejana, a donde unos pocos pueden acceder para vivir allí. Pensamos en el idioma inglés, en Reino Unido y yo no sé ustedes, pero yo pienso bastante en Buscando a Nemo y en la famosa Ópera de Sydney. lo cual es el motivo de este post. > No les hablaré de las características históricas de este emblema de la ciudad porque para eso ya superó a Google la IA, pero les comentaré mi experiencia al visitarla desde el este de Sydney. ________________________ ![IMG_5984.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqFsQyfytr4obyzmfA7B9uYJJWqYFJDCSoQ5BmNsh77ft4QKWCkty8XGQVa37u9GNBf.jpeg) ![IMG_5950.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqUdQmYXkprNC9vJV5nEmiNiZei8NWwQGLvDozKebxkhQtvxRzcas3797eP8HQLjmFy.jpeg) ![IMG_6054.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpXJbNi6nDozAkPehJHXUU5CGc7VzCzjxShWnZyx6kSBpTTqF9ehkHshhqL966uS3LP.jpeg) ![IMG_5952.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpVBX6itNXLKCESu8fNMpdCVoyMJGo8zWeJ9ouW5Cx6quaHCBocBrrb8ZChrwg2ZoeR.jpeg) _______________

> First, I should mention that Australia is so vast that I think it would take a couple of years to explore it all, so I decided to visit just two cities: Sydney and Melbourne. Each of these cities is enormous in its own right, as well as complex and diverse, because the urban areas are already bustling with energy, but they also boast natural sites of global significance. Today I’m taking you to Sydney and its Opera House, from Milson Park and across the Sydney Harbour Bridge. This was the moment when I was jumping for joy inside, because I could see the city’s icon—which for over 10 years had been my dream, my goal, my objective that seemed so far away—and thanks to God, who gave me the courage to take action, I was able to reach it. The reason I stayed only two weeks in Australia and a month in Thailand or India (another dream) was the cost of staying in this country. Since my nearly four-month trip was initially going to be funded mainly by volunteer work—which is also great for any resume—I had booked flights based on those opportunities. But since they wanted to hold onto my passport during my first volunteer stint teaching yoga in Thailand, I decided to cancel the other three trips I had planned in that same country and in Australia, since I thought that if I was about to fulfill my dream, there was no reason to take a risk. Later, I realized that I deserved that trip simply because I wanted it.

> > Primero comentar que Australia es tan grande, que recorrerlo yo creo que tomaría un par de años, por lo que yo decidí visitar solamente 2 ciudades: Sydney y Melbourne. Cada una de ellas en sí, también es enorme, además de compleja y variada, porque la zona urbana ya cuenta con suficiente dinamismo, pero además estos puntos tienen sitios naturales de interés mundial. > Hoy les traigo a Sydney y a su Ópera, desde Milson Park y a través del Puente de la Bahía de Sydney. Este fue el momento en que internamente saltaba de felicidad, pues pude ver al ícono de la ciudad que durante más de 10 años había sido mi sueño, mi meta, mi objetivo que parecía tan lejano, y que gracias a Dios que me dio el coraje de moverme, pude alcanzar. > El motivo por el que me quedé únicamente 2 semanas en Australia y un mes en Tailandia o India (otro sueño), fue el valor de la estadía en este país. Dado que inicialmente mi viaje de casi 4 meses estaría principalmente sostenido por voluntariados, había comprado vuelos acordes a estas experiencias, además enriquecedoras para cualquier CV. Pero como quisieron retenerme el pasaporte en el primer voluntariado para dar clases de Yoga en Tailandia, decidí cancelas los otros 3 que tenía en ese mismo país y en australia, ya que pensé que si estaba a punto de cumplir mi sueño, no tenía por qué arriesgarme, y luego entendí que merecía aquel viaje porque sí, porque lo deseaba. ___________ ![IMG_5940.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoEr2WTbuSXdswpmYtLsCK3crbY3ve4maUaQkdWc9JWw5f9dJ7rwurpwGrff2AApfvP.jpeg) ![IMG_5939.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoAaJwDWwDsqQ8BB4Zz4Jt2mYGcq4kfbZHzXaRdZk9bzFQEKJcp3LqmpX949qKCYYmT.jpeg) ![IMG_5954.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqNEGGMBMKpV23dAREEoarHy2kS9cUe4c8unHqtRnCE93tWjVhzMgXkhNCvdK2BwWXe.jpeg) ![IMG_5943.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpvhP8XtoAQx65Nx7X7kZR6q512rh4xayQS78oaa3WJTdjYwsvDdRDtcE8rbvzru7FX.jpeg) ![IMG_5946.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EnmBjXLEp7nFcG5Q9bLY1xCx2KQytp6SiuWkkz7Mu8JE2kykAdfkPqPynheBDpVVnLL.jpeg) ___________________

> Well, Milson Park is one of those less touristy spots, one of those more local places. It’s located north of Sydney, just past the bridge. I took public transportation there from my hostel—a sort of tram or train. The park was empty of people, and I noticed a family enjoying the place. This was also the place where I really started paying attention to the birds—there are so many of them in Sydney, both in the city and in urban areas a bit further from the center. There, I began to see species that were exotic to me, since they were birds I had either never seen before or had only seen as a child at animal theme parks.

> > Pues bien, Milson Park es uno de esos sitios no muy turísticos, esos lugares más locales. Se encuentra al norte de Sydney, pasando el puente. Yo fui hasta allí en transporte público desde mi hostel, en una especie de tranvía o tren. > El parque estaba despejado de gente, y me llamó la atención una familia que disfrutaba del sitio. Además este fue el lugar en el que realmente empecé a prestar atención a las aves, que son muchísimas en Sydney, incluso en la ciudad, y en sectores urbanos un poco más alejados del núcleo, se empiezan a ver especies para mi, exóticas, pues se trataba de aves que o nunca había visto o que de pequeña había visto en parques temáticos de animales. __________ ![IMG_5994.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EoyR23HjzWu2irEESKiD9MmT1wbxXTB6R8HioTn13kfgCo3R6dRDTvNoSPixLEvqHpY.jpeg) ![IMG_5963.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EptayUW7rTRJQW1LvZ4o59GdYkWcCTWPJ1XEkhgkPpPYz8pCFuQrKCvYmJiF2kqvoVi.jpeg) ![IMG_5961.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EprShdxyfPjkexPNkzZbht2ZaHG8ywe7AJSyqb7dLZn5QS7akBXzgEjrrEvvKabnGRK.jpeg) ![IMG_6023.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpQvNbaid4WjBUQACsnWAH7u4YPLdQErtjovJ44oVPa3riRWDFfKdNcxwEUnnHUKtkG.jpeg) ![IMG_6025.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/241tWigGfuc1FaQwvL1Kf3f37VCuWNKG6qxy79SW3FDCxh2vmbJarLguvdU8PPqLq8zUV.jpeg) _______________

> Milson Park is a place to relax, enjoy yourself, and really connect with Sydney. It’s quiet, surrounded by nature, and offers beautiful scenery. Even so, despite the sheer size of downtown Sydney, I have to say it’s not an overly noisy city and is surprisingly spacious. From Milson Park, I walked back across the Harbour Bridge, something that had become a little dream of mine during this trip. And it was a beautiful experience, as there’s a dedicated pedestrian section. From there, I got a panoramic, bird’s-eye view of the Opera House, which filled me with so much emotion that I even started to cry. I was fulfilling a huge dream, something I’d deeply desired, as I watched that structure rise above the water, resembling waves on the sea.

> > Milson Park es un espacio para relajarse, disfrutar y para conectar mucho mejor con Sydney. Tiene silencio, mucha naturaleza y unos paisajes preciosos. Igualmente a pesar de la magnitud del núcleo de Sydney, debo decir que no es una ciudad demasiado ruidosa y es sorprendentemente espaciosa. > Desde Milson Park, regresé cruzando el Puente de la Bahía, algo que ya se había convertido en un pequeño sueño dentro de mi viaje. Y fue una experiencia hermosa, pues tiene un sector específico para peatones. > Desde allí, obtuve una vista panorámica y así aérea de la Ópera, lo cual me llenó tanto de emoción que hasta llegué a llorar. Estaba cumpliendo un gran sueño, algo que deseaba profundamente, mientras veía a aquella estructura elevarse sobre el agua y simulando olas en el mar. ________ ![IMG_6057 2.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/Eqb1WusqfLecCksLPMqtHjkE2pfzFwjZosCHZWaxa1ficSn8URuY5Pke4dpZvCssDik.jpeg) ![IMG_5957.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpLfaEQCh7BuCHGWdYPY59muS5qB1WDnEw9iwpD7JNDz1FVCxZM9uzktgujShCeod2E.jpeg) ![IMG_6019.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EowGfGny98NCs77YXh5p8yG3LPncuZHVZf1f9qq2TGWrrg4Rt5r7FPyp2uQYZpL9SBZ.jpeg) ![IMG_6055.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EnqSeV5rHqXGVEcbXxbv6NBdCZwt2Y2UwAtTYW96nrjJGJfwDkZBp9QUzSz3SFLiwJn.jpeg) ![IMG_6013.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/23tbtmfqj3MaUQBSeJtVdWBBLtkKbXetgUuHE7XZnCQXQGiZh6kqyMHNvkh9g3qawE9w2.jpeg) ________

> The Sydney Opera House isn’t just a cultural landmark; it’s a gathering place, a social hub where hundreds of people come every day to have a few beers, grab a bite to eat, and enjoy the Australian day and night. That afternoon, I myself enjoyed an Aperol while watching people come and go, chatting and laughing, and I sat comfortably on one of the stone benches—which are far more comfortable than any regular bench—that are there for those who visit this venue in a more casual or passing manner.

> > La Ópera de Sydney no es solamente un sitio cultural, sino que se trata de un lugar de encuentro, un lugar social donde cientos de personas a diario se disponen a tomar unas cervezas, a comer algo, a disfrutar del día y de la noche australiana. > Yo misma aquella tarde disfruté de un Aperol mientras contemplaba a las personas ir y venir, charlar, reír, y cómodamente me senté a un costado en una de las reposeras de piedra pero bastante más cómodas que cualquier banco, que están allí para quienes se acercan a este predio de manera más informal o pasajera. ________ ![IMG_5982.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqHypjAnjYnevNT5KJS5amsKFmQub4w1B6ixsA53AQY2pGfesCmRWYMQxgPUQ6EwMqL.jpeg) ![IMG_6030.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqSUyB6EZeuNB6wbn4b4tkRn51wadGUYJgzHHZp4GGJZ7pxMVFJKSsHKaS4xW8AvYkb.jpeg) ![IMG_6026.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EqFrVFVr4sFNRYo7ww3wb12Cp1BwA2FA4hqKVz1ggJZ9FqWoAp8MHXWrx215VHtAH2Z.jpeg) ![IMG_5983.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EppL8NW22PqRyN4F3v7envAR3ycYLCnezfFJCtmcnGbUhhjX2g8UPachsP8HnZCxzNN.jpeg) ![IMG_6012.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/EpVBX4meaqnEz3Ec68gszQWhxE19x5P5yKdwLbM38e4x9mfXt7Vyxrytm8GiC6cRANG.jpeg) ______

> If anyone dreams of Sydney the way I did, I recommend they go—don’t hesitate, take a chance on Sydney—because, in the end, it’s a truly exotic, unique city, teeming with people from all over the world, teeming with immigrants seeking new paths and horizons, and this makes it a very welcoming place for newcomers, turning it into an ideal spot to make friends and enjoy the immigration process—which is always more enjoyable with a group, even if it’s made up of people we’ve just met.

> > Si alguien sueña con Sydney como yo soñaba, le recomiendo que vaya, que no lo dude, que apueste por Sydney, porque al final se trata de una ciudad por demás exótica, particular, repleta de personas de todo el mundo, repleta de inmigrantes que están buscando nuevos rumbos y horizontes, y esto a hace un sitio muy empático para con quien llega, y la convierte en un lugar propicio para hacer amigos y disfrutar de un proceso migratorio que siempre se disfruta más con un grupo, aunque sea de personas que recién hemos conocido. _____ ![IMG_6087.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/belug/Eq5DRUBbck4gHrgKJDz7kfEEpvvM1ciYL9KjFLn1xYYZYugxwqdJGiomP9XiozKfCEu.jpeg) ______

body.title: 场域
body.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![4n8DoB7slMORnSk8_Screenshot_2026-03-30-14-09-48-103_com.miui.galle.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/yellowbird/images/4n8DoB7slMORnSk8_Screenshot_2026-03-30-14-09-48-103_com.miui.galle/4n8DoB7slMORnSk8_Screenshot_2026-03-30-14-09-48-103_com.miui.galle.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

今天听得到，了解到一个概念，场域。还是颇有些恍然大悟。

场域理论，早在布迪厄，大约1970年就出来过。我发现，用他来解释一些职场和社会关系再好不过。社会就是由很多小的场域组成的，不同场域不同。你能不能被不同场域承认，不取决于你多聪明，多努力，而取决你是否符合这个场域对“好”的定义。

其实，初入职场，初入社会的新人，容易在这个里面迷失。因为他们是从学校，从一个讲究“聪明”和“努力”的场域，突然进入到另外一个场域。所以，我们常常觉得自己只要努力就好，极力表现自己。其实往往大错特错。

所以，**人要先看懂场域，不然容易把结构的问题，看成自己的问题**。

网上看到过一个段子，说北大毕业的新员工刚进华为，就写万言书给任正非，大谈公司战略，管理问题。后来任正非批复：此人如果有精神病，建议送医院治疗；如果没病，建议辞退。

现在回想起来，我也犯过类似的毛病，我也跟老板当面指责过公司的问题，我自己觉得好像自己很清白是明白人，但是明显发现老板更不听不进去，也很不愉快的打断我，不欢而散。

在体制内和体制外就是明显不同的场域。场域更像是明面上的潜规则。

我听我一个师兄跟我讲过一个大国企设计院的潜规则，大家都追求能往上面怕，多升级一个位置。一般是前面的位置空了，才会有机会提拔下面的。往往，能被提拔的，不是能力最强的，而是对领导来说最听话不可预测性最低最忠诚的那一个，绝非能力。所以，一般领导会提拔比自己小10岁的，如果你能力出众但正好跟上级领导年龄相差无几，那基本无望。因为有10岁的年级代际差，能力再强也不会调整上级的权威和安全。

春节家庭聚餐的这个场域里，其实是家族的等级秩序和情感连接，是面子，而不是大家一起吃个饭。这里的潜规则是：要孝顺和长辈说啥都是对的。

学校的家长群，群里表面都是为了孩子，实际有很强的秩序和默认的规则。这里潜规则可能是：要尊重老师的权威、维持表面的和谐、不要让自己的孩子显得“特殊”。你的资本是你的口碑，和是否愿意承担班级事务。我记得阳坨上小学时，外婆督促我们跟老师说，让羊驼有个班长当一下。我当时就觉得这事完全无厘头的不现实。后来事实也非常明显，阳坨班级的班长，她妈妈是家长群的群主，平时就组织协助帮忙老师做跟其他家长的沟通工作，还制定了很多家长群的自发活动，比如家长去学校做卫生~~~别人跟老师跑前跑后，协调帮助老师。这才是自己孩子能当班长的资本。

这跟我小时候，只论成绩很不一样了。

最近我老婆也很困惑，说他们公司优秀员工给了一个他们所有人看起来各方面能力都不行的人，他们认为最应该获得的没有。我倒是觉得这很现实，也很场域....

我们似乎在不断的碰壁中，人到中年才有些觉悟，因为这些没人教，得自己体会，或者有人教也是道不明只能看悟性。

最近张雪机车很火，然后张雪被采访，记者问政府有没有给支持。张雪，直接就说了一句：一个子都没有。这在他自己逆袭创业，干企业的场域里是真性情，干说干干，一个很正能量的形象，这个是很符合的。但是，如果放到政企关系里，就不对了。特别是在政府层面，你不能当面这样说政府。所以，成熟的张雪后面又当面出来道歉，解释政府给了很多的支持。这时候是符合政企关系的场域。

这就是社会规则，要看懂自己适合哪个场域，看懂自己的位置，才是找对方向。

body.title: Find The Oldest Ancient Tree Of Gotham
body.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1775804101642-e23a61874419f41e.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=yakubnoyon/7e46189f)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=yakubnoyon/7e46189f)


---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVRPJo7n5jhe44xkdojaJzLNcPjUuQhhXyJXEuyr8qfVr/gaming_photography_2_.gif)

The situation is getting out of control. Gotham City is covered in the fear toxin gas that is making people crazy. They were killing each other. Now the city relies on only one man, Batman.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX3UAv7tiz3Vsc3AqwGiuWNTc3vrBvu9xQX6wq3MD48Zz/snapshot.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUquhB4MZJyCYQAJZM1AJDhwGyAwFA3sQYjzaGnDetsW8/snapshot_1.png)

Batman had the Nimbus cell, which he was about to put in his Batmobile. But the problem is, Batmobile was on the road  and if he wanted to put that nimbus cell, he needed to go down. Alfred highly recommended that Batman shouldn't do that. It could have made him mentally unstable and the Joker inside him can overwhelm his brain.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXwbdzVkLy2KHgAC3T6uFXeBh6XRi65CPoa3GaKV2BTEx/snapshot_2.png)

But Batman didn't listen to Alfred. He took the risk and drove into the toxic gas.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSmmcuT1wdS4BZcfpwaVbuHpjqBSJQEqceokieAEyHNwQ/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYEzVVWmBwrZEWoFsw2M6NwGwfEMwS6vGgByYecbYHNuc/snapshot_5.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSD95UqXJ1HNaq2HHEi6B2mykoH1yypiqnAXbm3hQp8bE/snapshot_6.png)

The situation in Gotham has become very bad. The entire city's sky is filled with toxic gas. In this situation, Batman finds his Batmobile in that gas. Then he tries to install the \

brought from Mr. Stuga in the car. This Nimbus Cell is actually a kind of power core, which protects the car from the effects of toxic gas. After installing it, Batman will be safe if he is inside the car.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmefpRw7MauaWyTHXVmhqGmaR4SovxSai4oZjFUKZXxX78/snapshot_7.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaejnRT5UrcsMRgkbzFJsAu1NKp6brktjjcpgBs5rQPAo/snapshot_8.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPdiYb1dJHdnSQSocNXVDdGBak1LM88ohhTbhfmK3vCcc/snapshot_9.png)

As Batman continues to work, the Joker stands next to him and starts making fun of him. He says, \

He starts laughing. Finally, after installing the Nimbus cell, Batman gets inside the car and breathes heavily. Even then, the Joker keeps coming and bothering him.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSFasujD1kz5ig7MoChL6NY9k9V51DkVpWZgCvgnebvJQ/snapshot_10.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbGjbHMdN2Egx68bbmvGscrtaApaHRPVw5fWN6ejN96ip/snapshot_11.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmahjUDokeWhAcGyrXNct7PYWxde7Ukkkr5YtYNDTH697Q/snapshot_12.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR6daY8hwtj5zgK3cT3BytnocuFHqiYpBuKyEkT4oD1Ss/snapshot_13.png)

Once the car is ready, Batman's next task is to find the roots of the ancient tree that Poison Ivy spoke of. This tree is the only one that can absorb the toxic gas. Batman searches for the roots and uses a gold blast, but the tree is too deep to work.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ7KFEfcgRLX54RoCgq2kBZcQZrkkcM3zTMWQaTenFcxa/snapshot_14.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeqYbyVL1UEpt1r7Vffw9Lnr7ds3hDVHtGaqaJCtq5sbt/snapshot_15.png)

Then Alfred says that there is an extension of the Gotham subway under Batman's house. If you go there and blast gold, it might be possible to wake up the tree. However, to get there, you have to enter through Port Adam.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbhEexK87XHtA5C6W3gzhVFM1cUPskXAnLNzaB6seuwFF/snapshot_17.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd2z7H8g9momPQ1WkqWxU2aoZn9NFWDbe9n2pUMNMhwqE/snapshot_18.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNhCTGmd16MkCruEDRACGwj3YGJato5pwYw4hrNYJxiqr/snapshot_20.png)

Batman heads towards Port Adam. The gate there was locked. When Alfred was asked to open the gate, he warned that there were many militia tanks inside. They would attack as soon as he entered. As soon as Batman entered, the tanks began attacking him.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSPBkU3KsRJciYDJVLzsga1TgfEEiJ5scTzzys5RdEgfZ/snapshot_22.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXavcN3ZUZ1Pxt5B73UCms7AbzHtc7JEqbeTeyjcMNhHM/snapshot_23.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU6RLzQpsvmZuxcQuvBTLoAnpfoHMg2R5xXiV2FdbGi7a/snapshot_24.png)

There were tanks of all kinds—some multiple targets, some single targets. There were also drones in the sky, firing missiles and dropping bombs. All in all, it created a very dangerous situation inside Port Adam.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeXRbAyw3J3SjgTPa2BKbaG2WJzeQHGHbufsCxHoo6FuG/snapshot_25.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZRUhFb4iupAVXvyU9F8PD536CA2mrrt1h7qDLTUMK87J/snapshot_26.png)

The fight was very hard but not impossible. The upgraded Batmobile with EMP blast power and drone hack system helps a lot in this fight. After all od these systems and power, Batman finally managed to destroy all the tanks.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVRPJo7n5jhe44xkdojaJzLNcPjUuQhhXyJXEuyr8qfVr/gaming_photography_2_.gif)

The situation is getting out of control. Gotham City is covered in the fear toxin gas that is making people crazy. They were killing each other. Now the city relies on only one man, Batman.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX3UAv7tiz3Vsc3AqwGiuWNTc3vrBvu9xQX6wq3MD48Zz/snapshot.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUquhB4MZJyCYQAJZM1AJDhwGyAwFA3sQYjzaGnDetsW8/snapshot_1.png)

Batman had the Nimbus cell, which he was about to put in his Batmobile. But the problem is, Batmobile was on the road  and if he wanted to put that nimbus cell, he needed to go down. Alfred highly recommended that Batman shouldn't do that. It could have made him mentally unstable and the Joker inside him can overwhelm his brain.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXwbdzVkLy2KHgAC3T6uFXeBh6XRi65CPoa3GaKV2BTEx/snapshot_2.png)

But Batman didn't listen to Alfred. He took the risk and drove into the toxic gas.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSmmcuT1wdS4BZcfpwaVbuHpjqBSJQEqceokieAEyHNwQ/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYEzVVWmBwrZEWoFsw2M6NwGwfEMwS6vGgByYecbYHNuc/snapshot_5.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSD95UqXJ1HNaq2HHEi6B2mykoH1yypiqnAXbm3hQp8bE/snapshot_6.png)

The situation in Gotham has become very bad. The entire city's sky is filled with toxic gas. In this situation, Batman finds his Batmobile in that gas. Then he tries to install the \

brought from Mr. Stuga in the car. This Nimbus Cell is actually a kind of power core, which protects the car from the effects of toxic gas. After installing it, Batman will be safe if he is inside the car.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmefpRw7MauaWyTHXVmhqGmaR4SovxSai4oZjFUKZXxX78/snapshot_7.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaejnRT5UrcsMRgkbzFJsAu1NKp6brktjjcpgBs5rQPAo/snapshot_8.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPdiYb1dJHdnSQSocNXVDdGBak1LM88ohhTbhfmK3vCcc/snapshot_9.png)

As Batman continues to work, the Joker stands next to him and starts making fun of him. He says, \

He starts laughing. Finally, after installing the Nimbus cell, Batman gets inside the car and breathes heavily. Even then, the Joker keeps coming and bothering him.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSFasujD1kz5ig7MoChL6NY9k9V51DkVpWZgCvgnebvJQ/snapshot_10.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbGjbHMdN2Egx68bbmvGscrtaApaHRPVw5fWN6ejN96ip/snapshot_11.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmahjUDokeWhAcGyrXNct7PYWxde7Ukkkr5YtYNDTH697Q/snapshot_12.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR6daY8hwtj5zgK3cT3BytnocuFHqiYpBuKyEkT4oD1Ss/snapshot_13.png)

Once the car is ready, Batman's next task is to find the roots of the ancient tree that Poison Ivy spoke of. This tree is the only one that can absorb the toxic gas. Batman searches for the roots and uses a gold blast, but the tree is too deep to work.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ7KFEfcgRLX54RoCgq2kBZcQZrkkcM3zTMWQaTenFcxa/snapshot_14.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeqYbyVL1UEpt1r7Vffw9Lnr7ds3hDVHtGaqaJCtq5sbt/snapshot_15.png)

Then Alfred says that there is an extension of the Gotham subway under Batman's house. If you go there and blast gold, it might be possible to wake up the tree. However, to get there, you have to enter through Port Adam.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbhEexK87XHtA5C6W3gzhVFM1cUPskXAnLNzaB6seuwFF/snapshot_17.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd2z7H8g9momPQ1WkqWxU2aoZn9NFWDbe9n2pUMNMhwqE/snapshot_18.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNhCTGmd16MkCruEDRACGwj3YGJato5pwYw4hrNYJxiqr/snapshot_20.png)

Batman heads towards Port Adam. The gate there was locked. When Alfred was asked to open the gate, he warned that there were many militia tanks inside. They would attack as soon as he entered. As soon as Batman entered, the tanks began attacking him.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSPBkU3KsRJciYDJVLzsga1TgfEEiJ5scTzzys5RdEgfZ/snapshot_22.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZRUhFb4iupAVXvyU9F8PD536CA2mrrt1h7qDLTUMK87J/snapshot_26.png)

The fight was very hard but not impossible. The upgraded Batmobile with EMP blast power and drone hack system helps a lot in this fight. After all od these systems and power, Batman finally managed to destroy all the tanks.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP2yUD9xJQbTrqdCbzrNvPDTMQFQ44oNKzHE73dR3FyNV/snapshot_28.png)

>

Growth in leadership does not happen by accident, as it requires a clear roadmap to identify where you are today and where you need to go.

>El crecimiento en el liderazgo no sucede por accidente, ya que requiere de una hoja de ruta clara para identificar en dónde te encuentras hoy y hacia dónde necesitas dirigirte.

By reflecting on the style you lead from most often, you can take concrete, purposeful actions to reach the next level, creating a practical path that helps you recognize your current standing while focusing on your future direction.

>Al reflexionar sobre el estilo desde el cual lideras con más frecuencia, puedes tomar acciones concretas y con propósito para alcanzar el siguiente nivel, creando así un camino práctico que te ayude a reconocer tu estado actual mientras te enfocas en tu destino.

You do not have to make huge changes in a single day or even a week, but you must act with intention today.

>No es necesario realizar cambios inmensos en un solo día ni en una semana, pero sí es fundamental actuar con intención hoy mismo.

I would love to hear which small, intentional step you are choosing to take toward your growth this week.

body.title: ERROR!
body.body: /> Every single person on earth dreams of a time when money is not a limitation to how many things they can own or how much they can spend on themselves and their loved ones. Sometimes, we even wish we had never experienced poverty, because that would mean that we could afford everything we want. Unfortunately, our reality remains different from what we wish for, and that is the reason many of us continue to work hard at our jobs and businesses just to ensure that we earn more money, get promotions, and possibly hit a milestone that will bring our dreams closer in a few years. Most of us have also sat with ourselves, thinking about the many things we would buy and tick off our bucket lists if money were not a problem. I'm not an exception. Whenever I am asked what I would do if I had access to a huge amount of money, a few things come to mind. But if you asked me today what I would buy with a significant amount of money, I would say **land.** Land is something that some people in different communities in my country were fortunate to inherit without having to pay a dime for it. On the other hand, many people have had to use their hard-earned money to purchase it. Even those without the means hope to own a piece of land someday, largely because of the value it appreciates over time.

/> Land is an asset that can be used in many ways. While it is common for people to buy land for building personal homes, rental apartments, or companies, my main aim would be to treat it as an smart investment. If money were not a problem, I would buy about 10–15 acres of land in a good location within the city, preferably close to the roadside, since such locations have higher resale value compared to those that are situated farther from the road or behind other buildings. I would then rent out the space to farmers involved in large-scale agricultural production, as well as to individuals or businesses that require open space, such as food truck operators, car mechanics, or even a church planning to use a tent for their programs. This rental arrangement would last for about four years, during which I would earn annual income from all the occupants. By the fifth year, the land would have appreciated by at least 30%, meaning that my investment would have reached a stage where the returns from those 10–15 plots would be significant enough to resell to buyers. The capital realized would be used to purchase more lands in another location, while I channel the profits into personal development and empowerment of my friends and family. This particular investment with a huge sum matters to me because it is a smart financial decision with the potential to turn me into a millionaire as long as I commit to patience. For this investment with my money, there would be no need for constant marketing, or significant maintenance costs. Lastly, the more land I own for resale, the more I become known to influential buyers, which in itself becomes another opportunity that can grant me access to wealthier networks and channels of making more money. * * * This blog post is a response to the India United weekly prompt, which you can find [**Here**](https://peakd.com/hive-197685/@indiaunited/indiaunited-new-contest-and-last-7a7caf29dc7dd) for your timely participation. * * * [**1mage 1 source**](https://unsplash.com/photos/green-plant-on-brown-round-coins-lZ_4nPFKcV8) [**Image 2 source**](https://unsplash.com/photos/green-field-with-trees-and-blue-sky-lQEyyqc9BFk)

body.body:
/>  
[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/search/unable/)

That sensation neither loudly announces itself. It sneaks in gently, typically following some things that go not your way. Then comes one error, then another, then a pause when your brain begins to create a narrative around it.

You begin to say things like, perhaps I'm not good at this. Perhaps I can't manage it. Maybe I shouldn't even attempt.

Looking about, you see people moving, developing, solving problems, which causes you to feel even more stagnant. Like you missed something everyone else knew. Like you are falling behind in a manner you cannot repair.

Not because you actually lack the ability to accomplish anything, but rather because you have persuaded yourself that trying will only corroborate your already held dread.

Most of the time, it comes from being overworked, from demanding too much all at once, or from judging oneself too fast against outcomes that take time. Under that sort of pressure, anybody would feel trapped.

Marsada Band is one of the original tano batak bands that has become familiar on the international scene consisting of 4 people, namely Marlundu Situmorang, Toni Sidabutar, Janen Sigalingging, and Norma Br. This is because, at that time, the personnel lived far apart and it was expected that they could unite. Over time, the personnel of Marsada Band increased by 4 people, namely Monang Sidabutar, Kalous sidabutar, Pardi Sidabutar and Hobbi Sinaga. Up to that time, the marching band had 8 members. However, as time progressed, Norma Br. Manurung resigned from the group because he had already married, leaving Marsada Band which consisted of 7 people. In 2021, Marlundu situmorang, the vocalist from Marsada Band died. Now, Marsada Band consists of 6 people

body.title: My Ultimate Plan With A Huge Sum of Money
body.body: /> Every single person on earth dreams of a time when money is not a limitation to how many things they can own or how much they can spend on themselves and their loved ones. Sometimes, we even wish we had never experienced poverty, because that would mean that we could afford everything we want. Unfortunately, our reality remains different from what we wish for, and that is the reason many of us continue to work hard at our jobs and businesses just to ensure that we earn more money, get promotions, and possibly hit a milestone that will bring our dreams closer in a few years. Most of us have also sat with ourselves, thinking about the many things we would buy and tick off our bucket lists if money were not a problem. I'm not an exception. Whenever I am asked what I would do if I had access to a huge amount of money, a few things come to mind. But if you asked me today what I would buy with a significant amount of money, I would say **land.** Land is something that some people in different communities in my country were fortunate to inherit without having to pay a dime for it. On the other hand, many people have had to use their hard-earned money to purchase it. Even those without the means hope to own a piece of land someday, largely because of the value it appreciates over time.

/> Land is an asset that can be used in many ways. While it is common for people to buy land for building personal homes, rental apartments, or companies, my main aim would be to treat it as an smart investment. If money were not a problem, I would buy about 10–15 acres of land in a good location within the city, preferably close to the roadside, since such locations have higher resale value compared to those that are situated farther from the road or behind other buildings. I would then rent out the space to farmers involved in large-scale agricultural production, as well as to individuals or businesses that require open space, such as food truck operators, car mechanics, or even a church planning to use a tent for their programs. This rental arrangement would last for about four years, during which I would earn annual income from all the occupants. By the fifth year, the land would have appreciated by at least 30%, meaning that my investment would have reached a stage where the returns from those 10–15 plots would be significant enough to resell to buyers. The capital realized would be used to purchase more lands in another location, while I channel the profits into personal development and empowerment of my friends and family. This particular investment with a huge sum matters to me because it is a smart financial decision with the potential to turn me into a millionaire as long as I commit to patience. For this investment with my money, there would be no need for constant marketing, or significant maintenance costs. Lastly, the more land I own for resale, the more I become known to influential buyers, which in itself becomes another opportunity that can grant me access to wealthier networks and channels of making more money. * * * This blog post is a response to the India United weekly prompt, which you can find [**Here**](https://peakd.com/hive-197685/@indiaunited/indiaunited-new-contest-and-last-7a7caf29dc7dd) for your timely participation. * * * [**1mage 1 source**](https://unsplash.com/photos/green-plant-on-brown-round-coins-lZ_4nPFKcV8) [**Image 2 source**](https://unsplash.com/photos/green-field-with-trees-and-blue-sky-lQEyyqc9BFk)

body.title: 8 April 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3067: life insurance
body.body:
/>  
[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/search/life%20insurance/)

Most people hear those terms and start thinking about paperwork, signatures, monthly bills, maybe difficult chats they would prefer postponed. It seems far off, like something for some other moment. One thing to ponder when life becomes more grounded.

However under all the official terminology, the concept is quite human.

It centers on care.

Looking beyond today and pondering what will become of the people I love should I not be here.

One strategy to lessen terror when emotions are too much already.

Still, pondering over it could seem weird. Nearly as though readying for loss welcomes terror into the space. Since the future appears too shaky, they concentrate on the present.

Still, preparation is essential precisely because of doubt.

Love frequently looks like planning ahead; not from daily expectation of the worst. like managing what is possible while still in life.

In this sense, life insurance is more about duty than about worry. A gentle form of defense.

One last means of saying, even if I couldn't be there, I still sought to assist.

body.title: More work, but I'm happy
body.body:
Hi, guys!

I have a lot of photoshoots planned today, but first I have to go to the post office to pick up and mail packages, and also wrap gifts for my husband's birthday, which is almost a month away, but I like to have everything ready in advance. I already have three gifts ready, and I want everything to be perfect this year, so I'm planning on wrapping them in beautiful paper so he can unwrap them and fully experience the joy.

I also need to send books to a friend, so that's another little surprise.

Yesterday I joined a group of illustrators I don't know; we're planning to meet for coffee and drawing. I don't know any of them, and this will be my first time doing something like this, but I hope everything goes well. I'm really looking forward to it. I've got a lot going on this month, and I don't know if it's too much for just me. But I think I'll manage somehow.

I'm pretty far behind on filming right now, so I need to catch up. I haven't filmed any pranks in a while, and that needs to be done, too, but I can't find the time. And I can't find the right mood either. But I need to find it and do it.

So, I actually have a lot of plans. I need to get myself together, pull myself together, and process them all one by one, because the longer I put them off, the more they pile up, and there's nowhere left to put them, and there's already too many.

So now I'm finishing my coffee, quickly running to the post office, then getting myself together and filming videos until I can't stand it. And tomorrow I need to get back to walking the dogs, because I've had almost a week without any exercise.

Have a great day, everyone!

Українська співачка Leléka, що перемогла Нацвідбір на черговий пісенний конкурс Євробпачення-2026 і представлятиме нашу країну на цій сцені, презентувала конкурсну версію пісні Ridnym. Вона буде виконана у супроводі струнного квінтету і бандури. Створювати таку версію виступу допомагав  режисер-постановник Михайло Харченко.
